And*p on the sixth day eight bullocks, two rams, and fourteen lambs of the first year without blemish:
And*p their meat offering and their drink offerings for the bullocks, for the rams, and for the lambs, shall be according to their number, after the manner:
And*p one goat for a sin offering; beside the continual burnt offering, his meat offering, and his drink offering.
And*p on the seventh day seven bullocks, two rams, and fourteen lambs of the first year without blemish:
And*p their meat offering and their drink offerings for the bullocks, for the rams, and for the lambs, shall be according to their number, after the manner:
And*p one goat for a sin offering; beside the continual burnt offering, his meat offering, and his drink offering.
On*p the eighth day ye shall have a solemn assembly: ye shall do no servile work therein:
But*p ye shall offer a burnt offering, a sacrifice made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord:*s one bullock, one ram, seven lambs of the first year without blemish:
Their*p meat offering and their drink offerings for the bullock, for the ram, and for the lambs, shall be according to their number, after the manner:
And*p one goat for a sin offering; beside the continual burnt offering, and his meat offering, and his drink offering.

These*p things ye shall do unto the Lord*s in your set feasts, beside your vows, and your freewill offerings, for your burnt offerings, and for your meat offerings, and for your drink offerings, and for your peace offerings.
And*p Moses told the children of Israel according to all that the Lord*s commanded Moses.
Numbers 30
And*p Moses spake unto the heads of the tribes concerning the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing which the Lord*s hath commanded.
If*p a man vow a vow unto the Lord,*s or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.
If*p a woman also vow a vow unto the Lord,*s and bind herself by a bond, being in her father's house in her youth;

And*p her father hear her vow, and her bond wherewith she hath bound her soul, and her father shall hold his peace at her: then all her vows shall stand, and every bond wherewith she hath bound her soul shall stand.

But*p if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth; not any of her vows, or of her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand: and the Lord*s shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her.
And*p if she had at all an husband, when she vowed, or uttered ought out of her lips, wherewith she bound her soul;
And*p her husband heard it, and held his peace at her in the day that he heard it: then her vows shall stand, and her bonds wherewith she bound her soul shall stand.

But*p if her husband disallowed her on the day that he heard it; then he shall make her vow which she vowed, and that which she uttered with her lips, wherewith she bound her soul, of none effect: and the Lord*s shall forgive her.
But*p every vow of a widow, and of her that is divorced, wherewith they have bound their souls, shall stand against her.
And*p if she vowed in her husband's house, or bound her soul by a bond with an oath;
And*p her husband heard it, and held his peace at her, and disallowed her not: then all her vows shall stand, and every bond wherewith she bound her soul shall stand.

But*p if her husband hath utterly made them void on the day he heard them; then whatsoever proceeded out of her lips concerning her vows, or concerning the bond of her soul, shall not stand: her husband hath made them void; and the Lord*s shall forgive her.
Every*p vow, and every binding oath to afflict the soul, her husband may establish it, or her husband may make it void.

But*p if her husband altogether hold his peace at her from day to day; then he establisheth all her vows, or all her bonds, which are upon her: he confirmeth them, because he held his peace at her in the day that he heard them.
But*p if he shall any ways make them void after that he hath heard them; then he shall bear her iniquity.
These*p are the statutes, which the Lord*s commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between the father and his daughter, being yet in her youth in her father's house.
Numbers 31
And*p the Lord*s spake unto Moses, saying,
Avenge*p the children of Israel of the Midianites: afterward shalt thou be gathered unto thy people.
And*p Moses spake unto the people, saying, Arm some of yourselves unto the war, and let them go against the Midianites, and avenge the Lord*s of Midian.

And*p they warred against the Midianites, as the Lord*s commanded Moses; and they slew all the males.

And*p they took all the spoil, and all the prey, both of men and of beasts.

And*p they brought the captives, and the prey, and the spoil, unto Moses, and Eleazar the priest, and unto the congregation of the children of Israel, unto the camp at the plains of Moab, which are by Jordan near Jericho.

And*p Moses said unto them, Have ye saved all the women alive?
Behold,*p these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord*s in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.*s
Now*p therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman that hath known man by lying with him.
But*p all the women children, that have not known a man by lying with him, keep alive for yourselves.

And*p do ye abide without the camp seven days: whosoever hath killed any person, and whosoever hath touched any slain, purify both yourselves and your captives on the third day, and on the seventh day.
And*p purify all your raiment, and all that is made of skins, and all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood.
And*p Eleazar the priest said unto the men of war which went to the battle, This is the ordinance of the law which the Lord*s commanded Moses;
Only*p the gold, and the silver, the brass, the iron, the tin, and the lead,

Every*p thing that may abide the fire, ye shall make it go through the fire, and it shall be clean: nevertheless it shall be purified with the water of separation: and all that abideth not the fire ye shall make go through the water.
And*p ye shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and ye shall be clean, and afterward ye shall come into the camp.
And*p the Lord*s spake unto Moses, saying,
Take*p the sum of the prey that was taken, both of man and of beast, thou, and Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation:
And*p divide the prey into two parts; between them that took the war upon them, who went out to battle, and between all the congregation:
And*p levy a tribute unto the Lord*s of the men of war which went out to battle: one soul of five hundred, both of the persons, and of the beeves, and of the asses, and of the sheep:
Take*p it of their half, and give it unto Eleazar the priest, for an heave offering of the Lord.*s

And*p of the children of Israel's half, thou shalt take one portion of fifty, of the persons, of the beeves, of the asses, and of the flocks, of all manner of beasts, and give them unto the Levites, which keep the charge of the tabernacle of the Lord.*s
And*p Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord*s commanded Moses.
And*p the booty, being the rest of the prey which the men of war had caught, was six hundred thousand and seventy thousand and five thousand sheep,
And*p threescore and twelve thousand beeves,
And*p threescore and one thousand asses,
And*p thirty and two thousand persons in all, of women that had not known man by lying with him.
And*p the half, which was the portion of them that went out to war, was in number three hundred thousand and seven and thirty thousand and five hundred sheep:
And*p the Lord's*s tribute of the sheep was six hundred and threescore and fifteen.
And*p the beeves were thirty and six thousand; of which the Lord's*s tribute was threescore and twelve.
And*p the asses were thirty thousand and five hundred; of which the Lord's*s tribute was threescore and one.
And*p the persons were sixteen thousand; of which the Lord's*s tribute was thirty and two persons.
And*p Moses gave the tribute, which was the Lord's*s heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord*s commanded Moses.
And*p of the children of Israel's half, which Moses divided from the men that warred,
(Now*p the half that pertained unto the congregation was three hundred thousand and thirty thousand and seven thousand and five hundred sheep,
And*p thirty and six thousand beeves,
And*p thirty thousand asses and five hundred,
And*p sixteen thousand persons;)

Even*p of the children of Israel's half, Moses took one portion of fifty, both of man and of beast, and gave them unto the Levites, which kept the charge of the tabernacle of the Lord;*s as the Lord*s commanded Moses.
And*p the officers which were over thousands of the host, the captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, came near unto Moses:
And*p they said unto Moses, Thy servants have taken the sum of the men of war which are under our charge, and there lacketh not one man of us.

We*p have therefore brought an oblation for the Lord,*s what every man hath gotten, of jewels of gold, chains, and bracelets, rings, earrings, and tablets, to make an atonement for our souls before the Lord.*s
And*p Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold of them, even all wrought jewels.
And*p all the gold of the offering that they offered up to the Lord,*s of the captains of thousands, and of the captains of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels.
(For*p the men of war had taken spoil, every man for himself.)

And*p Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold of the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the tabernacle of the congregation, for a memorial for the children of Israel before the Lord.*s
Numbers 32
Now*p the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle: and when they saw the land of Jazer, and the land of Gilead, that, behold, the place was a place for cattle;
The*p children of Gad and the children of Reuben came and spake unto Moses, and to Eleazar the priest, and unto the princes of the congregation, saying,
Ataroth,*p and Dibon, and Jazer, and Nimrah, and Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Shebam, and Nebo, and Beon,
Even*p the country which the Lord*s smote before the congregation of Israel, is a land for cattle, and thy servants have cattle:
Wherefore,*p said they, if we have found grace in thy sight, let this land be given unto thy servants for a possession, and bring us not over Jordan.
And*p Moses said unto the children of Gad and to the children of Reuben, Shall your brethren go to war, and shall ye sit here?
And*p wherefore discourage ye the heart of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the Lord*s hath given them?
Thus*p did your fathers, when I sent them from Kadesh–barnea to see the land.
For*p when they went up unto the valley of Eshcol, and saw the land, they discouraged the heart of the children of Israel, that they should not go into the land which the Lord*s had given them.
And*p the Lord's*s anger was kindled the same time, and he sware, saying,

Surely*p none of the men that came up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob; because they have not wholly followed me:
Save*p Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite, and Joshua the son of Nun: for they have wholly followed the Lord.*s
And*p the Lord's*s anger was kindled against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation, that had done evil in the sight of the Lord,*s was consumed.
And,*p behold, ye are risen up in your fathers' stead, an increase of sinful men, to augment yet the fierce anger of the Lord*s toward Israel.
For*p if ye turn away from after him, he will yet again leave them in the wilderness; and ye shall destroy all this people.
And*p they came near unto him, and said, We will build sheepfolds here for our cattle, and cities for our little ones:

But*p we ourselves will go ready armed before the children of Israel, until we have brought them unto their place: and our little ones shall dwell in the fenced cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
We*p will not return unto our houses, until the children of Israel have inherited every man his inheritance.
For*p we will not inherit with them on yonder side Jordan, or forward; because our inheritance is fallen to us on this side Jordan eastward.
And*p Moses said unto them, If ye will do this thing, if ye will go armed before the Lord*s to war,
And*p will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord,*s until he hath driven out his enemies from before him,
And*p the land be subdued before the Lord:*s then afterward ye shall return, and be guiltless before the Lord,*s and before Israel; and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.*s
But*p if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord:*s and be sure your sin will find you out.
Build*p you cities for your little ones, and folds for your sheep; and do that which hath proceeded out of your mouth.
And*p the children of Gad and the children of Reuben spake unto Moses, saying, Thy servants will do as my lord commandeth.
Our*p little ones, our wives, our flocks, and all our cattle, shall be there in the cities of Gilead:
But*p thy servants will pass over, every man armed for war, before the Lord*s to battle, as my lord saith.
So*p concerning them Moses commanded Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the chief fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel:

And*p Moses said unto them, If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed to battle, before the Lord,*s and the land shall be subdued before you; then ye shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession:
But*p if they will not pass over with you armed, they shall have possessions among you in the land of Canaan.
And*p the children of Gad and the children of Reuben answered, saying, As the Lord*s hath said unto thy servants, so will we do.
We*p will pass over armed before the Lord*s into the land of Canaan, that the possession of our inheritance on this side Jordan may be ours.

And*p Moses gave unto them, even to the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuben, and unto half the tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land, with the cities thereof in the coasts, even the cities of the country round about.
And*p the children of Gad built Dibon, and Ataroth, and Aroer,
And*p Atroth Shophan, and Jaazer, and Jogbehah,
And*p Beth–nimrah, and Beth–haran, fenced cities: and folds for sheep.
And*p the children of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,
And*p Nebo, and Baal–meon, (their names being changed,) and Sibmah: and gave other names unto the cities which they builded.
And*p the children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead, and took it, and dispossessed the Amorite which was in it.
And*p Moses gave Gilead unto Machir the son of Manasseh; and he dwelt therein.
And*p Jair the son of Manasseh went and took the small towns thereof, and called them Havoth–jair.
And*p Nobah went and took Kenath, and the villages thereof, and called it Nobah, after his own name.
Numbers 33
These*p are the journeys of the children of Israel, which went forth out of the land of Egypt with their armies under the hand of Moses and Aaron.
And*p Moses wrote their goings out according to their journeys by the commandment of the Lord:*s and these are their journeys according to their goings out.

And*p they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Israel went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.
For*p the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which the Lord*s had smitten among them: upon their gods also the Lord*s executed judgments.
And*p the children of Israel removed from Rameses, and pitched in Succoth.
And*p they departed from Succoth, and pitched in Etham, which is in the edge of the wilderness.
And*p they removed from Etham, and turned again unto Pi–hahiroth, which is before Baal–zephon: and they pitched before Migdol.
And*p they departed from before Pi–hahiroth, and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, and went three days' journey in the wilderness of Etham, and pitched in Marah.
And*p they removed from Marah, and came unto Elim: and in Elim were twelve fountains of water, and threescore and ten palm trees; and they pitched there.
And*p they removed from Elim, and encamped by the Red sea.
And*p they removed from the Red sea, and encamped in the wilderness of Sin.
And*p they took their journey out of the wilderness of Sin, and encamped in Dophkah.
And*p they departed from Dophkah, and encamped in Alush.
And*p they removed from Alush, and encamped at Rephidim, where was no water for the people to drink.
And*p they departed from Rephidim, and pitched in the wilderness of Sinai.
And*p they removed from the desert of Sinai, and pitched at Kibroth–hattaavah.
And*p they departed from Kibroth–hattaavah, and encamped at Hazeroth.
And*p they departed from Hazeroth, and pitched in Rithmah.
And*p they departed from Rithmah, and pitched at Rimmon–perez.
And*p they departed from Rimmon–perez, and pitched in Libnah.
And*p they removed from Libnah, and pitched at Rissah.
And*p they journeyed from Rissah, and pitched in Kehelathah.
And*p they went from Kehelathah, and pitched in mount Shapher.
And*p they removed from mount Shapher, and encamped in Haradah.
And*p they removed from Haradah, and pitched in Makheloth.
And*p they removed from Makheloth, and encamped at Tahath.
And*p they departed from Tahath, and pitched at Tarah.
And*p they removed from Tarah, and pitched in Mithcah.
And*p they went from Mithcah, and pitched in Hashmonah.
And*p they departed from Hashmonah, and encamped at Moseroth.
And*p they departed from Moseroth, and pitched in Bene–jaakan.
And*p they removed from Bene–jaakan, and encamped at Hor–haggiggad.
And*p they went from Hor–haggiggad, and pitched in Jotbathah.
And*p they removed from Jotbathah, and encamped at Ebronah.
And*p they departed from Ebronah, and encamped at Ezion–geber.
And*p they removed from Ezion–geber, and pitched in the wilderness of Zin, which is Kadesh.
And*p they removed from Kadesh, and pitched in mount Hor, in the edge of the land of Edom.

And*p Aaron the priest went up into mount Hor at the commandment of the Lord,*s and died there, in the fortieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the first day of the fifth month.
And*p Aaron was an hundred and twenty and three years old when he died in mount Hor.
And*p king Arad the Canaanite, which dwelt in the south in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the children of Israel.
And*p they departed from mount Hor, and pitched in Zalmonah.
And*p they departed from Zalmonah, and pitched in Punon.
And*p they departed from Punon, and pitched in Oboth.
And*p they departed from Oboth, and pitched in Iye–abarim, in the border of Moab.
And*p they departed from Iim, and pitched in Dibon–gad.
And*p they removed from Dibon–gad, and encamped in Almon–diblathaim.
And*p they removed from Almon–diblathaim, and pitched in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
And*p they departed from the mountains of Abarim, and pitched in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho.
And*p they pitched by Jordan, from Beth–jeshimoth even unto Abel–shittim in the plains of Moab.
And*p the Lord*s spake unto Moses in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, saying,
Speak*p unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye are passed over Jordan into the land of Canaan;
Then*p ye shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their pictures, and destroy all their molten images, and quite pluck down all their high places:
And*p ye shall dispossess the inhabitants of the land, and dwell therein: for I have given you the land to possess it.

And*p ye shall divide the land by lot for an inheritance among your families: and to the more ye shall give the more inheritance, and to the fewer ye shall give the less inheritance: every man's inheritance shall be in the place where his lot falleth; according to the tribes of your fathers ye shall inherit.

But*p if ye will not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you; then it shall come to pass, that those which ye let remain of them shall be pricks in your eyes, and thorns in your sides, and shall vex you in the land wherein ye dwell.
Moreover*p it shall come to pass, that I shall do unto you, as I thought to do unto them.
Numbers 34
And*p the Lord*s spake unto Moses, saying,

Command*p the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land of Canaan; (this is the land that shall fall unto you for an inheritance, even the land of Canaan with the coasts thereof:)
Then*p your south quarter shall be from the wilderness of Zin along by the coast of Edom, and your south border shall be the outmost coast of the salt sea eastward:

And*p your border shall turn from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim, and pass on to Zin: and the going forth thereof shall be from the south to Kadesh–barnea, and shall go on to Hazar–addar, and pass on to Azmon:
And*p the border shall fetch a compass from Azmon unto the river of Egypt, and the goings out of it shall be at the sea.
And*p as for the western border, ye shall even have the great sea for a border: this shall be your west border.
And*p this shall be your north border: from the great sea ye shall point out for you mount Hor:
From*p mount Hor ye shall point out your border unto the entrance of Hamath; and the goings forth of the border shall be to Zedad:
And*p the border shall go on to Ziphron, and the goings out of it shall be at Hazar–enan: this shall be your north border.
And*p ye shall point out your east border from Hazar–enan to Shepham:
And*p the coast shall go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain; and the border shall descend, and shall reach unto the side of the sea of Chinnereth eastward:
And*p the border shall go down to Jordan, and the goings out of it shall be at the salt sea: this shall be your land with the coasts thereof round about.
And*p Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying, This is the land which ye shall inherit by lot, which the Lord*s commanded to give unto the nine tribes, and to the half tribe:

For*p the tribe of the children of Reuben according to the house of their fathers, and the tribe of the children of Gad according to the house of their fathers, have received their inheritance; and half the tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance:
The*p two tribes and the half tribe have received their inheritance on this side Jordan near Jericho eastward, toward the sunrising.
And*p the Lord*s spake unto Moses, saying,
These*p are the names of the men which shall divide the land unto you: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun.
And*p ye shall take one prince of every tribe, to divide the land by inheritance.
And*p the names of the men are these: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
And*p of the tribe of the children of Simeon, Shemuel the son of Ammihud.
Of*p the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon.
And*p the prince of the tribe of the children of Dan, Bukki the son of Jogli.
The*p prince of the children of Joseph, for the tribe of the children of Manasseh, Hanniel the son of Ephod.
And*p the prince of the tribe of the children of Ephraim, Kemuel the son of Shiphtan.
And*p the prince of the tribe of the children of Zebulun, Elizaphan the son of Parnach.
And*p the prince of the tribe of the children of Issachar, Paltiel the son of Azzan.
And*p the prince of the tribe of the children of Asher, Ahihud the son of Shelomi.
And*p the prince of the tribe of the children of Naphtali, Pedahel the son of Ammihud.
These*p are they whom the Lord*s commanded to divide the inheritance unto the children of Israel in the land of Canaan.
Numbers 35
And*p the Lord*s spake unto Moses in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, saying,

Command*p the children of Israel, that they give unto the Levites of the inheritance of their possession cities to dwell in; and ye shall give also unto the Levites suburbs for the cities round about them.
And*p the cities shall they have to dwell in; and the suburbs of them shall be for their cattle, and for their goods, and for all their beasts.
And*p the suburbs of the cities, which ye shall give unto the Levites, shall reach from the wall of the city and outward a thousand cubits round about.

And*p ye shall measure from without the city on the east side two thousand cubits, and on the south side two thousand cubits, and on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits; and the city shall be in the midst: this shall be to them the suburbs of the cities.

And*p among the cities which ye shall give unto the Levites there shall be six cities for refuge, which ye shall appoint for the manslayer, that he may flee thither: and to them ye shall add forty and two cities.
So*p all the cities which ye shall give to the Levites shall be forty and eight cities: them shall ye give with their suburbs.

And*p the cities which ye shall give shall be of the possession of the children of Israel: from them that have many ye shall give many; but from them that have few ye shall give few: every one shall give of his cities unto the Levites according to his inheritance which he inheriteth.
And*p the Lord*s spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak*p unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come over Jordan into the land of Canaan;
Then*p ye shall appoint you cities to be cities of refuge for you; that the slayer may flee thither, which killeth any person at unawares.
And*p they shall be unto you cities for refuge from the avenger; that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.
And*p of these cities which ye shall give six cities shall ye have for refuge.
Ye*p shall give three cities on this side Jordan, and three cities shall ye give in the land of Canaan, which shall be cities of refuge.
These*p six cities shall be a refuge, both for the children of Israel, and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them: that every one that killeth any person unawares may flee thither.
And*p if he smite him with an instrument of iron, so that he die, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
And*p if he smite him with throwing a stone, wherewith he may die, and he die, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
Or*p if he smite him with an hand weapon of wood, wherewith he may die, and he die, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
The*p revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer: when he meeteth him, he shall slay him.
But*p if he thrust him of hatred, or hurl at him by laying of wait, that he die;
Or*p in enmity smite him with his hand, that he die: he that smote him shall surely be put to death; for he is a murderer: the revenger of blood shall slay the murderer, when he meeteth him.
But*p if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or have cast upon him any thing without laying of wait,
Or*p with any stone, wherewith a man may die, seeing him not, and cast it upon him, that he die, and was not his enemy, neither sought his harm:
Then*p the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments:

And*p the congregation shall deliver the slayer out of the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, whither he was fled: and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.
But*p if the slayer shall at any time come without the border of the city of his refuge, whither he was fled;
And*p the revenger of blood find him without the borders of the city of his refuge, and the revenger of blood kill the slayer; he shall not be guilty of blood:
Because*p he should have remained in the city of his refuge until the death of the high priest: but after the death of the high priest the slayer shall return into the land of his possession.
So*p these things shall be for a statute of judgment unto you throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
Whoso*p killeth any person, the murderer shall be put to death by the mouth of witnesses: but one witness shall not testify against any person to cause him to die.
Moreover*p ye shall take no satisfaction for the life of a murderer, which is guilty of death: but he shall be surely put to death.
And*p ye shall take no satisfaction for him that is fled to the city of his refuge, that he should come again to dwell in the land, until the death of the priest.
So*p ye shall not pollute the land wherein ye are: for blood it defileth the land: and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it.
Defile*p not therefore the land which ye shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I the Lord*s dwell among the children of Israel.
Numbers 36

And*p the chief fathers of the families of the children of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of the sons of Joseph, came near, and spake before Moses, and before the princes, the chief fathers of the children of Israel:

And*p they said, The Lord*s commanded my lord to give the land for an inheritance by lot to the children of Israel: and my lord was commanded by the Lord*s to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother unto his daughters.

And*p if they be married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Israel, then shall their inheritance be taken from the inheritance of our fathers, and shall be put to the inheritance of the tribe whereunto they are received: so shall it be taken from the lot of our inheritance.

And*p when the jubilee of the children of Israel shall be, then shall their inheritance be put unto the inheritance of the tribe whereunto they are received: so shall their inheritance be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.
And*p Moses commanded the children of Israel according to the word of the Lord,*s saying, The tribe of the sons of Joseph hath said well.

This*p is the thing which the Lord*s doth command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.
So*p shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Israel shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.

And*p every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Israel, shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.
Neither*p shall the inheritance remove from one tribe to another tribe; but every one of the tribes of the children of Israel shall keep himself to his own inheritance.
Even*p as the Lord*s commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad:
For*p Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married unto their father's brothers' sons:
And*p they were married into the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.
These*p are the commandments and the judgments, which the Lord*s commanded by the hand of Moses unto the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho.
Deuteronomy 1
These*p be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness, in the plain over against the Red sea, between Paran, and Tophel, and Laban, and Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
(There*p are eleven days' journey from Horeb by the way of mount Seir unto Kadesh–barnea.)

And*p it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spake unto the children of Israel, according unto all that the Lord*s had given him in commandment unto them;
After*p he had slain Sihon the king of the Amorites, which dwelt in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, which dwelt at Ashtaroth in Edrei:
On*p this side Jordan, in the land of Moab, began Moses to declare this law, saying,
The*p Lord*s our God spake unto us in Horeb, saying, Ye have dwelt long enough in this mount:

Turn*p you, and take your journey, and go to the mount of the Amorites, and unto all the places nigh thereunto, in the plain, in the hills, and in the vale, and in the south, and by the sea side, to the land of the Canaanites, and unto Lebanon, unto the great river, the river Euphrates.
Behold,*p I have set the land before you: go in and possess the land which the Lord*s sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them and to their seed after them.
And*p I spake unto you at that time, saying, I am not able to bear you myself alone:
The*p Lord*s your God hath multiplied you, and, behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude.
(The*p Lord*s God of your fathers make you a thousand times so many more as ye are, and bless you, as he hath promised you!)
How*p can I myself alone bear your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife?
Take*p you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.
And*p ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do.

So*p I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.
And*p I charged your judges at that time, saying, Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.

Ye*p shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God's: and the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.
And*p I commanded you at that time all the things which ye should do.

And*p when we departed from Horeb, we went through all that great and terrible wilderness, which ye saw by the way of the mountain of the Amorites, as the Lord*s our God commanded us; and we came to Kadesh–barnea.
And*p I said unto you, Ye are come unto the mountain of the Amorites, which the Lord*s our God doth give unto us.
Behold,*p the Lord*s thy God hath set the land before thee: go up and possess it, as the Lord*s God of thy fathers hath said unto thee; fear not, neither be discouraged.

And*p ye came near unto me every one of you, and said, We will send men before us, and they shall search us out the land, and bring us word again by what way we must go up, and into what cities we shall come.
And*p the saying pleased me well: and I took twelve men of you, one of a tribe:
And*p they turned and went up into the mountain, and came unto the valley of Eshcol, and searched it out.
And*p they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down unto us, and brought us word again, and said, It is a good land which the Lord*s our God doth give us.
Notwithstanding*p ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord*s your God:
And*p ye murmured in your tents, and said, Because the Lord*s hated us, he hath brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.

Whither*p shall we go up? our brethren have discouraged our heart, saying, The people is greater and taller than we; the cities are great and walled up to heaven; and moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakims there.
Then*p I said unto you, Dread not, neither be afraid of them.
The*p Lord*s your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes;
And*p in the wilderness, where thou hast seen how that the Lord*s thy God bare thee, as a man doth bear his son, in all the way that ye went, until ye came into this place.
Yet*p in this thing ye did not believe the Lord*s your God,
Who*p went in the way before you, to search you out a place to pitch your tents in, in fire by night, to shew you by what way ye should go, and in a cloud by day.
And*p the Lord*s heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and sware, saying,
Surely*p there shall not one of these men of this evil generation see that good land, which I sware to give unto your fathers,
Save*p Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it, and to him will I give the land that he hath trodden upon, and to his children, because he hath wholly followed the Lord.*s
Also*p the Lord*s was angry with me for your sakes, saying, Thou also shalt not go in thither.
But*p Joshua the son of Nun, which standeth before thee, he shall go in thither: encourage him: for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.

Moreover*p your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, and your children, which in that day had no knowledge between good and evil, they shall go in thither, and unto them will I give it, and they shall possess it.
But*p as for you, turn you, and take your journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea.

Then*p ye answered and said unto me, We have sinned against the Lord,*s we will go up and fight, according to all that the Lord*s our God commanded us. And when ye had girded on every man his weapons of war, ye were ready to go up into the hill.
And*p the Lord*s said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies.
So*p I spake unto you; and ye would not hear, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord,*s and went presumptuously up into the hill.
And*p the Amorites, which dwelt in that mountain, came out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and destroyed you in Seir, even unto Hormah.
And*p ye returned and wept before the Lord;*s but the Lord*s would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you.
So*p ye abode in Kadesh many days, according unto the days that ye abode there.
Deuteronomy 2
Then*p we turned, and took our journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea, as the Lord*s spake unto me: and we compassed mount Seir many days.
And*p the Lord*s spake unto me, saying,
Ye*p have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.

And*p command thou the people, saying, Ye are to pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir; and they shall be afraid of you: take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore:
Meddle*p not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as a foot breadth; because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession.
Ye*p shall buy meat of them for money, that ye may eat; and ye shall also buy water of them for money, that ye may drink.

For*p the Lord*s thy God hath blessed thee in all the works of thy hand: he knoweth thy walking through this great wilderness: these forty years the Lord*s thy God hath been with thee; thou hast lacked nothing.

And*p when we passed by from our brethren the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, through the way of the plain from Elath, and from Ezion–geber, we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

And*p the Lord*s said unto me, Distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle: for I will not give thee of their land for a possession; because I have given Ar unto the children of Lot for a possession.
The*p Emims dwelt therein in times past, a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims;
Which*p also were accounted giants, as the Anakims; but the Moabites call them Emims.

The*p Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime; but the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead; as Israel did unto the land of his possession, which the Lord*s gave unto them.
Now*p rise up, said I, and get you over the brook Zered. And we went over the brook Zered.

And*p the space in which we came from Kadesh–barnea, until we were come over the brook Zered, was thirty and eight years; until all the generation of the men of war were wasted out from among the host, as the Lord*s sware unto them.
For*p indeed the hand of the Lord*s was against them, to destroy them from among the host, until they were consumed.
So*p it came to pass, when all the men of war were consumed and dead from among the people,
That*p the Lord*s spake unto me, saying,
Thou*p art to pass over through Ar, the coast of Moab, this day:

And*p when thou comest nigh over against the children of Ammon, distress them not, nor meddle with them: for I will not give thee of the land of the children of Ammon any possession; because I have given it unto the children of Lot for a possession.
(That*p also was accounted a land of giants: giants dwelt therein in old time; and the Ammonites call them Zamzummims;
A*p people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; but the Lord*s destroyed them before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead:
As*p he did to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day:
And*p the Avims which dwelt in Hazerim, even unto Gaza, the Caphtorims, which came forth out of Caphtor, destroyed them, and dwelt in their stead.)

Rise*p ye up, take your journey, and pass over the river Arnon: behold, I have given into thine hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land: begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle.

This*p day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.
And*p I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,
Let*p me pass through thy land: I will go along by the high way, I will neither turn unto the right hand nor to the left.
Thou*p shalt sell me meat for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink: only I will pass through on my feet;
(As*p the children of Esau which dwell in Seir, and the Moabites which dwell in Ar, did unto me;) until I shall pass over Jordan into the land which the Lord*s our God giveth us.
But*p Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him: for the Lord*s thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as appeareth this day.
And*p the Lord*s said unto me, Behold, I have begun to give Sihon and his land before thee: begin to possess, that thou mayest inherit his land.
Then*p Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to fight at Jahaz.
And*p the Lord*s our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.
And*p we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city, we left none to remain:
Only*p the cattle we took for a prey unto ourselves, and the spoil of the cities which we took.

From*p Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the Lord*s our God delivered all unto us:
Only*p unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not, nor unto any place of the river Jabbok, nor unto the cities in the mountains, nor unto whatsoever the Lord*s our God forbad us.
Deuteronomy 3
Then*p we turned, and went up the way to Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

And*p the Lord*s said unto me, Fear him not: for I will deliver him, and all his people, and his land, into thy hand; and thou shalt do unto him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
So*p the Lord*s our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.
And*p we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All*p these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many.
And*p we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city.
But*p all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, we took for a prey to ourselves.
And*p we took at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites the land that was on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon;
(Which*p Hermon the Sidonians call Sirion; and the Amorites call it Senir;)
All*p the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, unto Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For*p only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.
And*p this land, which we possessed at that time, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, and half mount Gilead, and the cities thereof, gave I unto the Reubenites and to the Gadites.
And*p the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, being the kingdom of Og, gave I unto the half tribe of Manasseh; all the region of Argob, with all Bashan, which was called the land of giants.
Jair*p the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob unto the coasts of Geshuri and Maachathi; and called them after his own name, Bashan–havoth–jair, unto this day.
And*p I gave Gilead unto Machir.
And*p unto the Reubenites and unto the Gadites I gave from Gilead even unto the river Arnon half the valley, and the border even unto the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;
The*p plain also, and Jordan, and the coast thereof, from Chinnereth even unto the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, under Ashdoth–pisgah eastward.

And*p I commanded you at that time, saying, The Lord*s your God hath given you this land to possess it: ye shall pass over armed before your brethren the children of Israel, all that are meet for the war.
But*p your wives, and your little ones, and your cattle, (for I know that ye have much cattle,) shall abide in your cities which I have given you;

Until*p the Lord*s have given rest unto your brethren, as well as unto you, and until they also possess the land which the Lord*s your God hath given them beyond Jordan: and then shall ye return every man unto his possession, which I have given you.
And*p I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Thine eyes have seen all that the Lord*s your God hath done unto these two kings: so shall the Lord*s do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest.
Ye*p shall not fear them: for the Lord*s your God he shall fight for you.
And*p I besought the Lord*s at that time, saying,
O*p Lord God,*s thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness, and thy mighty hand: for what God is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy might?
I*p pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.
But*p the Lord*s was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me: and the Lord*s said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter.

So*p we abode in the valley over against Beth–peor.
Deuteronomy 4

Now*p therefore hearken, O Israel, unto the statutes and unto the judgments, which I teach you, for to do them, that ye may live, and go in and possess the land which the Lord*s God of your fathers giveth you.

For*p what nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them, as the Lord*s our God is in all things that we call upon him for?
And*p what nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?

Only*p take heed to thyself, and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things which thine eyes have seen, and lest they depart from thy heart all the days of thy life: but teach them thy sons, and thy sons' sons;

And*p ye came near and stood under the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire unto the midst of heaven, with darkness, clouds, and thick darkness.
And*p the Lord*s spake unto you out of the midst of the fire: ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude; only ye heard a voice.

Lest*p ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female,
The*p likeness of any beast that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged fowl that flieth in the air,
The*p likeness of any thing that creepeth on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the waters beneath the earth:

And*p lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which the Lord*s thy God hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.
But*p the Lord*s hath taken you, and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance, as ye are this day.

Furthermore*p the Lord*s was angry with me for your sakes, and sware that I should not go over Jordan, and that I should not go in unto that good land, which the Lord*s thy God giveth thee for an inheritance:
But*p I must die in this land, I must not go over Jordan: but ye shall go over, and possess that good land.

Take*p heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of the Lord*s your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, which the Lord*s thy God hath forbidden thee.
For*p the Lord*s thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God.

When*p thou shalt beget children, and children's children, and ye shall have remained long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, and shall do evil in the sight of the Lord*s thy God, to provoke him to anger:

I*p call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.

And*p there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
But*p if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord*s thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul.

For*p ask now of the days that are past, which were before thee, since the day that God created man upon the earth, and ask from the one side of heaven unto the other, whether there hath been any such thing as this great thing is, or hath been heard like it?

Or*p hath God assayed to go and take him a nation from the midst of another nation, by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by a stretched out arm, and by great terrors, according to all that the Lord*s your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?

Thou*p shalt keep therefore his statutes, and his commandments, which I command thee this day, that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days upon the earth, which the Lord*s thy God giveth thee, for ever.
Then*p Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising;
That*p the slayer might flee thither, which should kill his neighbour unawares, and hated him not in times past; and that fleeing unto one of these cities he might live:
Namely,*p Bezer in the wilderness, in the plain country, of the Reubenites; and Ramoth in Gilead, of the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, of the Manassites.
And*p this is the law which Moses set before the children of Israel:
These*p are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments, which Moses spake unto the children of Israel, after they came forth out of Egypt,

On*p this side Jordan, in the valley over against Beth–peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon, whom Moses and the children of Israel smote, after they were come forth out of Egypt:
And*p they possessed his land, and the land of Og king of Bashan, two kings of the Amorites, which were on this side Jordan toward the sunrising;
From*p Aroer, which is by the bank of the river Arnon, even unto mount Sion, which is Hermon,
And*p all the plain on this side Jordan eastward, even unto the sea of the plain, under the springs of Pisgah.
Deuteronomy 5
And*p Moses called all Israel, and said unto them, Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments which I speak in your ears this day, that ye may learn them, and keep, and do them.
The*p Lord*s our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.
The*p Lord*s made not this covenant with our fathers, but with us, even us, who are all of us here alive this day.

(I*p stood between the Lord*s and you at that time, to shew you the word of the Lord:*s for ye were afraid by reason of the fire, and went not up into the mount;) saying,
I*p am the Lord*s thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
Thou*p shalt have none other gods before me.
Thou*p shalt not make thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the waters beneath the earth:

But*p the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord*s thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, nor thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thine ox, nor thine ass, nor any of thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates; that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou.

And*p remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord*s thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the Lord*s thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.

These*p words the Lord*s spake unto all your assembly in the mount out of the midst of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, with a great voice: and he added no more. And he wrote them in two tables of stone, and delivered them unto me.
And*p it came to pass, when ye heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, (for the mountain did burn with fire,) that ye came near unto me, even all the heads of your tribes, and your elders;

And*p ye said, Behold, the Lord*s our God hath shewed us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire: we have seen this day that God doth talk with man, and he liveth.

Deuteronomy 6
Now*p these are the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments, which the Lord*s your God commanded to teach you, that ye might do them in the land whither ye go to possess it:

And*p thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord:*s that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest go in and possess the good land which the Lord*s sware unto thy fathers,
To*p cast out all thine enemies from before thee, as the Lord*s hath spoken.

Then*p thou shalt say unto thy son, We were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt; and the Lord*s brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand:

Deuteronomy 7

When*p the Lord*s thy God shall bring thee into the land whither thou goest to possess it, and hath cast out many nations before thee, the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than thou;
And*p when the Lord*s thy God shall deliver them before thee; thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them:

And*p repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them: he will not be slack to him that hateth him, he will repay him to his face.

Wherefore*p it shall come to pass, if ye hearken to these judgments, and keep, and do them, that the Lord*s thy God shall keep unto thee the covenant and the mercy which he sware unto thy fathers:

And*p he will love thee, and bless thee, and multiply thee: he will also bless the fruit of thy womb, and the fruit of thy land, thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep, in the land which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee.
Thou*p shalt be blessed above all people: there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle.
And*p the Lord*s will take away from thee all sickness, and will put none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which thou knowest, upon thee; but will lay them upon all them that hate thee.

Deuteronomy 9

Remember,*p and forget not, how thou provokedst the Lord*s thy God to wrath in the wilderness: from the day that thou didst depart out of the land of Egypt, until ye came unto this place, ye have been rebellious against the Lord.*s

When*p I was gone up into the mount to receive the tables of stone, even the tables of the covenant which the Lord*s made with you, then I abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, I neither did eat bread nor drink water:

And*p the Lord*s delivered unto me two tables of stone written with the finger of God; and on them was written according to all the words, which the Lord*s spake with you in the mount out of the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly.

Deuteronomy 11

For*p the land, whither thou goest in to possess it, is not as the land of Egypt, from whence ye came out, where thou sowedst thy seed, and wateredst it with thy foot, as a garden of herbs:

Thou*p shalt not eat it; that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee, when thou shalt do that which is right in the sight of the Lord.*s

The*p hart, and the roebuck, and the fallow deer, and the wild goat, and the pygarg, and the wild ox, and the chamois.

And*p the glede, and the kite, and the vulture after his kind,
And*p every raven after his kind,
And*p the owl, and the night hawk, and the cuckow, and the hawk after his kind,
The*p little owl, and the great owl, and the swan,
