So*p Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
And*p the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king's face.
But*p in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

And*p when he polled his head, (for it was at every year's end that he polled it: because the hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king's weight.
And*p unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.
So*p Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king's face.
Therefore*p Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.
Therefore*p he said unto his servants, See, Joab's field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
Then*p Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?

And*p Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur? it had been good for me to have been there still: now therefore let me see the king's face; and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me.
So*p Joab came to the king, and told him: and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.
2 Samuel 15
And*p it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

And*p Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
And*p Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.
Absalom*p said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!
And*p it was so, that when any man came nigh to him to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.
And*p on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
And*p it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto the Lord,*s in Hebron.
For*p thy servant vowed a vow while I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the Lord*s shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I will serve the Lord.*s
And*p the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and went to Hebron.
But*p Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.
And*p with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, that were called; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew not any thing.

And*p Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.
And*p there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.

And*p David said unto all his servants that were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not else escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.
And*p the king's servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint.
And*p the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women, which were concubines, to keep the house.
And*p the king went forth, and all the people after him, and tarried in a place that was far off.
And*p all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men which came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Then*p said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also with us? return to thy place, and abide with the king: for thou art a stranger, and also an exile.
Whereas*p thou camest but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and down with us? seeing I go whither I may, return thou, and take back thy brethren: mercy and truth be with thee.

And*p Ittai answered the king, and said, As the Lord*s liveth, and as my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will thy servant be.
And*p David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that were with him.
And*p all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.

And*p lo Zadok also, and all the Levites were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
And*p the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favour in the eyes of the Lord,*s he will bring me again, and shew me both it, and his habitation:
But*p if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.
The*p king said also unto Zadok the priest, Art not thou a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
See,*p I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.
Zadok*p therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there.

And*p David went up by the ascent of mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot: and all the people that was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
And*p one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O Lord,*s I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.
And*p it came to pass, that when David was come to the top of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head:
Unto*p whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:

But*p if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father's servant hitherto, so will I now also be thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.

And*p hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, that what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king's house, thou shalt tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
Behold,*p they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok's son, and Jonathan Abiathar's son; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.
So*p Hushai David's friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
2 Samuel 16

And*p when David was a little past the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

And*p the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses be for the king's household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.
And*p the king said, And where is thy master's son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
Then*p said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.
And*p when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
And*p he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
And*p thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:

The*p Lord*s hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the Lord*s hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou art taken in thy mischief, because thou art a bloody man.
Then*p said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
And*p the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the Lord*s hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

And*p David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the Lord*s hath bidden him.
It*p may be that the Lord*s will look on mine affliction, and that the Lord*s will requite me good for his cursing this day.
And*p as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill's side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.
And*p the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.
And*p Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
And*p it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.
And*p Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?
And*p Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the Lord,*s and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.
And*p again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father's presence, so will I be in thy presence.
Then*p said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.

And*p Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father's concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
So*p they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
And*p the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
2 Samuel 17
Moreover*p Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
And*p I will come upon him while he is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
And*p I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.
And*p the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.
Then*p said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.
And*p when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do after his saying? if not; speak thou.
And*p Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given is not good at this time.

For,*p said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.

Behold,*p he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.
And*p he also that is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father is a mighty man, and they which be with him are valiant men.
Therefore*p I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beer–sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.

So*p shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that are with him there shall not be left so much as one.
Moreover,*p if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.

And*p Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the Lord*s had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the Lord*s might bring evil upon Absalom.
Then*p said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.

Now*p therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.
Now*p Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by En–rogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.
Nevertheless*p a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man's house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.
And*p the woman took and spread a covering over the well's mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.

And*p when Absalom's servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

And*p it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
Then*p David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.

And*p when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.
Then*p David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

And*p Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man's son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab's mother.
So*p Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.

And*p it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo–debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
Brought*p beds, and basins, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched pulse,
And*p honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
2 Samuel 18
And*p David numbered the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

And*p David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.

But*p the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now thou art worth ten thousand of us: therefore now it is better that thou succour us out of the city.
And*p the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.

And*p the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.
So*p the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;
Where*p the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand men.
For*p the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

And*p Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away.
And*p a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
And*p Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten shekels of silver, and a girdle.

And*p the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against the king's son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.
Otherwise*p I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against me.
Then*p said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
And*p ten young men that bare Joab's armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.
And*p Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.
And*p they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.

Now*p Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which is in the king's dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom's place.
Then*p said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the Lord*s hath avenged him of his enemies.
And*p Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king's son is dead.
Then*p said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what thou hast seen. And Cushi bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.

Then*p said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready?
But*p howsoever, said he, let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.
And*p David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
And*p the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.
And*p the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold another man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.
And*p the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and cometh with good tidings.

And*p Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed be the Lord*s thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.
And*p the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king's servant, and me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.
And*p the king said unto him, Turn aside, and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.
And,*p behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the Lord*s hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.
And*p the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do thee hurt, be as that young man is.

And*p the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!
2 Samuel 19
And*p it was told Joab, Behold, the king weepeth and mourneth for Absalom.
And*p the victory that day was turned into mourning unto all the people: for the people heard say that day how the king was grieved for his son.
And*p the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
But*p the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!

And*p Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, which this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;

In*p that thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends. For thou hast declared this day, that thou regardest neither princes nor servants: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased thee well.

Now*p therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants: for I swear by the Lord,*s if thou go not forth, there will not tarry one with thee this night: and that will be worse unto thee than all the evil that befell thee from thy youth until now.

Then*p the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king doth sit in the gate. And all the people came before the king: for Israel had fled every man to his tent.

And*p all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.
And*p Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak ye not a word of bringing the king back?

And*p king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, even to his house.
Ye*p are my brethren, ye are my bones and my flesh: wherefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?
And*p say ye to Amasa, Art thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.
And*p he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as the heart of one man; so that they sent this word unto the king, Return thou, and all thy servants.
So*p the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.
And*p Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
And*p there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.
And*p there went over a ferry boat to carry over the king's household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was come over Jordan;

And*p said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
For*p thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.
But*p Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the Lord's*s anointed?

And*p David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I am this day king over Israel?
Therefore*p the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.

And*p Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came again in peace.
And*p it came to pass, when he was come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest not thou with me, Mephibosheth?
And*p he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I will saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go to the king; because thy servant is lame.
And*p he hath slandered thy servant unto my lord the king; but my lord the king is as an angel of God: do therefore what is good in thine eyes.

For*p all of my father's house were but dead men before my lord the king: yet didst thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine own table. What right therefore have I yet to cry any more unto the king?
And*p the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba divide the land.
And*p Mephibosheth said unto the king, Yea, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord the king is come again in peace unto his own house.
And*p Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
Now*p Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.
And*p the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.
And*p Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?

I*p am this day fourscore years old: and can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?
Thy*p servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?

Let*p thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
And*p the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.
And*p all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
Then*p the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him: and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel.

And,*p behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David's men with him, over Jordan?

And*p all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to us: wherefore then be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king's cost? or hath he given us any gift?

And*p the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
2 Samuel 20

And*p there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
So*p every man of Israel went up from after David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.

And*p David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them, but went not in unto them. So they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood.
Then*p said the king to Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah within three days, and be thou here present.
So*p Amasa went to assemble the men of Judah: but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him.
And*p David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord's servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.
And*p there went out after him Joab's men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

When*p they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa went before them. And Joab's garment that he had put on was girded unto him, and upon it a girdle with a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.
And*p Joab said to Amasa, Art thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.

But*p Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab's hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
And*p one of Joab's men stood by him, and said, He that favoureth Joab, and he that is for David, let him go after Joab.

And*p Amasa wallowed in blood in the midst of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he removed Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a cloth upon him, when he saw that every one that came by him stood still.
When*p he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
And*p he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Beth–maachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.

And*p they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth–maachah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it stood in the trench: and all the people that were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.
Then*p cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.
And*p when he was come near unto her, the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he answered, I am he. Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.
Then*p she spake, saying, They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask counsel at Abel: and so they ended the matter.
I*p am one of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the Lord?*s
And*p Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

The*p matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.

Then*p the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.
Now*p Joab was over all the host of Israel: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites:
And*p Adoram was over the tribute: and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder:
And*p Sheva was scribe: and Zadok and Abiathar were the priests:
And*p Ira also the Jairite was a chief ruler about David.
2 Samuel 21

Then*p there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David enquired of the Lord.*s And the Lord*s answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.

And*p the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them; (now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal to the children of Israel and Judah.)
Wherefore*p David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the Lord?*s

And*p the Gibeonites said unto him, We will have no silver nor gold of Saul, nor of his house; neither for us shalt thou kill any man in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that will I do for you.
And*p they answered the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the coasts of Israel,
Let*p seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto the Lord*s in Gibeah of Saul, whom the Lord*s did choose. And the king said, I will give them.
But*p the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the Lord's*s oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

But*p the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:

And*p he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the Lord:*s and they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.

And*p Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and suffered neither the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
And*p it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

And*p David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh–gilead, which had stolen them from the street of Beth–shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:
And*p he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.

And*p the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was entreated for the land.
Moreover*p the Philistines had yet war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines: and David waxed faint.
And*p Ishbi–benob, which was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of brass in weight, he being girded with a new sword, thought to have slain David.

But*p Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the light of Israel.
And*p it came to pass after this, that there was again a battle with the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbecai the Hushathite slew Saph, which was of the sons of the giant.

And*p there was again a battle in Gob with the Philistines, where Elhanan the son of Jaare–oregim, a Beth–lehemite, slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
And*p there was yet a battle in Gath, where was a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to the giant.
And*p when he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimeah the brother of David slew him.
These*p four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
2 Samuel 22
And*p David spake unto the Lord*s the words of this song in the day that the Lord*s had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul:
And*p he said, The Lord*s is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;
The*p God of my rock; in him will I trust: he is my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge, my saviour; thou savest me from violence.
I*p will call on the Lord,*s who is worthy to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies.
When*p the waves of death compassed me, the floods of ungodly men made me afraid;
The*p sorrows of hell compassed me about; the snares of death prevented me;
In*p my distress I called upon the Lord,*s and cried to my God: and he did hear my voice out of his temple, and my cry did enter into his ears.
Then*p the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of heaven moved and shook, because he was wroth.
There*p went up a smoke out of his nostrils, and fire out of his mouth devoured: coals were kindled by it.
He*p bowed the heavens also, and came down; and darkness was under his feet.
And*p he rode upon a cherub, and did fly: and he was seen upon the wings of the wind.
And*p he made darkness pavilions round about him, dark waters, and thick clouds of the skies.
Through*p the brightness before him were coals of fire kindled.
The*p Lord*s thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.
And*p he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.
And*p the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the Lord,*s at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
He*p sent from above, he took me; he drew me out of many waters;
He*p delivered me from my strong enemy, and from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me.
They*p prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the Lord*s was my stay.
He*p brought me forth also into a large place: he delivered me, because he delighted in me.
The*p Lord*s rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.
For*p I have kept the ways of the Lord,*s and have not wickedly departed from my God.
For*p all his judgments were before me: and as for his statutes, I did not depart from them.
I*p was also upright before him, and have kept myself from mine iniquity.
Therefore*p the Lord*s hath recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to my cleanness in his eye sight.
With*p the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful, and with the upright man thou wilt shew thyself upright.
With*p the pure thou wilt shew thyself pure; and with the froward thou wilt shew thyself unsavoury.
And*p the afflicted people thou wilt save: but thine eyes are upon the haughty, that thou mayest bring them down.
For*p thou art my lamp, O Lord:*s and the Lord*s will lighten my darkness.
For*p by thee I have run through a troop: by my God have I leaped over a wall.
As*p for God, his way is perfect; the word of the Lord*s is tried: he is a buckler to all them that trust in him.
For*p who is God, save the Lord?*s and who is a rock, save our God?
God*p is my strength and power: and he maketh my way perfect.
He*p maketh my feet like hinds' feet: and setteth me upon my high places.
He*p teacheth my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.
Thou*p hast also given me the shield of thy salvation: and thy gentleness hath made me great.
Thou*p hast enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not slip.
I*p have pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them; and turned not again until I had consumed them.
And*p I have consumed them, and wounded them, that they could not arise: yea, they are fallen under my feet.
For*p thou hast girded me with strength to battle: them that rose up against me hast thou subdued under me.
Thou*p hast also given me the necks of mine enemies, that I might destroy them that hate me.
They*p looked, but there was none to save; even unto the Lord,*s but he answered them not.
Then*p did I beat them as small as the dust of the earth, I did stamp them as the mire of the street, and did spread them abroad.
Thou*p also hast delivered me from the strivings of my people, thou hast kept me to be head of the heathen: a people which I knew not shall serve me.
Strangers*p shall submit themselves unto me: as soon as they hear, they shall be obedient unto me.
Strangers*p shall fade away, and they shall be afraid out of their close places.
The*p Lord*s liveth; and blessed be my rock; and exalted be the God of the rock of my salvation.
It*p is God that avengeth me, and that bringeth down the people under me,
And*p that bringeth me forth from mine enemies: thou also hast lifted me up on high above them that rose up against me: thou hast delivered me from the violent man.
Therefore*p I will give thanks unto thee, O Lord,*s among the heathen, and I will sing praises unto thy name.
He*p is the tower of salvation for his king: and sheweth mercy to his anointed, unto David, and to his seed for evermore.
2 Samuel 23
Now*p these be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,
The*p Spirit of the Lord*s spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.
The*p God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.
And*p he shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.

Although*p my house be not so with God; yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure: for this is all my salvation, and all my desire, although he make it not to grow.
But*p the sons of Belial shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands:
But*p the man that shall touch them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear; and they shall be utterly burned with fire in the same place.

These*p be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time.

And*p after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:
He*p arose, and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave unto the sword: and the Lord*s wrought a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to spoil.

And*p after him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where was a piece of ground full of lentiles: and the people fled from the Philistines.
But*p he stood in the midst of the ground, and defended it, and slew the Philistines: and the Lord*s wrought a great victory.
And*p three of the thirty chief went down, and came to David in the harvest time unto the cave of Adullam: and the troop of the Philistines pitched in the valley of Rephaim.
And*p David was then in an hold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Beth–lehem.
And*p David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Beth–lehem, which is by the gate!

And*p the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Beth–lehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: nevertheless he would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto the Lord.*s

And*p he said, Be it far from me, O Lord,*s that I should do this: is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men.
And*p Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief among three. And he lifted up his spear against three hundred, and slew them, and had the name among three.
Was*p he not most honourable of three? therefore he was their captain: howbeit he attained not unto the first three.

And*p Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, of Kabzeel, who had done many acts, he slew two lionlike men of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow:

And*p he slew an Egyptian, a goodly man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and slew him with his own spear.
These*p things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had the name among three mighty men.
He*p was more honourable than the thirty, but he attained not to the first three. And David set him over his guard.
Asahel*p the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Beth–lehem,
Shammah*p the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
Helez*p the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
Abiezer*p the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
Zalmon*p the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
Heleb*p the son of Baanah, a Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
Benaiah*p the Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,
Abi–albon*p the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
Eliahba*p the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah*p the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite,
Eliphelet*p the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
Hezrai*p the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
Igal*p the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
Zelek*p the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armourbearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah,
Ira*p an Ithrite, Gareb an Ithrite,
Uriah*p the Hittite: thirty and seven in all.
2 Samuel 24
And*p again the anger of the Lord*s was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.

For*p the king said to Joab the captain of the host, which was with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beer–sheba, and number ye the people, that I may know the number of the people.

And*p Joab said unto the king, Now the Lord*s thy God add unto the people, how many soever they be, an hundredfold, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see it: but why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?

Notwithstanding*p the king's word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.
And*p they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that lieth in the midst of the river of Gad, and toward Jazer:
Then*p they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim–hodshi; and they came to Dan–jaan, and about to Zidon,
And*p came to the strong hold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites: and they went out to the south of Judah, even to Beer–sheba.
So*p when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

And*p Joab gave up the sum of the number of the people unto the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

And*p David's heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto the Lord,*s I have sinned greatly in that I have done: and now, I beseech thee, O Lord,*s take away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.
For*p when David was up in the morning, the word of the Lord*s came unto the prophet Gad, David's seer, saying,
Go*p and say unto David, Thus saith the Lord,*s I offer thee three things; choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.

So*p Gad came to David, and told him, and said unto him, Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thine enemies, while they pursue thee? or that there be three days' pestilence in thy land? now advise, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me.
And*p David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of the Lord;*s for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.
So*p the Lord*s sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the time appointed: and there died of the people from Dan even to Beer–sheba seventy thousand men.

And*p when the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it, the Lord*s repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, It is enough: stay now thine hand. And the angel of the Lord*s was by the threshingplace of Araunah the Jebusite.

And*p David spake unto the Lord*s when he saw the angel that smote the people, and said, Lo, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father's house.
And*p Gad came that day to David, and said unto him, Go up, rear an altar unto the Lord*s in the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite.
And*p David, according to the saying of Gad, went up as the Lord*s commanded.
And*p Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming on toward him: and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king on his face upon the ground.

And*p Araunah said, Wherefore is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshingfloor of thee, to build an altar unto the Lord,*s that the plague may be stayed from the people.

And*p Araunah said unto David, Let my lord the king take and offer up what seemeth good unto him: behold, here be oxen for burnt sacrifice, and threshing instruments and other instruments of the oxen for wood.
All*p these things did Araunah, as a king, give unto the king. And Araunah said unto the king, The Lord*s thy God accept thee.

And*p the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the Lord*s my God of that which doth cost me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
And*p David built there an altar unto the Lord,*s and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the Lord*s was entreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.
1 Kings 1
Now*p king David was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.

Wherefore*p his servants said unto him, Let there be sought for my lord the king a young virgin: and let her stand before the king, and let her cherish him, and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get heat.
So*p they sought for a fair damsel throughout all the coasts of Israel, and found Abishag a Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
And*p the damsel was very fair, and cherished the king, and ministered to him: but the king knew her not.
Then*p Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
And*p his father had not displeased him at any time in saying, Why hast thou done so? and he also was a very goodly man; and his mother bare him after Absalom.
And*p he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest: and they following Adonijah helped him.
But*p Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men which belonged to David, were not with Adonijah.
And*p Adonijah slew sheep and oxen and fat cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, which is by En–rogel, and called all his brethren the king's sons, and all the men of Judah the king's servants:
But*p Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother, he called not.
Wherefore*p Nathan spake unto Bath–sheba the mother of Solomon, saying, Hast thou not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith doth reign, and David our lord knoweth it not?
Now*p therefore come, let me, I pray thee, give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine own life, and the life of thy son Solomon.

Go*p and get thee in unto king David, and say unto him, Didst not thou, my lord, O king, swear unto thine handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne? why then doth Adonijah reign?
Behold,*p while thou yet talkest there with the king, I also will come in after thee, and confirm thy words.
And*p Bath–sheba went in unto the king into the chamber: and the king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite ministered unto the king.
And*p Bath–sheba bowed, and did obeisance unto the king. And the king said, What wouldest thou?
And*p she said unto him, My lord, thou swarest by the Lord*s thy God unto thine handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne.
And*p now, behold, Adonijah reigneth; and now, my lord the king, thou knowest it not:

And*p he hath slain oxen and fat cattle and sheep in abundance, and hath called all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the host: but Solomon thy servant hath he not called.
And*p thou, my lord, O king, the eyes of all Israel are upon thee, that thou shouldest tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
Otherwise*p it shall come to pass, when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon shall be counted offenders.
And,*p lo, while she yet talked with the king, Nathan the prophet also came in.
And*p they told the king, saying, Behold Nathan the prophet. And when he was come in before the king, he bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.
And*p Nathan said, My lord, O king, hast thou said, Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne?

For*p he is gone down this day, and hath slain oxen and fat cattle and sheep in abundance, and hath called all the king's sons, and the captains of the host, and Abiathar the priest; and, behold, they eat and drink before him, and say, God save king Adonijah.
But*p me, even me thy servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and thy servant Solomon, hath he not called.
Is*p this thing done by my lord the king, and thou hast not shewed it unto thy servant, who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?
Then*p king David answered and said, Call me Bath–sheba. And she came into the king's presence, and stood before the king.
And*p the king sware, and said, As the Lord*s liveth, that hath redeemed my soul out of all distress,
Even*p as I sware unto thee by the Lord*s God of Israel, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead; even so will I certainly do this day.
Then*p Bath–sheba bowed with her face to the earth, and did reverence to the king, and said, Let my lord king David live for ever.
And*p king David said, Call me Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada. And they came before the king.
The*p king also said unto them, Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride upon mine own mule, and bring him down to Gihon:
And*p let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel: and blow ye with the trumpet, and say, God save king Solomon.
Then*p ye shall come up after him, that he may come and sit upon my throne; for he shall be king in my stead: and I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah.
And*p Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king, and said, Amen: the Lord*s God of my lord the king say so too.
As*p the Lord*s hath been with my lord the king, even so be he with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord king David.

So*p Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, went down, and caused Solomon to ride upon king David's mule, and brought him to Gihon.
And*p Zadok the priest took an horn of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet; and all the people said, God save king Solomon.
And*p all the people came up after him, and the people piped with pipes, and rejoiced with great joy, so that the earth rent with the sound of them.

And*p Adonijah and all the guests that were with him heard it as they had made an end of eating. And when Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, Wherefore is this noise of the city being in an uproar?
And*p while he yet spake, behold, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came: and Adonijah said unto him, Come in; for thou art a valiant man, and bringest good tidings.
And*p Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, Verily our lord king David hath made Solomon king.

And*p the king hath sent with him Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and they have caused him to ride upon the king's mule:
And*p Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon: and they are come up from thence rejoicing, so that the city rang again. This is the noise that ye have heard.
And*p also Solomon sitteth on the throne of the kingdom.

And*p moreover the king's servants came to bless our lord king David, saying, God make the name of Solomon better than thy name, and make his throne greater than thy throne. And the king bowed himself upon the bed.
And*p also thus said the king, Blessed be the Lord*s God of Israel, which hath given one to sit on my throne this day, mine eyes even seeing it.
And*p all the guests that were with Adonijah were afraid, and rose up, and went every man his way.
And*p Adonijah feared because of Solomon, and arose, and went, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

And*p it was told Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonijah feareth king Solomon: for, lo, he hath caught hold on the horns of the altar, saying, Let king Solomon swear unto me to day that he will not slay his servant with the sword.
And*p Solomon said, If he will shew himself a worthy man, there shall not an hair of him fall to the earth: but if wickedness shall be found in him, he shall die.
So*p king Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed himself to king Solomon: and Solomon said unto him, Go to thine house.
1 Kings 2
Now*p the days of David drew nigh that he should die; and he charged Solomon his son, saying,
I*p go the way of all the earth: be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man;

And*p keep the charge of the Lord*s thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself:

That*p the Lord*s may continue his word which he spake concerning me, saying, If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.

Moreover*p thou knowest also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, unto Abner the son of Ner, and unto Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war upon his girdle that was about his loins, and in his shoes that were on his feet.
Do*p therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace.
But*p shew kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table: for so they came to me when I fled because of Absalom thy brother.

And,*p behold, thou hast with thee Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite of Bahurim, which cursed me with a grievous curse in the day when I went to Mahanaim: but he came down to meet me at Jordan, and I sware to him by the Lord,*s saying, I will not put thee to death with the sword.
Now*p therefore hold him not guiltless: for thou art a wise man, and knowest what thou oughtest to do unto him; but his hoar head bring thou down to the grave with blood.
So*p David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David.
And*p the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: seven years reigned he in Hebron, and thirty and three years reigned he in Jerusalem.
Then*p sat Solomon upon the throne of David his father; and his kingdom was established greatly.
And*p Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bath–sheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, Comest thou peaceably? And he said, Peaceably.
He*p said moreover, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And she said, Say on.

And*p he said, Thou knowest that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign: howbeit the kingdom is turned about, and is become my brother's: for it was his from the Lord.*s
And*p now I ask one petition of thee, deny me not. And she said unto him, Say on.
And*p he said, Speak, I pray thee, unto Solomon the king, (for he will not say thee nay,) that he give me Abishag the Shunammite to wife.
And*p Bath–sheba said, Well; I will speak for thee unto the king.

Bath–sheba*p therefore went unto king Solomon, to speak unto him for Adonijah. And the king rose up to meet her, and bowed himself unto her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a seat to be set for the king's mother; and she sat on his right hand.
Then*p she said, I desire one small petition of thee; I pray thee, say me not nay. And the king said unto her, Ask on, my mother: for I will not say thee nay.
And*p she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah thy brother to wife.

And*p king Solomon answered and said unto his mother, And why dost thou ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? ask for him the kingdom also; for he is mine elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.
Then*p king Solomon sware by the Lord,*s saying, God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah have not spoken this word against his own life.
Now*p therefore, as the Lord*s liveth, which hath established me, and set me on the throne of David my father, and who hath made me an house, as he promised, Adonijah shall be put to death this day.
And*p king Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell upon him that he died.

And*p unto Abiathar the priest said the king, Get thee to Anathoth, unto thine own fields; for thou art worthy of death: but I will not at this time put thee to death, because thou barest the ark of the Lord God*s before David my father, and because thou hast been afflicted in all wherein my father was afflicted.
So*p Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest unto the Lord;*s that he might fulfil the word of the Lord,*s which he spake concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
Then*p tidings came to Joab: for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he turned not after Absalom. And Joab fled unto the tabernacle of the Lord,*s and caught hold on the horns of the altar.
And*p it was told king Solomon that Joab was fled unto the tabernacle of the Lord;*s and, behold, he is by the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, fall upon him.

And*p Benaiah came to the tabernacle of the Lord,*s and said unto him, Thus saith the king, Come forth. And he said, Nay; but I will die here. And Benaiah brought the king word again, saying, Thus said Joab, and thus he answered me.
And*p the king said unto him, Do as he hath said, and fall upon him, and bury him; that thou mayest take away the innocent blood, which Joab shed, from me, and from the house of my father.

And*p the Lord*s shall return his blood upon his own head, who fell upon two men more righteous and better than he, and slew them with the sword, my father David not knowing thereof, to wit, Abner the son of Ner, captain of the host of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, captain of the host of Judah.

Their*p blood shall therefore return upon the head of Joab, and upon the head of his seed for ever: but upon David, and upon his seed, and upon his house, and upon his throne, shall there be peace for ever from the Lord.*s
So*p Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up, and fell upon him, and slew him: and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
And*p the king put Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his room over the host: and Zadok the priest did the king put in the room of Abiathar.
And*p the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Build thee an house in Jerusalem, and dwell there, and go not forth thence any whither.
For*p it shall be, that on the day thou goest out, and passest over the brook Kidron, thou shalt know for certain that thou shalt surely die: thy blood shall be upon thine own head.
And*p Shimei said unto the king, The saying is good: as my lord the king hath said, so will thy servant do. And Shimei dwelt in Jerusalem many days.
And*p it came to pass at the end of three years, that two of the servants of Shimei ran away unto Achish son of Maachah king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, Behold, thy servants be in Gath.
And*p Shimei arose, and saddled his ass, and went to Gath to Achish to seek his servants: and Shimei went, and brought his servants from Gath.
And*p it was told Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath, and was come again.

And*p the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Did I not make thee to swear by the Lord,*s and protested unto thee, saying, Know for a certain, on the day thou goest out, and walkest abroad any whither, that thou shalt surely die? and thou saidst unto me, The word that I have heard is good.
Why*p then hast thou not kept the oath of the Lord,*s and the commandment that I have charged thee with?

The*p king said moreover to Shimei, Thou knowest all the wickedness which thine heart is privy to, that thou didst to David my father: therefore the Lord*s shall return thy wickedness upon thine own head;
And*p king Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the Lord*s for ever.
So*p the king commanded Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; which went out, and fell upon him, that he died. And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.
1 Kings 3

And*p Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh's daughter, and brought her into the city of David, until he had made an end of building his own house, and the house of the Lord,*s and the wall of Jerusalem round about.
Only*p the people sacrificed in high places, because there was no house built unto the name of the Lord,*s until those days.
And*p Solomon loved the Lord,*s walking in the statutes of David his father: only he sacrificed and burnt incense in high places.
And*p the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that was the great high place: a thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar.
In*p Gibeon the Lord*s appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.

And*p Solomon said, Thou hast shewed unto thy servant David my father great mercy, according as he walked before thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with thee; and thou hast kept for him this great kindness, that thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.
And*p now, O Lord*s my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in.
And*p thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.
Give*p therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
And*p the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.

And*p God said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment;
Behold,*p I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.
And*p I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour: so that there shall not be any among the kings like unto thee all thy days.
And*p if thou wilt walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did walk, then I will lengthen thy days.

And*p Solomon awoke; and, behold, it was a dream. And he came to Jerusalem, and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord,*s and offered up burnt offerings, and offered peace offerings, and made a feast to all his servants.
Then*p came there two women, that were harlots, unto the king, and stood before him.
And*p the one woman said, O my lord, I and this woman dwell in one house; and I was delivered of a child with her in the house.
And*p it came to pass the third day after that I was delivered, that this woman was delivered also: and we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house, save we two in the house.
And*p this woman's child died in the night; because she overlaid it.
And*p she arose at midnight, and took my son from beside me, while thine handmaid slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.
And*p when I rose in the morning to give my child suck, behold, it was dead: but when I had considered it in the morning, behold, it was not my son, which I did bear.
And*p the other woman said, Nay; but the living is my son, and the dead is thy son. And this said, No; but the dead is thy son, and the living is my son. Thus they spake before the king.
Then*p said the king, The one saith, This is my son that liveth, and thy son is the dead: and the other saith, Nay; but thy son is the dead, and my son is the living.
And*p the king said, Bring me a sword. And they brought a sword before the king.
And*p the king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

Then*p spake the woman whose the living child was unto the king, for her bowels yearned upon her son, and she said, O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it. But the other said, Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it.
Then*p the king answered and said, Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof.
And*p all Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king: for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do judgment.
1 Kings 4
So*p king Solomon was king over all Israel.
And*p these were the princes which he had; Azariah the son of Zadok the priest,
Elihoreph*p and Ahiah, the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder.
And*p Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the host: and Zadok and Abiathar were the priests:
And*p Azariah the son of Nathan was over the officers: and Zabud the son of Nathan was principal officer, and the king's friend:
And*p Ahishar was over the household: and Adoniram the son of Abda was over the tribute.
And*p Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, which provided victuals for the king and his household: each man his month in a year made provision.
And*p these are their names: The son of Hur, in mount Ephraim:
The*p son of Dekar, in Makaz, and in Shaalbim, and Beth–shemesh, and Elon–beth–hanan:
The*p son of Hesed, in Aruboth; to him pertained Soco, and all the land of Hepher:
The*p son of Abinadab, in all the region of Dor; which had Taphath the daughter of Solomon to wife:
Baana*p the son of Ahilud; to him pertained Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth–shean, which is by Zarethan beneath Jezreel, from Beth–shean to Abel–meholah, even unto the place that is beyond Jokmeam:

The*p son of Geber, in Ramoth–gilead; to him pertained the towns of Jair the son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead; to him also pertained the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, threescore great cities with walls and brasen bars:
Ahinadab*p the son of Iddo had Mahanaim:
Ahimaaz*p was in Naphtali; he also took Basmath the daughter of Solomon to wife:
Baanah*p the son of Hushai was in Asher and in Aloth:
Jehoshaphat*p the son of Paruah, in Issachar:
Shimei*p the son of Elah, in Benjamin:
Geber*p the son of Uri was in the country of Gilead, in the country of Sihon king of the Amorites, and of Og king of Bashan; and he was the only officer which was in the land.
Judah*p and Israel were many, as the sand which is by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking, and making merry.
And*p Solomon reigned over all kingdoms from the river unto the land of the Philistines, and unto the border of Egypt: they brought presents, and served Solomon all the days of his life.
And*p Solomon's provision for one day was thirty measures of fine flour, and threescore measures of meal,
Ten*p fat oxen, and twenty oxen out of the pastures, and an hundred sheep, beside harts, and roebucks, and fallowdeer, and fatted fowl.
For*p he had dominion over all the region on this side the river, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings on this side the river: and he had peace on all sides round about him.
And*p Judah and Israel dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beer–sheba, all the days of Solomon.
And*p Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
And*p those officers provided victual for king Solomon, and for all that came unto king Solomon's table, every man in his month: they lacked nothing.
Barley*p also and straw for the horses and dromedaries brought they unto the place where the officers were, every man according to his charge.
And*p God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore.
And*p Solomon's wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.
For*p he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.
And*p he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five.
And*p he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.
And*p there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, which had heard of his wisdom.
1 Kings 5
And*p Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon; for he had heard that they had anointed him king in the room of his father: for Hiram was ever a lover of David.
And*p Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

Thou*p knowest how that David my father could not build an house unto the name of the Lord*s his God for the wars which were about him on every side, until the Lord*s put them under the soles of his feet.
But*p now the Lord*s my God hath given me rest on every side, so that there is neither adversary nor evil occurrent.

And,*p behold, I purpose to build an house unto the name of the Lord*s my God, as the Lord*s spake unto David my father, saying, Thy son, whom I will set upon thy throne in thy room, he shall build an house unto my name.

Now*p therefore command thou that they hew me cedar trees out of Lebanon; and my servants shall be with thy servants: and unto thee will I give hire for thy servants according to all that thou shalt appoint: for thou knowest that there is not among us any that can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians.
And*p it came to pass, when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, that he rejoiced greatly, and said, Blessed be the Lord*s this day, which hath given unto David a wise son over this great people.
And*p Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, I have considered the things which thou sentest to me for: and I will do all thy desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning timber of fir.

My*p servants shall bring them down from Lebanon unto the sea: and I will convey them by sea in floats unto the place that thou shalt appoint me, and will cause them to be discharged there, and thou shalt receive them: and thou shalt accomplish my desire, in giving food for my household.
So*p Hiram gave Solomon cedar trees and fir trees according to all his desire.
And*p Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat for food to his household, and twenty measures of pure oil: thus gave Solomon to Hiram year by year.
And*p the Lord*s gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him: and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together.
And*p king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.
And*p he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by courses: a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home: and Adoniram was over the levy.
And*p Solomon had threescore and ten thousand that bare burdens, and fourscore thousand hewers in the mountains;
Beside*p the chief of Solomon's officers which were over the work, three thousand and three hundred, which ruled over the people that wrought in the work.
And*p the king commanded, and they brought great stones, costly stones, and hewed stones, to lay the foundation of the house.
And*p Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders did hew them, and the stonesquarers: so they prepared timber and stones to build the house.
1 Kings 6
