And*p after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord*s was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.

And*p it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entering in of the cave. And, behold, there came a voice unto him, and said, What doest thou here, Elijah?

And*p he said, I have been very zealous for the Lord*s God of hosts: because the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.
And*p the Lord*s said unto him, Go, return on thy way to the wilderness of Damascus: and when thou comest, anoint Hazael to be king over Syria:
And*p Jehu the son of Nimshi shalt thou anoint to be king over Israel: and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel–meholah shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room.
And*p it shall come to pass, that him that escapeth the sword of Hazael shall Jehu slay: and him that escapeth from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha slay.
Yet*p I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him.
So*p he departed thence, and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he with the twelfth: and Elijah passed by him, and cast his mantle upon him.

And*p he left the oxen, and ran after Elijah, and said, Let me, I pray thee, kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow thee. And he said unto him, Go back again: for what have I done to thee?

And*p he returned back from him, and took a yoke of oxen, and slew them, and boiled their flesh with the instruments of the oxen, and gave unto the people, and they did eat. Then he arose, and went after Elijah, and ministered unto him.
1 Kings 20
And*p Ben–hadad the king of Syria gathered all his host together: and there were thirty and two kings with him, and horses, and chariots: and he went up and besieged Samaria, and warred against it.
And*p he sent messengers to Ahab king of Israel into the city, and said unto him, Thus saith Ben–hadad,
Thy*p silver and thy gold is mine; thy wives also and thy children, even the goodliest, are mine.
And*p the king of Israel answered and said, My lord, O king, according to thy saying, I am thine, and all that I have.
And*p the messengers came again, and said, Thus speaketh Ben–hadad, saying, Although I have sent unto thee, saying, Thou shalt deliver me thy silver, and thy gold, and thy wives, and thy children;

Yet*p I will send my servants unto thee to morrow about this time, and they shall search thine house, and the houses of thy servants; and it shall be, that whatsoever is pleasant in thine eyes, they shall put it in their hand, and take it away.

Then*p the king of Israel called all the elders of the land, and said, Mark, I pray you, and see how this man seeketh mischief: for he sent unto me for my wives, and for my children, and for my silver, and for my gold; and I denied him not.
And*p all the elders and all the people said unto him, Hearken not unto him, nor consent.

Wherefore*p he said unto the messengers of Ben–hadad, Tell my lord the king, All that thou didst send for to thy servant at the first I will do: but this thing I may not do. And the messengers departed, and brought him word again.
And*p Ben–hadad sent unto him, and said, The gods do so unto me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people that follow me.
And*p the king of Israel answered and said, Tell him, Let not him that girdeth on his harness boast himself as he that putteth it off.

And*p it came to pass, when Ben–hadad heard this message, as he was drinking, he and the kings in the pavilions, that he said unto his servants, Set yourselves in array. And they set themselves in array against the city.

And,*p behold, there came a prophet unto Ahab king of Israel, saying, Thus saith the Lord,*s Hast thou seen all this great multitude? behold, I will deliver it into thine hand this day; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.*s
And*p Ahab said, By whom? And he said, Thus saith the Lord,*s Even by the young men of the princes of the provinces. Then he said, Who shall order the battle? And he answered, Thou.

Then*p he numbered the young men of the princes of the provinces, and they were two hundred and thirty two: and after them he numbered all the people, even all the children of Israel, being seven thousand.
And*p they went out at noon. But Ben–hadad was drinking himself drunk in the pavilions, he and the kings, the thirty and two kings that helped him.
And*p the young men of the princes of the provinces went out first; and Ben–hadad sent out, and they told him, saying, There are men come out of Samaria.
And*p he said, Whether they be come out for peace, take them alive; or whether they be come out for war, take them alive.
So*p these young men of the princes of the provinces came out of the city, and the army which followed them.
And*p they slew every one his man: and the Syrians fled; and Israel pursued them: and Ben–hadad the king of Syria escaped on an horse with the horsemen.
And*p the king of Israel went out, and smote the horses and chariots, and slew the Syrians with a great slaughter.
And*p the prophet came to the king of Israel, and said unto him, Go, strengthen thyself, and mark, and see what thou doest: for at the return of the year the king of Syria will come up against thee.

And*p the servants of the king of Syria said unto him, Their gods are gods of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we; but let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they.
And*p do this thing, Take the kings away, every man out of his place, and put captains in their rooms:

And*p number thee an army, like the army that thou hast lost, horse for horse, and chariot for chariot: and we will fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they. And he hearkened unto their voice, and did so.
And*p it came to pass at the return of the year, that Ben–hadad numbered the Syrians, and went up to Aphek, to fight against Israel.

And*p the children of Israel were numbered, and were all present, and went against them: and the children of Israel pitched before them like two little flocks of kids; but the Syrians filled the country.

And*p there came a man of God, and spake unto the king of Israel, and said, Thus saith the Lord,*s Because the Syrians have said, The Lord*s is God of the hills, but he is not God of the valleys, therefore will I deliver all this great multitude into thine hand, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s

And*p they pitched one over against the other seven days. And so it was, that in the seventh day the battle was joined: and the children of Israel slew of the Syrians an hundred thousand footmen in one day.
But*p the rest fled to Aphek, into the city; and there a wall fell upon twenty and seven thousand of the men that were left. And Ben–hadad fled, and came into the city, into an inner chamber.

And*p his servants said unto him, Behold now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings: let us, I pray thee, put sackcloth on our loins, and ropes upon our heads, and go out to the king of Israel: peradventure he will save thy life.

So*p they girded sackcloth on their loins, and put ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel, and said, Thy servant Ben–hadad saith, I pray thee, let me live. And he said, Is he yet alive? he is my brother.

Now*p the men did diligently observe whether any thing would come from him, and did hastily catch it: and they said, Thy brother Ben–hadad. Then he said, Go ye, bring him. Then Ben–hadad came forth to him; and he caused him to come up into the chariot.

And*p Ben–hadad said unto him, The cities, which my father took from thy father, I will restore; and thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria. Then said Ahab, I will send thee away with this covenant. So he made a covenant with him, and sent him away.
And*p a certain man of the sons of the prophets said unto his neighbour in the word of the Lord,*s Smite me, I pray thee. And the man refused to smite him.

Then*p said he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voice of the Lord,*s behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lion shall slay thee. And as soon as he was departed from him, a lion found him, and slew him.
Then*p he found another man, and said, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man smote him, so that in smiting he wounded him.
So*p the prophet departed, and waited for the king by the way, and disguised himself with ashes upon his face.

And*p as the king passed by, he cried unto the king: and he said, Thy servant went out into the midst of the battle; and, behold, a man turned aside, and brought a man unto me, and said, Keep this man: if by any means he be missing, then shall thy life be for his life, or else thou shalt pay a talent of silver.
And*p as thy servant was busy here and there, he was gone. And the king of Israel said unto him, So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it.
And*p he hasted, and took the ashes away from his face; and the king of Israel discerned him that he was of the prophets.

And*p he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord,*s Because thou hast let go out of thy hand a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
And*p the king of Israel went to his house heavy and displeased, and came to Samaria.
1 Kings 21
And*p it came to pass after these things, that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, which was in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

And*p Ahab spake unto Naboth, saying, Give me thy vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it is near unto my house: and I will give thee for it a better vineyard than it; or, if it seem good to thee, I will give thee the worth of it in money.
And*p Naboth said to Ahab, The Lord*s forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.

And*p Ahab came into his house heavy and displeased because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him: for he had said, I will not give thee the inheritance of my fathers. And he laid him down upon his bed, and turned away his face, and would eat no bread.
But*p Jezebel his wife came to him, and said unto him, Why is thy spirit so sad, that thou eatest no bread?

And*p he said unto her, Because I spake unto Naboth the Jezreelite, and said unto him, Give me thy vineyard for money; or else, if it please thee, I will give thee another vineyard for it: and he answered, I will not give thee my vineyard.
And*p Jezebel his wife said unto him, Dost thou now govern the kingdom of Israel? arise, and eat bread, and let thine heart be merry: I will give thee the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
So*p she wrote letters in Ahab's name, and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters unto the elders and to the nobles that were in his city, dwelling with Naboth.
And*p she wrote in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people:
And*p set two men, sons of Belial, before him, to bear witness against him, saying, Thou didst blaspheme God and the king. And then carry him out, and stone him, that he may die.
And*p the men of his city, even the elders and the nobles who were the inhabitants in his city, did as Jezebel had sent unto them, and as it was written in the letters which she had sent unto them.
They*p proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people.

And*p there came in two men, children of Belial, and sat before him: and the men of Belial witnessed against him, even against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying, Naboth did blaspheme God and the king. Then they carried him forth out of the city, and stoned him with stones, that he died.
Then*p they sent to Jezebel, saying, Naboth is stoned, and is dead.

And*p it came to pass, when Jezebel heard that Naboth was stoned, and was dead, that Jezebel said to Ahab, Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give thee for money: for Naboth is not alive, but dead.
And*p it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab rose up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
And*p the word of the Lord*s came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Arise,*p go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, which is in Samaria: behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, whither he is gone down to possess it.

And*p thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord,*s Hast thou killed, and also taken possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord,*s In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.
And*p Ahab said to Elijah, Hast thou found me, O mine enemy? And he answered, I have found thee: because thou hast sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the Lord.*s
Behold,*p I will bring evil upon thee, and will take away thy posterity, and will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel,

And*p will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, for the provocation wherewith thou hast provoked me to anger, and made Israel to sin.
And*p of Jezebel also spake the Lord,*s saying, The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.
Him*p that dieth of Ahab in the city the dogs shall eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat.
But*p there was none like unto Ahab, which did sell himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord,*s whom Jezebel his wife stirred up.
And*p he did very abominably in following idols, according to all things as did the Amorites, whom the Lord*s cast out before the children of Israel.
And*p it came to pass, when Ahab heard those words, that he rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his flesh, and fasted, and lay in sackcloth, and went softly.
And*p the word of the Lord*s came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Seest*p thou how Ahab humbleth himself before me? because he humbleth himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days: but in his son's days will I bring the evil upon his house.
1 Kings 22
And*p they continued three years without war between Syria and Israel.
And*p it came to pass in the third year, that Jehoshaphat the king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.
And*p the king of Israel said unto his servants, Know ye that Ramoth in Gilead is ours, and we be still, and take it not out of the hand of the king of Syria?
And*p he said unto Jehoshaphat, Wilt thou go with me to battle to Ramoth–gilead? And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses.
And*p Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of the Lord*s to day.

Then*p the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said unto them, Shall I go against Ramoth–gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king.
And*p Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord*s besides, that we might enquire of him?

And*p the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, by whom we may enquire of the Lord:*s but I hate him; for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.
Then*p the king of Israel called an officer, and said, Hasten hither Micaiah the son of Imlah.

And*p the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah sat each on his throne, having put on their robes, in a void place in the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.
And*p Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made him horns of iron: and he said, Thus saith the Lord,*s With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until thou have consumed them.
And*p all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth–gilead, and prosper: for the Lord*s shall deliver it into the king's hand.

And*p the messenger that was gone to call Micaiah spake unto him, saying, Behold now, the words of the prophets declare good unto the king with one mouth: let thy word, I pray thee, be like the word of one of them, and speak that which is good.
And*p Micaiah said, As the Lord*s liveth, what the Lord*s saith unto me, that will I speak.

So*p he came to the king. And the king said unto him, Micaiah, shall we go against Ramoth–gilead to battle, or shall we forbear? And he answered him, Go, and prosper: for the Lord*s shall deliver it into the hand of the king.
And*p the king said unto him, How many times shall I adjure thee that thou tell me nothing but that which is true in the name of the Lord?*s
And*p he said, I saw all Israel scattered upon the hills, as sheep that have not a shepherd: and the Lord*s said, These have no master: let them return every man to his house in peace.
And*p the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee that he would prophesy no good concerning me, but evil?
And*p he said, Hear thou therefore the word of the Lord:*s I saw the Lord*s sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.
And*p the Lord*s said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead? And one said on this manner, and another said on that manner.
And*p there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord,*s and said, I will persuade him.

And*p the Lord*s said unto him, Wherewith? And he said, I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.
Now*p therefore, behold, the Lord*s hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the Lord*s hath spoken evil concerning thee.
But*p Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah went near, and smote Micaiah on the cheek, and said, Which way went the Spirit of the Lord*s from me to speak unto thee?
And*p Micaiah said, Behold, thou shalt see in that day, when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.
And*p the king of Israel said, Take Micaiah, and carry him back unto Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king's son;
And*p say, Thus saith the king, Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.
And*p Micaiah said, If thou return at all in peace, the Lord*s hath not spoken by me. And he said, Hearken, O people, every one of you.
So*p the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went up to Ramoth–gilead.
And*p the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself, and enter into the battle; but put thou on thy robes. And the king of Israel disguised himself, and went into the battle.
But*p the king of Syria commanded his thirty and two captains that had rule over his chariots, saying, Fight neither with small nor great, save only with the king of Israel.
And*p it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, Surely it is the king of Israel. And they turned aside to fight against him: and Jehoshaphat cried out.
And*p it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots perceived that it was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him.

And*p a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
And*p the battle increased that day: and the king was stayed up in his chariot against the Syrians, and died at even: and the blood ran out of the wound into the midst of the chariot.
And*p there went a proclamation throughout the host about the going down of the sun, saying, Every man to his city, and every man to his own country.
So*p the king died, and was brought to Samaria; and they buried the king in Samaria.
And*p one washed the chariot in the pool of Samaria; and the dogs licked up his blood; and they washed his armour; according unto the word of the Lord*s which he spake.

Now*p the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house which he made, and all the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
So*p Ahab slept with his fathers; and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.
And*p Jehoshaphat the son of Asa began to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat*p was thirty and five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

And*p he walked in all the ways of Asa his father; he turned not aside from it, doing that which was right in the eyes of the Lord:*s nevertheless the high places were not taken away; for the people offered and burnt incense yet in the high places.
And*p Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
Now*p the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he shewed, and how he warred, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And*p the remnant of the sodomites, which remained in the days of his father Asa, he took out of the land.
There*p was then no king in Edom: a deputy was king.
Jehoshaphat*p made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold: but they went not; for the ships were broken at Ezion–geber.
Then*p said Ahaziah the son of Ahab unto Jehoshaphat, Let my servants go with thy servants in the ships. But Jehoshaphat would not.
And*p Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.
Ahaziah*p the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned two years over Israel.
And*p he did evil in the sight of the Lord,*s and walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin:
For*p he served Baal, and worshipped him, and provoked to anger the Lord*s God of Israel, according to all that his father had done.
2 Kings 1
Then*p Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.

And*p Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.

But*p the angel of the Lord*s said to Elijah the Tishbite, Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say unto them, Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron?
Now*p therefore thus saith the Lord,*s Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. And Elijah departed.
And*p when the messengers turned back unto him, he said unto them, Why are ye now turned back?

And*p they said unto him, There came a man up to meet us, and said unto us, Go, turn again unto the king that sent you, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord,*s Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that thou sendest to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron? therefore thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.
And*p he said unto them, What manner of man was he which came up to meet you, and told you these words?
And*p they answered him, He was an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins. And he said, It is Elijah the Tishbite.

Then*p the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

And*p Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
Again*p also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come down quickly.

And*p Elijah answered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came down from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.

And*p he sent again a captain of the third fifty with his fifty. And the third captain of fifty went up, and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and besought him, and said unto him, O man of God, I pray thee, let my life, and the life of these fifty thy servants, be precious in thy sight.
Behold,*p there came fire down from heaven, and burnt up the two captains of the former fifties with their fifties: therefore let my life now be precious in thy sight.
And*p the angel of the Lord*s said unto Elijah, Go down with him: be not afraid of him. And he arose, and went down with him unto the king.

And*p he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord,*s Forasmuch as thou hast sent messengers to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron, is it not because there is no God in Israel to enquire of his word? therefore thou shalt not come down off that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.
So*p he died according to the word of the Lord*s which Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram reigned in his stead in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; because he had no son.
Now*p the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 2
And*p it came to pass, when the Lord*s would take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind, that Elijah went with Elisha from Gilgal.

And*p Elijah said unto Elisha, Tarry here, I pray thee; for the Lord*s hath sent me to Beth–el. And Elisha said unto him, As the Lord*s liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they went down to Beth–el.

And*p the sons of the prophets that were at Beth–el came forth to Elisha, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Lord*s will take away thy master from thy head to day? And he said, Yea, I know it; hold ye your peace.

And*p Elijah said unto him, Elisha, tarry here, I pray thee; for the Lord*s hath sent me to Jericho. And he said, As the Lord*s liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they came to Jericho.

And*p the sons of the prophets that were at Jericho came to Elisha, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Lord*s will take away thy master from thy head to day? And he answered, Yea, I know it; hold ye your peace.
And*p Elijah said unto him, Tarry, I pray thee, here; for the Lord*s hath sent me to Jordan. And he said, As the Lord*s liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And they two went on.
And*p fifty men of the sons of the prophets went, and stood to view afar off: and they two stood by Jordan.
And*p Elijah took his mantle, and wrapped it together, and smote the waters, and they were divided hither and thither, so that they two went over on dry ground.

And*p it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.
And*p he said, Thou hast asked a hard thing: nevertheless, if thou see me when I am taken from thee, it shall be so unto thee; but if not, it shall not be so.

And*p it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
And*p Elisha saw it, and he cried, My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof. And he saw him no more: and he took hold of his own clothes, and rent them in two pieces.
He*p took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and went back, and stood by the bank of Jordan;

And*p he took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and said, Where is the Lord*s God of Elijah? and when he also had smitten the waters, they parted hither and thither: and Elisha went over.

And*p when the sons of the prophets which were to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him.

And*p they said unto him, Behold now, there be with thy servants fifty strong men; let them go, we pray thee, and seek thy master: lest peradventure the Spirit of the Lord*s hath taken him up, and cast him upon some mountain, or into some valley. And he said, Ye shall not send.
And*p when they urged him till he was ashamed, he said, Send. They sent therefore fifty men; and they sought three days, but found him not.
And*p when they came again to him, (for he tarried at Jericho,) he said unto them, Did I not say unto you, Go not?
And*p the men of the city said unto Elisha, Behold, I pray thee, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord seeth: but the water is naught, and the ground barren.
And*p he said, Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein. And they brought it to him.

And*p he went forth unto the spring of the waters, and cast the salt in there, and said, Thus saith the Lord,*s I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land.
So*p the waters were healed unto this day, according to the saying of Elisha which he spake.

And*p he went up from thence unto Beth–el: and as he was going up by the way, there came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head; go up, thou bald head.
And*p he turned back, and looked on them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord.*s And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them.
And*p he went from thence to mount Carmel, and from thence he returned to Samaria.
2 Kings 3
Now*p Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned twelve years.
And*p he wrought evil in the sight of the Lord;*s but not like his father, and like his mother: for he put away the image of Baal that his father had made.
Nevertheless*p he cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom.
And*p Mesha king of Moab was a sheepmaster, and rendered unto the king of Israel an hundred thousand lambs, and an hundred thousand rams, with the wool.
But*p it came to pass, when Ahab was dead, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
And*p king Jehoram went out of Samaria the same time, and numbered all Israel.

And*p he went and sent to Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, saying, The king of Moab hath rebelled against me: wilt thou go with me against Moab to battle? And he said, I will go up: I am as thou art, my people as thy people, and my horses as thy horses.
And*p he said, Which way shall we go up? And he answered, The way through the wilderness of Edom.

So*p the king of Israel went, and the king of Judah, and the king of Edom: and they fetched a compass of seven days' journey: and there was no water for the host, and for the cattle that followed them.
And*p the king of Israel said, Alas! that the Lord*s hath called these three kings together, to deliver them into the hand of Moab!

But*p Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord,*s that we may enquire of the Lord*s by him? And one of the king of Israel's servants answered and said, Here is Elisha the son of Shaphat, which poured water on the hands of Elijah.
And*p Jehoshaphat said, The word of the Lord*s is with him. So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

And*p Elisha said unto the king of Israel, What have I to do with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother. And the king of Israel said unto him, Nay: for the Lord*s hath called these three kings together, to deliver them into the hand of Moab.
And*p Elisha said, As the Lord*s of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, surely, were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward thee, nor see thee.
But*p now bring me a minstrel. And it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the Lord*s came upon him.
And*p he said, Thus saith the Lord,*s Make this valley full of ditches.
For*p thus saith the Lord,*s Ye shall not see wind, neither shall ye see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, that ye may drink, both ye, and your cattle, and your beasts.
And*p this is but a light thing in the sight of the Lord:*s he will deliver the Moabites also into your hand.
And*p ye shall smite every fenced city, and every choice city, and shall fell every good tree, and stop all wells of water, and mar every good piece of land with stones.
And*p it came to pass in the morning, when the meat offering was offered, that, behold, there came water by the way of Edom, and the country was filled with water.
And*p when all the Moabites heard that the kings were come up to fight against them, they gathered all that were able to put on armour, and upward, and stood in the border.
And*p they rose up early in the morning, and the sun shone upon the water, and the Moabites saw the water on the other side as red as blood:
And*p they said, This is blood: the kings are surely slain, and they have smitten one another: now therefore, Moab, to the spoil.
And*p when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and smote the Moabites, so that they fled before them: but they went forward smiting the Moabites, even in their country.

And*p they beat down the cities, and on every good piece of land cast every man his stone, and filled it; and they stopped all the wells of water, and felled all the good trees: only in Kir–hareseth left they the stones thereof; howbeit the slingers went about it, and smote it.
And*p when the king of Moab saw that the battle was too sore for him, he took with him seven hundred men that drew swords, to break through even unto the king of Edom: but they could not.

Then*p he took his eldest son that should have reigned in his stead, and offered him for a burnt offering upon the wall. And there was great indignation against Israel: and they departed from him, and returned to their own land.
2 Kings 4

Now*p there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant did fear the Lord:*s and the creditor is come to take unto him my two sons to be bondmen.
And*p Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.
Then*p he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.
And*p when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.
So*p she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out.
And*p it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.
Then*p she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.
And*p it fell on a day, that Elisha passed to Shunem, where was a great woman; and she constrained him to eat bread. And so it was, that as oft as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread.
And*p she said unto her husband, Behold now, I perceive that this is an holy man of God, which passeth by us continually.

Let*p us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.
And*p it fell on a day, that he came thither, and he turned into the chamber, and lay there.
And*p he said to Gehazi his servant, Call this Shunammite. And when he had called her, she stood before him.

And*p he said unto him, Say now unto her, Behold, thou hast been careful for us with all this care; what is to be done for thee? wouldest thou be spoken for to the king, or to the captain of the host? And she answered, I dwell among mine own people.
And*p he said, What then is to be done for her? And Gehazi answered, Verily she hath no child, and her husband is old.
And*p he said, Call her. And when he had called her, she stood in the door.
And*p he said, About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son. And she said, Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid.
And*p the woman conceived, and bare a son at that season that Elisha had said unto her, according to the time of life.
And*p when the child was grown, it fell on a day, that he went out to his father to the reapers.
And*p he said unto his father, My head, my head. And he said to a lad, Carry him to his mother.
And*p when he had taken him, and brought him to his mother, he sat on her knees till noon, and then died.
And*p she went up, and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door upon him, and went out.
And*p she called unto her husband, and said, Send me, I pray thee, one of the young men, and one of the asses, that I may run to the man of God, and come again.
And*p he said, Wherefore wilt thou go to him to day? it is neither new moon, nor sabbath. And she said, It shall be well.
Then*p she saddled an ass, and said to her servant, Drive, and go forward; slack not thy riding for me, except I bid thee.
So*p she went and came unto the man of God to mount Carmel. And it came to pass, when the man of God saw her afar off, that he said to Gehazi his servant, Behold, yonder is that Shunammite:
Run*p now, I pray thee, to meet her, and say unto her, Is it well with thee? is it well with thy husband? is it well with the child? And she answered, It is well.

And*p when she came to the man of God to the hill, she caught him by the feet: but Gehazi came near to thrust her away. And the man of God said, Let her alone; for her soul is vexed within her: and the Lord*s hath hid it from me, and hath not told me.
Then*p she said, Did I desire a son of my lord? did I not say, Do not deceive me?

Then*p he said to Gehazi, Gird up thy loins, and take my staff in thine hand, and go thy way: if thou meet any man, salute him not; and if any salute thee, answer him not again: and lay my staff upon the face of the child.
And*p the mother of the child said, As the Lord*s liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And he arose, and followed her.

And*p Gehazi passed on before them, and laid the staff upon the face of the child; but there was neither voice, nor hearing. Wherefore he went again to meet him, and told him, saying, The child is not awaked.
And*p when Elisha was come into the house, behold, the child was dead, and laid upon his bed.
He*p went in therefore, and shut the door upon them twain, and prayed unto the Lord.*s

And*p he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands: and he stretched himself upon the child; and the flesh of the child waxed warm.
Then*p he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
And*p he called Gehazi, and said, Call this Shunammite. So he called her. And when she was come in unto him, he said, Take up thy son.
Then*p she went in, and fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground, and took up her son, and went out.

And*p Elisha came again to Gilgal: and there was a dearth in the land; and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him: and he said unto his servant, Set on the great pot, and seethe pottage for the sons of the prophets.
And*p one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered thereof wild gourds his lap full, and came and shred them into the pot of pottage: for they knew them not.

So*p they poured out for the men to eat. And it came to pass, as they were eating of the pottage, that they cried out, and said, O thou man of God, there is death in the pot. And they could not eat thereof.
But*p he said, Then bring meal. And he cast it into the pot; and he said, Pour out for the people, that they may eat. And there was no harm in the pot.

And*p there came a man from Baal–shalishah, and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in the husk thereof. And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat.
And*p his servitor said, What, should I set this before an hundred men? He said again, Give the people, that they may eat: for thus saith the Lord,*s They shall eat, and shall leave thereof.
So*p he set it before them, and they did eat, and left thereof, according to the word of the Lord.*s
2 Kings 5

Now*p Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the Lord*s had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper.
And*p the Syrians had gone out by companies, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid; and she waited on Naaman's wife.
And*p she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.
And*p one went in, and told his lord, saying, Thus and thus said the maid that is of the land of Israel.

And*p the king of Syria said, Go to, go, and I will send a letter unto the king of Israel. And he departed, and took with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment.

And*p he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, Now when this letter is come unto thee, behold, I have therewith sent Naaman my servant to thee, that thou mayest recover him of his leprosy.

And*p it came to pass, when the king of Israel had read the letter, that he rent his clothes, and said, Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy? wherefore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarrel against me.

And*p it was so, when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.
So*p Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.
And*p Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

But*p Naaman was wroth, and went away, and said, Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the Lord*s his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper.
Are*p not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.

And*p his servants came near, and spake unto him, and said, My father, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean?
Then*p went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

And*p he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.
But*p he said, As the Lord*s liveth, before whom I stand, I will receive none. And he urged him to take it; but he refused.

And*p Naaman said, Shall there not then, I pray thee, be given to thy servant two mules' burden of earth? for thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, but unto the Lord.*s

In*p this thing the Lord*s pardon thy servant, that when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the Lord*s pardon thy servant in this thing.
And*p he said unto him, Go in peace. So he departed from him a little way.

But*p Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, Behold, my master hath spared Naaman this Syrian, in not receiving at his hands that which he brought: but, as the Lord*s liveth, I will run after him, and take somewhat of him.
So*p Gehazi followed after Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running after him, he lighted down from the chariot to meet him, and said, Is all well?

And*p he said, All is well. My master hath sent me, saying, Behold, even now there be come to me from mount Ephraim two young men of the sons of the prophets: give them, I pray thee, a talent of silver, and two changes of garments.

And*p Naaman said, Be content, take two talents. And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and laid them upon two of his servants; and they bare them before him.
And*p when he came to the tower, he took them from their hand, and bestowed them in the house: and he let the men go, and they departed.
But*p he went in, and stood before his master. And Elisha said unto him, Whence comest thou, Gehazi? And he said, Thy servant went no whither.

And*p he said unto him, Went not mine heart with thee, when the man turned again from his chariot to meet thee? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants?
The*p leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence a leper as white as snow.
2 Kings 6
And*p the sons of the prophets said unto Elisha, Behold now, the place where we dwell with thee is too strait for us.
Let*p us go, we pray thee, unto Jordan, and take thence every man a beam, and let us make us a place there, where we may dwell. And he answered, Go ye.
And*p one said, Be content, I pray thee, and go with thy servants. And he answered, I will go.
So*p he went with them. And when they came to Jordan, they cut down wood.
But*p as one was felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water: and he cried, and said, Alas, master! for it was borrowed.
And*p the man of God said, Where fell it? And he shewed him the place. And he cut down a stick, and cast it in thither; and the iron did swim.
Therefore*p said he, Take it up to thee. And he put out his hand, and took it.
Then*p the king of Syria warred against Israel, and took counsel with his servants, saying, In such and such a place shall be my camp.
And*p the man of God sent unto the king of Israel, saying, Beware that thou pass not such a place; for thither the Syrians are come down.
And*p the king of Israel sent to the place which the man of God told him and warned him of, and saved himself there, not once nor twice.
Therefore*p the heart of the king of Syria was sore troubled for this thing; and he called his servants, and said unto them, Will ye not shew me which of us is for the king of Israel?
And*p one of his servants said, None, my lord, O king: but Elisha, the prophet that is in Israel, telleth the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy bedchamber.
And*p he said, Go and spy where he is, that I may send and fetch him. And it was told him, saying, Behold, he is in Dothan.
Therefore*p sent he thither horses, and chariots, and a great host: and they came by night, and compassed the city about.

And*p when the servant of the man of God was risen early, and gone forth, behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do?
And*p he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.

And*p Elisha prayed, and said, Lord,*s I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord*s opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.
And*p when they came down to him, Elisha prayed unto the Lord,*s and said, Smite this people, I pray thee, with blindness. And he smote them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
And*p Elisha said unto them, This is not the way, neither is this the city: follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom ye seek. But he led them to Samaria.

And*p it came to pass, when they were come into Samaria, that Elisha said, Lord,*s open the eyes of these men, that they may see. And the Lord*s opened their eyes, and they saw; and, behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.
And*p the king of Israel said unto Elisha, when he saw them, My father, shall I smite them? shall I smite them?

And*p he answered, Thou shalt not smite them: wouldest thou smite those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow? set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.
And*p he prepared great provision for them: and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. So the bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel.
And*p it came to pass after this, that Ben–hadad king of Syria gathered all his host, and went up, and besieged Samaria.

And*p there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass's head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.
And*p as the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall, there cried a woman unto him, saying, Help, my lord, O king.
And*p he said, If the Lord*s do not help thee, whence shall I help thee? out of the barnfloor, or out of the winepress?
And*p the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, This woman said unto me, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son to morrow.
So*p we boiled my son, and did eat him: and I said unto her on the next day, Give thy son, that we may eat him: and she hath hid her son.

And*p it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the woman, that he rent his clothes; and he passed by upon the wall, and the people looked, and, behold, he had sackcloth within upon his flesh.
Then*p he said, God do so and more also to me, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat shall stand on him this day.

But*p Elisha sat in his house, and the elders sat with him; and the king sent a man from before him: but ere the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, See ye how this son of a murderer hath sent to take away mine head? look, when the messenger cometh, shut the door, and hold him fast at the door: is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?
And*p while he yet talked with them, behold, the messenger came down unto him: and he said, Behold, this evil is of the Lord;*s what should I wait for the Lord*s any longer?
2 Kings 7

Then*p Elisha said, Hear ye the word of the Lord;*s Thus saith the Lord,*s To morrow about this time shall a measure of fine flour be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.

Then*p a lord on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God, and said, Behold, if the Lord*s would make windows in heaven, might this thing be? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.
And*p there were four leprous men at the entering in of the gate: and they said one to another, Why sit we here until we die?

If*p we say, We will enter into the city, then the famine is in the city, and we shall die there: and if we sit still here, we die also. Now therefore come, and let us fall unto the host of the Syrians: if they save us alive, we shall live; and if they kill us, we shall but die.
And*p they rose up in the twilight, to go unto the camp of the Syrians: and when they were come to the uttermost part of the camp of Syria, behold, there was no man there.

For*p the Lord had made the host of the Syrians to hear a noise of chariots, and a noise of horses, even the noise of a great host: and they said one to another, Lo, the king of Israel hath hired against us the kings of the Hittites, and the kings of the Egyptians, to come upon us.
Wherefore*p they arose and fled in the twilight, and left their tents, and their horses, and their asses, even the camp as it was, and fled for their life.

And*p when these lepers came to the uttermost part of the camp, they went into one tent, and did eat and drink, and carried thence silver, and gold, and raiment, and went and hid it; and came again, and entered into another tent, and carried thence also, and went and hid it.

Then*p they said one to another, We do not well: this day is a day of good tidings, and we hold our peace: if we tarry till the morning light, some mischief will come upon us: now therefore come, that we may go and tell the king's household.

So*p they came and called unto the porter of the city: and they told them, saying, We came to the camp of the Syrians, and, behold, there was no man there, neither voice of man, but horses tied, and asses tied, and the tents as they were.
And*p he called the porters; and they told it to the king's house within.

And*p the king arose in the night, and said unto his servants, I will now shew you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we be hungry; therefore are they gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, When they come out of the city, we shall catch them alive, and get into the city.

And*p one of his servants answered and said, Let some take, I pray thee, five of the horses that remain, which are left in the city, (behold, they are as all the multitude of Israel that are left in it: behold, I say, they are even as all the multitude of the Israelites that are consumed:) and let us send and see.
They*p took therefore two chariot horses; and the king sent after the host of the Syrians, saying, Go and see.
And*p they went after them unto Jordan: and, lo, all the way was full of garments and vessels, which the Syrians had cast away in their haste. And the messengers returned, and told the king.
And*p the people went out, and spoiled the tents of the Syrians. So a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the Lord.*s

And*p the king appointed the lord on whose hand he leaned to have the charge of the gate: and the people trode upon him in the gate, and he died, as the man of God had said, who spake when the king came down to him.

And*p it came to pass as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, Two measures of barley for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, shall be to morrow about this time in the gate of Samaria:

And*p that lord answered the man of God, and said, Now, behold, if the Lord*s should make windows in heaven, might such a thing be? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.
And*p so it fell out unto him: for the people trode upon him in the gate, and he died.
2 Kings 8

Then*p spake Elisha unto the woman, whose son he had restored to life, saying, Arise, and go thou and thine household, and sojourn wheresoever thou canst sojourn: for the Lord*s hath called for a famine; and it shall also come upon the land seven years.
And*p the woman arose, and did after the saying of the man of God: and she went with her household, and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.
And*p it came to pass at the seven years' end, that the woman returned out of the land of the Philistines: and she went forth to cry unto the king for her house and for her land.
And*p the king talked with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, Tell me, I pray thee, all the great things that Elisha hath done.

And*p it came to pass, as he was telling the king how he had restored a dead body to life, that, behold, the woman, whose son he had restored to life, cried to the king for her house and for her land. And Gehazi said, My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.

And*p when the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed unto her a certain officer, saying, Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.
And*p Elisha came to Damascus; and Ben–hadad the king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, The man of God is come hither.
And*p the king said unto Hazael, Take a present in thine hand, and go, meet the man of God, and enquire of the Lord*s by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?

So*p Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels' burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Ben–hadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
And*p Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the Lord*s hath shewed me that he shall surely die.
And*p he settled his countenance stedfastly, until he was ashamed: and the man of God wept.

And*p Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.
And*p Hazael said, But what, is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha answered, The Lord*s hath shewed me that thou shalt be king over Syria.
So*p he departed from Elisha, and came to his master; who said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he answered, He told me that thou shouldest surely recover.
And*p it came to pass on the morrow, that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.
And*p in the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign.
Thirty*p and two years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
And*p he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.*s
Yet*p the Lord*s would not destroy Judah for David his servant's sake, as he promised him to give him alway a light, and to his children.
In*p his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.

So*p Joram went over to Zair, and all the chariots with him: and he rose by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him about, and the captains of the chariots: and the people fled into their tents.
Yet*p Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. Then Libnah revolted at the same time.
And*p the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And*p Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.
In*p the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel did Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah begin to reign.
Two*p and twenty years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
And*p he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord,*s as did the house of Ahab: for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab.
And*p he went with Joram the son of Ahab to the war against Hazael king of Syria in Ramoth–gilead; and the Syrians wounded Joram.

And*p king Joram went back to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.
2 Kings 9
And*p Elisha the prophet called one of the children of the prophets, and said unto him, Gird up thy loins, and take this box of oil in thine hand, and go to Ramoth–gilead:
And*p when thou comest thither, look out there Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and go in, and make him arise up from among his brethren, and carry him to an inner chamber;
Then*p take the box of oil, and pour it on his head, and say, Thus saith the Lord,*s I have anointed thee king over Israel. Then open the door, and flee, and tarry not.
So*p the young man, even the young man the prophet, went to Ramoth–gilead.
And*p when he came, behold, the captains of the host were sitting; and he said, I have an errand to thee, O captain. And Jehu said, Unto which of all us? And he said, To thee, O captain.

And*p he arose, and went into the house; and he poured the oil on his head, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord*s God of Israel, I have anointed thee king over the people of the Lord,*s even over Israel.
And*p thou shalt smite the house of Ahab thy master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the Lord,*s at the hand of Jezebel.
For*p the whole house of Ahab shall perish: and I will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel:
And*p I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah:
And*p the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there shall be none to bury her. And he opened the door, and fled.
Then*p Jehu came forth to the servants of his lord: and one said unto him, Is all well? wherefore came this mad fellow to thee? And he said unto them, Ye know the man, and his communication.
And*p they said, It is false; tell us now. And he said, Thus and thus spake he to me, saying, Thus saith the Lord,*s I have anointed thee king over Israel.
Then*p they hasted, and took every man his garment, and put it under him on the top of the stairs, and blew with trumpets, saying, Jehu is king.
So*p Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. (Now Joram had kept Ramoth–gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Syria.

But*p king Joram was returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians had given him, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria.) And Jehu said, If it be your minds, then let none go forth nor escape out of the city to go to tell it in Jezreel.
So*p Jehu rode in a chariot, and went to Jezreel; for Joram lay there. And Ahaziah king of Judah was come down to see Joram.

And*p there stood a watchman on the tower in Jezreel, and he spied the company of Jehu as he came, and said, I see a company. And Joram said, Take an horseman, and send to meet them, and let him say, Is it peace?

So*p there went one on horseback to meet him, and said, Thus saith the king, Is it peace? And Jehu said, What hast thou to do with peace? turn thee behind me. And the watchman told, saying, The messenger came to them, but he cometh not again.
Then*p he sent out a second on horseback, which came to them, and said, Thus saith the king, Is it peace? And Jehu answered, What hast thou to do with peace? turn thee behind me.
And*p the watchman told, saying, He came even unto them, and cometh not again: and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi; for he driveth furiously.

And*p Joram said, Make ready. And his chariot was made ready. And Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, and they went out against Jehu, and met him in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite.
And*p it came to pass, when Joram saw Jehu, that he said, Is it peace, Jehu? And he answered, What peace, so long as the whoredoms of thy mother Jezebel and her witchcrafts are so many?
And*p Joram turned his hands, and fled, and said to Ahaziah, There is treachery, O Ahaziah.
And*p Jehu drew a bow with his full strength, and smote Jehoram between his arms, and the arrow went out at his heart, and he sunk down in his chariot.

Then*p said Jehu to Bidkar his captain, Take up, and cast him in the portion of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite: for remember how that, when I and thou rode together after Ahab his father, the Lord*s laid this burden upon him;

Surely*p I have seen yesterday the blood of Naboth, and the blood of his sons, saith the Lord;*s and I will requite thee in this plat, saith the Lord.*s Now therefore take and cast him into the plat of ground, according to the word of the Lord.*s

But*p when Ahaziah the king of Judah saw this, he fled by the way of the garden house. And Jehu followed after him, and said, Smite him also in the chariot. And they did so at the going up to Gur, which is by Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo, and died there.
And*p his servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and buried him in his sepulchre with his fathers in the city of David.
And*p in the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab began Ahaziah to reign over Judah.
And*p when Jehu was come to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it; and she painted her face, and tired her head, and looked out at a window.
And*p as Jehu entered in at the gate, she said, Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
And*p he lifted up his face to the window, and said, Who is on my side? who? And there looked out to him two or three eunuchs.
And*p he said, Throw her down. So they threw her down: and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses: and he trode her under foot.
And*p when he was come in, he did eat and drink, and said, Go, see now this cursed woman, and bury her: for she is a king's daughter.
And*p they went to bury her: but they found no more of her than the skull, and the feet, and the palms of her hands.

Wherefore*p they came again, and told him. And he said, This is the word of the Lord,*s which he spake by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel:
And*p the carcase of Jezebel shall be as dung upon the face of the field in the portion of Jezreel; so that they shall not say, This is Jezebel.
2 Kings 10
And*p Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters, and sent to Samaria, unto the rulers of Jezreel, to the elders, and to them that brought up Ahab's children, saying,
Now*p as soon as this letter cometh to you, seeing your master's sons are with you, and there are with you chariots and horses, a fenced city also, and armour;
Look*p even out the best and meetest of your master's sons, and set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house.
But*p they were exceedingly afraid, and said, Behold, two kings stood not before him: how then shall we stand?

And*p he that was over the house, and he that was over the city, the elders also, and the bringers up of the children, sent to Jehu, saying, We are thy servants, and will do all that thou shalt bid us; we will not make any king: do thou that which is good in thine eyes.

Then*p he wrote a letter the second time to them, saying, If ye be mine, and if ye will hearken unto my voice, take ye the heads of the men your master's sons, and come to me to Jezreel by to morrow this time. Now the king's sons, being seventy persons, were with the great men of the city, which brought them up.
And*p it came to pass, when the letter came to them, that they took the king's sons, and slew seventy persons, and put their heads in baskets, and sent him them to Jezreel.
And*p there came a messenger, and told him, saying, They have brought the heads of the king's sons. And he said, Lay ye them in two heaps at the entering in of the gate until the morning.
And*p it came to pass in the morning, that he went out, and stood, and said to all the people, Ye be righteous: behold, I conspired against my master, and slew him: but who slew all these?

Know*p now that there shall fall unto the earth nothing of the word of the Lord,*s which the Lord*s spake concerning the house of Ahab: for the Lord*s hath done that which he spake by his servant Elijah.
So*p Jehu slew all that remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, and his kinsfolks, and his priests, until he left him none remaining.
And*p he arose and departed, and came to Samaria. And as he was at the shearing house in the way,

Jehu*p met with the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah, and said, Who are ye? And they answered, We are the brethren of Ahaziah; and we go down to salute the children of the king and the children of the queen.
And*p he said, Take them alive. And they took them alive, and slew them at the pit of the shearing house, even two and forty men; neither left he any of them.

And*p when he was departed thence, he lighted on Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him: and he saluted him, and said to him, Is thine heart right, as my heart is with thy heart? And Jehonadab answered, It is. If it be, give me thine hand. And he gave him his hand; and he took him up to him into the chariot.
And*p he said, Come with me, and see my zeal for the Lord.*s So they made him ride in his chariot.
And*p when he came to Samaria, he slew all that remained unto Ahab in Samaria, till he had destroyed him, according to the saying of the Lord,*s which he spake to Elijah.
And*p Jehu gathered all the people together, and said unto them, Ahab served Baal a little; but Jehu shall serve him much.

Now*p therefore call unto me all the prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests; let none be wanting: for I have a great sacrifice to do to Baal; whosoever shall be wanting, he shall not live. But Jehu did it in subtilty, to the intent that he might destroy the worshippers of Baal.
And*p Jehu said, Proclaim a solemn assembly for Baal. And they proclaimed it.

And*p Jehu sent through all Israel: and all the worshippers of Baal came, so that there was not a man left that came not. And they came into the house of Baal; and the house of Baal was full from one end to another.
And*p he said unto him that was over the vestry, Bring forth vestments for all the worshippers of Baal. And he brought them forth vestments.

And*p Jehu went, and Jehonadab the son of Rechab, into the house of Baal, and said unto the worshippers of Baal, Search, and look that there be here with you none of the servants of the Lord,*s but the worshippers of Baal only.

And*p when they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings, Jehu appointed fourscore men without, and said, If any of the men whom I have brought into your hands escape, he that letteth him go, his life shall be for the life of him.

And*p it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the guard and to the captains, Go in, and slay them; let none come forth. And they smote them with the edge of the sword; and the guard and the captains cast them out, and went to the city of the house of Baal.
And*p they brought forth the images out of the house of Baal, and burned them.
And*p they brake down the image of Baal, and brake down the house of Baal, and made it a draught house unto this day.
Thus*p Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
Howbeit*p from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, Jehu departed not from after them, to wit, the golden calves that were in Beth–el, and that were in Dan.

And*p the Lord*s said unto Jehu, Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that was in mine heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.
But*p Jehu took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord*s God of Israel with all his heart: for he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, which made Israel to sin.
In*p those days the Lord*s began to cut Israel short: and Hazael smote them in all the coasts of Israel;
From*p Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.
Now*p the rest of the acts of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And*p Jehu slept with his fathers: and they buried him in Samaria. And Jehoahaz his son reigned in his stead.
And*p the time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty and eight years.
2 Kings 11
And*p when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal.

But*p Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons which were slain; and they hid him, even him and his nurse, in the bedchamber from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.
And*p he was with her hid in the house of the Lord*s six years. And Athaliah did reign over the land.

And*p the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the rulers over hundreds, with the captains and the guard, and brought them to him into the house of the Lord,*s and made a covenant with them, and took an oath of them in the house of the Lord,*s and shewed them the king's son.
And*p he commanded them, saying, This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you that enter in on the sabbath shall even be keepers of the watch of the king's house;
And*p a third part shall be at the gate of Sur; and a third part at the gate behind the guard: so shall ye keep the watch of the house, that it be not broken down.
And*p two parts of all you that go forth on the sabbath, even they shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord*s about the king.

And*p ye shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand: and he that cometh within the ranges, let him be slain: and be ye with the king as he goeth out and as he cometh in.

And*p the captains over the hundreds did according to all things that Jehoiada the priest commanded: and they took every man his men that were to come in on the sabbath, with them that should go out on the sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
And*p to the captains over hundreds did the priest give king David's spears and shields, that were in the temple of the Lord.*s
And*p the guard stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, round about the king, from the right corner of the temple to the left corner of the temple, along by the altar and the temple.
And*p he brought forth the king's son, and put the crown upon him, and gave him the testimony; and they made him king, and anointed him; and they clapped their hands, and said, God save the king.
And*p when Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and of the people, she came to the people into the temple of the Lord.*s

And*p when she looked, behold, the king stood by a pillar, as the manner was, and the princes and the trumpeters by the king, and all the people of the land rejoiced, and blew with trumpets: and Athaliah rent her clothes, and cried, Treason, Treason.

But*p Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of the hundreds, the officers of the host, and said unto them, Have her forth without the ranges: and him that followeth her kill with the sword. For the priest had said, Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord.*s
And*p they laid hands on her; and she went by the way by the which the horses came into the king's house: and there was she slain.
And*p Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord*s and the king and the people, that they should be the Lord's*s people; between the king also and the people.

And*p all the people of the land went into the house of Baal, and brake it down; his altars and his images brake they in pieces thoroughly, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. And the priest appointed officers over the house of the Lord.*s

And*p he took the rulers over hundreds, and the captains, and the guard, and all the people of the land; and they brought down the king from the house of the Lord,*s and came by the way of the gate of the guard to the king's house. And he sat on the throne of the kings.
And*p all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was in quiet: and they slew Athaliah with the sword beside the king's house.
Seven*p years old was Jehoash when he began to reign.
2 Kings 12
In*p the seventh year of Jehu Jehoash began to reign; and forty years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Zibiah of Beer–sheba.
And*p Jehoash did that which was right in the sight of the Lord*s all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
But*p the high places were not taken away: the people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.

And*p Jehoash said to the priests, All the money of the dedicated things that is brought into the house of the Lord,*s even the money of every one that passeth the account, the money that every man is set at, and all the money that cometh into any man's heart to bring into the house of the Lord,*s
Let*p the priests take it to them, every man of his acquaintance: and let them repair the breaches of the house, wheresoever any breach shall be found.
But*p it was so, that in the three and twentieth year of king Jehoash the priests had not repaired the breaches of the house.

Then*p king Jehoash called for Jehoiada the priest, and the other priests, and said unto them, Why repair ye not the breaches of the house? now therefore receive no more money of your acquaintance, but deliver it for the breaches of the house.
And*p the priests consented to receive no more money of the people, neither to repair the breaches of the house.

But*p Jehoiada the priest took a chest, and bored a hole in the lid of it, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one cometh into the house of the Lord:*s and the priests that kept the door put therein all the money that was brought into the house of the Lord.*s

And*p it was so, when they saw that there was much money in the chest, that the king's scribe and the high priest came up, and they put up in bags, and told the money that was found in the house of the Lord.*s

And*p they gave the money, being told, into the hands of them that did the work, that had the oversight of the house of the Lord:*s and they laid it out to the carpenters and builders, that wrought upon the house of the Lord,*s
And*p to masons, and hewers of stone, and to buy timber and hewed stone to repair the breaches of the house of the Lord,*s and for all that was laid out for the house to repair it.

Howbeit*p there were not made for the house of the Lord*s bowls of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, any vessels of gold, or vessels of silver, of the money that was brought into the house of the Lord:*s
But*p they gave that to the workmen, and repaired therewith the house of the Lord.*s
Moreover*p they reckoned not with the men, into whose hand they delivered the money to be bestowed on workmen: for they dealt faithfully.
The*p trespass money and sin money was not brought into the house of the Lord:*s it was the priests'.
Then*p Hazael king of Syria went up, and fought against Gath, and took it: and Hazael set his face to go up to Jerusalem.
