Make*p ye mention to the nations; behold, publish against Jerusalem, that watchers come from a far country, and give out their voice against the cities of Judah.
As*p keepers of a field, are they against her round about; because she hath been rebellious against me, saith the Lord.*s
Thy*p way and thy doings have procured these things unto thee; this is thy wickedness, because it is bitter, because it reacheth unto thine heart.
My*p bowels, my bowels! I am pained at my very heart; my heart maketh a noise in me; I cannot hold my peace, because thou hast heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
Destruction*p upon destruction is cried; for the whole land is spoiled: suddenly are my tents spoiled, and my curtains in a moment.
How*p long shall I see the standard, and hear the sound of the trumpet?
For*p my people is foolish, they have not known me; they are sottish children, and they have none understanding: they are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge.
I*p beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light.
I*p beheld the mountains, and, lo, they trembled, and all the hills moved lightly.
I*p beheld, and, lo, there was no man, and all the birds of the heavens were fled.
I*p beheld, and, lo, the fruitful place was a wilderness, and all the cities thereof were broken down at the presence of the Lord,*s and by his fierce anger.
For*p thus hath the Lord*s said, The whole land shall be desolate; yet will I not make a full end.
For*p this shall the earth mourn, and the heavens above be black: because I have spoken it, I have purposed it, and will not repent, neither will I turn back from it.
The*p whole city shall flee for the noise of the horsemen and bowmen; they shall go into thickets, and climb up upon the rocks: every city shall be forsaken, and not a man dwell therein.

And*p when thou art spoiled, what wilt thou do? Though thou clothest thyself with crimson, though thou deckest thee with ornaments of gold, though thou rentest thy face with painting, in vain shalt thou make thyself fair; thy lovers will despise thee, they will seek thy life.

For*p I have heard a voice as of a woman in travail, and the anguish as of her that bringeth forth her first child, the voice of the daughter of Zion, that bewaileth herself, that spreadeth her hands, saying, Woe is me now! for my soul is wearied because of murderers.
Jeremiah 5

Run*p ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be any that executeth judgment, that seeketh the truth; and I will pardon it.
And*p though they say, The Lord*s liveth; surely they swear falsely.

O*p Lord,*s are not thine eyes upon the truth? thou hast stricken them, but they have not grieved; thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction: they have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return.
Therefore*p I said, Surely these are poor; they are foolish: for they know not the way of the Lord,*s nor the judgment of their God.
I*p will get me unto the great men, and will speak unto them; for they have known the way of the Lord,*s and the judgment of their God: but these have altogether broken the yoke, and burst the bonds.

Wherefore*p a lion out of the forest shall slay them, and a wolf of the evenings shall spoil them, a leopard shall watch over their cities: every one that goeth out thence shall be torn in pieces: because their transgressions are many, and their backslidings are increased.

How*p shall I pardon thee for this? thy children have forsaken me, and sworn by them that are no gods: when I had fed them to the full, they then committed adultery, and assembled themselves by troops in the harlots' houses.
They*p were as fed horses in the morning: every one neighed after his neighbour's wife.
Shall*p I not visit for these things? saith the Lord:*s and shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
Go*p ye up upon her walls, and destroy; but make not a full end: take away her battlements; for they are not the Lord's.*s
For*p the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me, saith the Lord.*s
They*p have belied the Lord,*s and said, It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine:
And*p the prophets shall become wind, and the word is not in them: thus shall it be done unto them.
Wherefore*p thus saith the Lord*s God of hosts, Because ye speak this word, behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.

Lo,*p I will bring a nation upon you from far, O house of Israel, saith the Lord:*s it is a mighty nation, it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language thou knowest not, neither understandest what they say.
Their*p quiver is as an open sepulchre, they are all mighty men.

And*p they shall eat up thine harvest, and thy bread, which thy sons and thy daughters should eat: they shall eat up thy flocks and thine herds: they shall eat up thy vines and thy fig trees: they shall impoverish thy fenced cities, wherein thou trustedst, with the sword.
Nevertheless*p in those days, saith the Lord,*s I will not make a full end with you.

And*p it shall come to pass, when ye shall say, Wherefore doeth the Lord*s our God all these things unto us? then shalt thou answer them, Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.
Declare*p this in the house of Jacob, and publish it in Judah, saying,
Hear*p now this, O foolish people, and without understanding; which have eyes, and see not; which have ears, and hear not:

Fear*p ye not me? saith the Lord:*s will ye not tremble at my presence, which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it: and though the waves thereof toss themselves, yet can they not prevail; though they roar, yet can they not pass over it?
But*p this people hath a revolting and a rebellious heart; they are revolted and gone.
Neither*p say they in their heart, Let us now fear the Lord*s our God, that giveth rain, both the former and the latter, in his season: he reserveth unto us the appointed weeks of the harvest.
Your*p iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withholden good things from you.
For*p among my people are found wicked men: they lay wait, as he that setteth snares; they set a trap, they catch men.
As*p a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit: therefore they are become great, and waxen rich.
They*p are waxen fat, they shine: yea, they overpass the deeds of the wicked: they judge not the cause, the cause of the fatherless, yet they prosper; and the right of the needy do they not judge.
Shall*p I not visit for these things? saith the Lord:*s shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
A*p wonderful and horrible thing is committed in the land;
The*p prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests bear rule by their means; and my people love to have it so: and what will ye do in the end thereof?
Jeremiah 6

O*p ye children of Benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in Beth–haccerem: for evil appeareth out of the north, and great destruction.
I*p have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.
The*p shepherds with their flocks shall come unto her; they shall pitch their tents against her round about; they shall feed every one in his place.
Prepare*p ye war against her; arise, and let us go up at noon. Woe unto us! for the day goeth away, for the shadows of the evening are stretched out.
Arise,*p and let us go by night, and let us destroy her palaces.
For*p thus hath the Lord*s of hosts said, Hew ye down trees, and cast a mount against Jerusalem: this is the city to be visited; she is wholly oppression in the midst of her.
As*p a fountain casteth out her waters, so she casteth out her wickedness: violence and spoil is heard in her; before me continually is grief and wounds.
Be*p thou instructed, O Jerusalem, lest my soul depart from thee; lest I make thee desolate, a land not inhabited.
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, They shall thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel as a vine: turn back thine hand as a grapegatherer into the baskets.

To*p whom shall I speak, and give warning, that they may hear? behold, their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken: behold, the word of the Lord*s is unto them a reproach; they have no delight in it.

Therefore*p I am full of the fury of the Lord;*s I am weary with holding in: I will pour it out upon the children abroad, and upon the assembly of young men together: for even the husband with the wife shall be taken, the aged with him that is full of days.
And*p their houses shall be turned unto others, with their fields and wives together: for I will stretch out my hand upon the inhabitants of the land, saith the Lord.*s
For*p from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely.
They*p have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace.

Were*p they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore they shall fall among them that fall: at the time that I visit them they shall be cast down, saith the Lord.*s

Thus*p saith the Lord,*s Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.
Also*p I set watchmen over you, saying, Hearken to the sound of the trumpet. But they said, We will not hearken.
Therefore*p hear, ye nations, and know, O congregation, what is among them.
Hear,*p O earth: behold, I will bring evil upon this people, even the fruit of their thoughts, because they have not hearkened unto my words, nor to my law, but rejected it.
To*p what purpose cometh there to me incense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country? your burnt offerings are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices sweet unto me.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord,*s Behold, I will lay stumblingblocks before this people, and the fathers and the sons together shall fall upon them; the neighbour and his friend shall perish.
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s Behold, a people cometh from the north country, and a great nation shall be raised from the sides of the earth.
They*p shall lay hold on bow and spear; they are cruel, and have no mercy; their voice roareth like the sea; and they ride upon horses, set in array as men for war against thee, O daughter of Zion.
We*p have heard the fame thereof: our hands wax feeble: anguish hath taken hold of us, and pain, as of a woman in travail.
Go*p not forth into the field, nor walk by the way; for the sword of the enemy and fear is on every side.
O*p daughter of my people, gird thee with sackcloth, and wallow thyself in ashes: make thee mourning, as for an only son, most bitter lamentation: for the spoiler shall suddenly come upon us.
I*p have set thee for a tower and a fortress among my people, that thou mayest know and try their way.
They*p are all grievous revolters, walking with slanders: they are brass and iron; they are all corrupters.
The*p bellows are burned, the lead is consumed of the fire; the founder melteth in vain: for the wicked are not plucked away.

Jeremiah 7
The*p word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord,*s saying,
Stand*p in the gate of the Lord's*s house, and proclaim there this word, and say, Hear the word of the Lord,*s all ye of Judah, that enter in at these gates to worship the Lord.*s
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel, Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place.
Trust*p ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of the Lord,*s The temple of the Lord,*s The temple of the Lord,*s are these.
For*p if ye thoroughly amend your ways and your doings; if ye thoroughly execute judgment between a man and his neighbour;
If*p ye oppress not the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, and shed not innocent blood in this place, neither walk after other gods to your hurt:
Then*p will I cause you to dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers, for ever and ever.
Behold,*p ye trust in lying words, that cannot profit.
Will*p ye steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not;
And*p come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, We are delivered to do all these abominations?
Is*p this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the Lord.*s
But*p go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.
And*p now, because ye have done all these works, saith the Lord,*s and I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not;
Therefore*p will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh.
And*p I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.
Therefore*p pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear thee.
Seest*p thou not what they do in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

The*p children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto other gods, that they may provoke me to anger.
Do*p they provoke me to anger? saith the Lord:*s do they not provoke themselves to the confusion of their own faces?

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, mine anger and my fury shall be poured out upon this place, upon man, and upon beast, and upon the trees of the field, and upon the fruit of the ground; and it shall burn, and shall not be quenched.
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh.
For*p I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices:
But*p this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.
But*p they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear, but walked in the counsels and in the imagination of their evil heart, and went backward, and not forward.
Since*p the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them:
Yet*p they hearkened not unto me, nor inclined their ear, but hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers.
Therefore*p thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee.
But*p thou shalt say unto them, This is a nation that obeyeth not the voice of the Lord*s their God, nor receiveth correction: truth is perished, and is cut off from their mouth.

And*p they have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.

Therefore,*p behold, the days come, saith the Lord,*s that it shall no more be called Topheth, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Topheth, till there be no place.
And*p the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and none shall fray them away.

Then*p will I cause to cease from the cities of Judah, and from the streets of Jerusalem, the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride: for the land shall be desolate.
Jeremiah 8

At*p that time, saith the Lord,*s they shall bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of his princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of their graves:

And*p they shall spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served, and after whom they have walked, and whom they have sought, and whom they have worshipped: they shall not be gathered, nor be buried; they shall be for dung upon the face of the earth.
And*p death shall be chosen rather than life by all the residue of them that remain of this evil family, which remain in all the places whither I have driven them, saith the Lord*s of hosts.
Moreover*p thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord;*s Shall they fall, and not arise? shall he turn away, and not return?
Why*p then is this people of Jerusalem slidden back by a perpetual backsliding? they hold fast deceit, they refuse to return.
I*p hearkened and heard, but they spake not aright: no man repented him of his wickedness, saying, What have I done? every one turned to his course, as the horse rusheth into the battle.
Yea,*p the stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times; and the turtle and the crane and the swallow observe the time of their coming; but my people know not the judgment of the Lord.*s
How*p do ye say, We are wise, and the law of the Lord*s is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain.

Therefore*p will I give their wives unto others, and their fields to them that shall inherit them: for every one from the least even unto the greatest is given to covetousness, from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely.
For*p they have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace.

Were*p they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore shall they fall among them that fall: in the time of their visitation they shall be cast down, saith the Lord.*s

I*p will surely consume them, saith the Lord:*s there shall be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade; and the things that I have given them shall pass away from them.

Why*p do we sit still? assemble yourselves, and let us enter into the defenced cities, and let us be silent there: for the Lord*s our God hath put us to silence, and given us water of gall to drink, because we have sinned against the Lord.*s

The*p snorting of his horses was heard from Dan: the whole land trembled at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones; for they are come, and have devoured the land, and all that is in it; the city, and those that dwell therein.
For,*p behold, I will send serpents, cockatrices, among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall bite you, saith the Lord.*s
When*p I would comfort myself against sorrow, my heart is faint in me.

Behold*p the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people because of them that dwell in a far country: Is not the Lord*s in Zion? is not her king in her? Why have they provoked me to anger with their graven images, and with strange vanities?
The*p harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.
For*p the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt; I am black; astonishment hath taken hold on me.
Is*p there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?
Jeremiah 9
Oh*p that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
Oh*p that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.
And*p they bend their tongues like their bow for lies: but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth; for they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me, saith the Lord.*s
Take*p ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.
And*p they will deceive every one his neighbour, and will not speak the truth: they have taught their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity.
Thine*p habitation is in the midst of deceit; through deceit they refuse to know me, saith the Lord.*s
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, Behold, I will melt them, and try them; for how shall I do for the daughter of my people?
Their*p tongue is as an arrow shot out; it speaketh deceit: one speaketh peaceably to his neighbour with his mouth, but in heart he layeth his wait.
Shall*p I not visit them for these things? saith the Lord:*s shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?

For*p the mountains will I take up a weeping and wailing, and for the habitations of the wilderness a lamentation, because they are burned up, so that none can pass through them; neither can men hear the voice of the cattle; both the fowl of the heavens and the beast are fled; they are gone.
And*p I will make Jerusalem heaps, and a den of dragons; and I will make the cities of Judah desolate, without an inhabitant.

Who*p is the wise man, that may understand this? and who is he to whom the mouth of the Lord*s hath spoken, that he may declare it, for what the land perisheth and is burned up like a wilderness, that none passeth through?
And*p the Lord*s saith, Because they have forsaken my law which I set before them, and have not obeyed my voice, neither walked therein;
But*p have walked after the imagination of their own heart, and after Baalim, which their fathers taught them:
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will feed them, even this people, with wormwood, and give them water of gall to drink.
I*p will scatter them also among the heathen, whom neither they nor their fathers have known: and I will send a sword after them, till I have consumed them.
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, Consider ye, and call for the mourning women, that they may come; and send for cunning women, that they may come:
And*p let them make haste, and take up a wailing for us, that our eyes may run down with tears, and our eyelids gush out with waters.
For*p a voice of wailing is heard out of Zion, How are we spoiled! we are greatly confounded, because we have forsaken the land, because our dwellings have cast us out.
Yet*p hear the word of the Lord,*s O ye women, and let your ear receive the word of his mouth, and teach your daughters wailing, and every one her neighbour lamentation.
For*p death is come up into our windows, and is entered into our palaces, to cut off the children from without, and the young men from the streets.
Speak,*p Thus saith the Lord,*s Even the carcases of men shall fall as dung upon the open field, and as the handful after the harvestman, and none shall gather them.
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches:

But*p let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the Lord*s which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the Lord.*s
Behold,*p the days come, saith the Lord,*s that I will punish all them which are circumcised with the uncircumcised;

Egypt,*p and Judah, and Edom, and the children of Ammon, and Moab, and all that are in the utmost corners, that dwell in the wilderness: for all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in the heart.
Jeremiah 10
Hear*p ye the word which the Lord*s speaketh unto you, O house of Israel:
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.

Forasmuch*p as there is none like unto thee, O Lord;*s thou art great, and thy name is great in might.

When*p he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.
Every*p man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They*p are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish.
The*p portion of Jacob is not like them: for he is the former of all things; and Israel is the rod of his inheritance: The Lord*s of hosts is his name.
Gather*p up thy wares out of the land, O inhabitant of the fortress.
For*p thus saith the Lord,*s Behold, I will sling out the inhabitants of the land at this once, and will distress them, that they may find it so.
Woe*p is me for my hurt! my wound is grievous: but I said, Truly this is a grief, and I must bear it.
My*p tabernacle is spoiled, and all my cords are broken: my children are gone forth of me, and they are not: there is none to stretch forth my tent any more, and to set up my curtains.
For*p the pastors are become brutish, and have not sought the Lord:*s therefore they shall not prosper, and all their flocks shall be scattered.
Behold,*p the noise of the bruit is come, and a great commotion out of the north country, to make the cities of Judah desolate, and a den of dragons.
O*p Lord,*s I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his steps.
O*p Lord,*s correct me, but with judgment; not in thine anger, lest thou bring me to nothing.

Pour*p out thy fury upon the heathen that know thee not, and upon the families that call not on thy name: for they have eaten up Jacob, and devoured him, and consumed him, and have made his habitation desolate.
Jeremiah 11
The*p word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord,*s saying,
Hear*p ye the words of this covenant, and speak unto the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem;
And*p say thou unto them, Thus saith the Lord*s God of Israel; Cursed be the man that obeyeth not the words of this covenant,

Which*p I commanded your fathers in the day that I brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, from the iron furnace, saying, Obey my voice, and do them, according to all which I command you: so shall ye be my people, and I will be your God:
That*p I may perform the oath which I have sworn unto your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day. Then answered I, and said, So be it, O Lord.*s
Then*p the Lord*s said unto me, Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, saying, Hear ye the words of this covenant, and do them.
For*p I earnestly protested unto your fathers in the day that I brought them up out of the land of Egypt, even unto this day, rising early and protesting, saying, Obey my voice.

Yet*p they obeyed not, nor inclined their ear, but walked every one in the imagination of their evil heart: therefore I will bring upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do; but they did them not.
And*p the Lord*s said unto me, A conspiracy is found among the men of Judah, and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They*p are turned back to the iniquities of their forefathers, which refused to hear my words; and they went after other gods to serve them: the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant which I made with their fathers.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord,*s Behold, I will bring evil upon them, which they shall not be able to escape; and though they shall cry unto me, I will not hearken unto them.
Then*p shall the cities of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem go, and cry unto the gods unto whom they offer incense: but they shall not save them at all in the time of their trouble.

For*p according to the number of thy cities were thy gods, O Judah; and according to the number of the streets of Jerusalem have ye set up altars to that shameful thing, even altars to burn incense unto Baal.
Therefore*p pray not thou for this people, neither lift up a cry or prayer for them: for I will not hear them in the time that they cry unto me for their trouble.
What*p hath my beloved to do in mine house, seeing she hath wrought lewdness with many, and the holy flesh is passed from thee? when thou doest evil, then thou rejoicest.
The*p Lord*s called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.

For*p the Lord*s of hosts, that planted thee, hath pronounced evil against thee, for the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which they have done against themselves to provoke me to anger in offering incense unto Baal.
And*p the Lord*s hath given me knowledge of it, and I know it: then thou shewedst me their doings.

But*p I was like a lamb or an ox that is brought to the slaughter; and I knew not that they had devised devices against me, saying, Let us destroy the tree with the fruit thereof, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be no more remembered.
But,*p O Lord*s of hosts, that judgest righteously, that triest the reins and the heart, let me see thy vengeance on them: for unto thee have I revealed my cause.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of the men of Anathoth, that seek thy life, saying, Prophesy not in the name of the Lord,*s that thou die not by our hand:
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, Behold, I will punish them: the young men shall die by the sword; their sons and their daughters shall die by famine:
And*p there shall be no remnant of them: for I will bring evil upon the men of Anathoth, even the year of their visitation.
Jeremiah 12

Righteous*p art thou, O Lord,*s when I plead with thee: yet let me talk with thee of thy judgments: Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper? wherefore are all they happy that deal very treacherously?
Thou*p hast planted them, yea, they have taken root: they grow, yea, they bring forth fruit: thou art near in their mouth, and far from their reins.
But*p thou, O Lord,*s knowest me: thou hast seen me, and tried mine heart toward thee: pull them out like sheep for the slaughter, and prepare them for the day of slaughter.

How*p long shall the land mourn, and the herbs of every field wither, for the wickedness of them that dwell therein? the beasts are consumed, and the birds; because they said, He shall not see our last end.

If*p thou hast run with the footmen, and they have wearied thee, then how canst thou contend with horses? and if in the land of peace, wherein thou trustedst, they wearied thee, then how wilt thou do in the swelling of Jordan?

For*p even thy brethren, and the house of thy father, even they have dealt treacherously with thee; yea, they have called a multitude after thee: believe them not, though they speak fair words unto thee.
I*p have forsaken mine house, I have left mine heritage; I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies.
Mine*p heritage is unto me as a lion in the forest; it crieth out against me: therefore have I hated it.
Mine*p heritage is unto me as a speckled bird, the birds round about are against her; come ye, assemble all the beasts of the field, come to devour.
Many*p pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot, they have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.
They*p have made it desolate, and being desolate it mourneth unto me; the whole land is made desolate, because no man layeth it to heart.

The*p spoilers are come upon all high places through the wilderness: for the sword of the Lord*s shall devour from the one end of the land even to the other end of the land: no flesh shall have peace.
They*p have sown wheat, but shall reap thorns: they have put themselves to pain, but shall not profit: and they shall be ashamed of your revenues because of the fierce anger of the Lord.*s

Thus*p saith the Lord*s against all mine evil neighbours, that touch the inheritance which I have caused my people Israel to inherit; Behold, I will pluck them out of their land, and pluck out the house of Judah from among them.
And*p it shall come to pass, after that I have plucked them out I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.

And*p it shall come to pass, if they will diligently learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, The Lord*s liveth; as they taught my people to swear by Baal; then shall they be built in the midst of my people.
But*p if they will not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation, saith the Lord.*s
Jeremiah 13
Thus*p saith the Lord*s unto me, Go and get thee a linen girdle, and put it upon thy loins, and put it not in water.
So*p I got a girdle according to the word of the Lord,*s and put it on my loins.
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me the second time, saying,
Take*p the girdle that thou hast got, which is upon thy loins, and arise, go to Euphrates, and hide it there in a hole of the rock.
So*p I went, and hid it by Euphrates, as the Lord*s commanded me.
And*p it came to pass after many days, that the Lord*s said unto me, Arise, go to Euphrates, and take the girdle from thence, which I commanded thee to hide there.
Then*p I went to Euphrates, and digged, and took the girdle from the place where I had hid it: and, behold, the girdle was marred, it was profitable for nothing.
Then*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.

This*p evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.

For*p as the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man, so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, saith the Lord;*s that they might be unto me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear.

Therefore*p thou shalt speak unto them this word; Thus saith the Lord*s God of Israel, Every bottle shall be filled with wine: and they shall say unto thee, Do we not certainly know that every bottle shall be filled with wine?

Then*p shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the Lord,*s Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings that sit upon David's throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness.
And*p I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the Lord:*s I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.
Hear*p ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord*s hath spoken.

Give*p glory to the Lord*s your God, before he cause darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains, and, while ye look for light, he turn it into the shadow of death, and make it gross darkness.
But*p if ye will not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret places for your pride; and mine eye shall weep sore, and run down with tears, because the Lord's*s flock is carried away captive.
Say*p unto the king and to the queen, Humble yourselves, sit down: for your principalities shall come down, even the crown of your glory.
The*p cities of the south shall be shut up, and none shall open them: Judah shall be carried away captive all of it, it shall be wholly carried away captive.
Lift*p up your eyes, and behold them that come from the north: where is the flock that was given thee, thy beautiful flock?
What*p wilt thou say when he shall punish thee? for thou hast taught them to be captains, and as chief over thee: shall not sorrows take thee, as a woman in travail?
And*p if thou say in thine heart, Wherefore come these things upon me? For the greatness of thine iniquity are thy skirts discovered, and thy heels made bare.
Can*p the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil.
Therefore*p will I scatter them as the stubble that passeth away by the wind of the wilderness.
This*p is thy lot, the portion of thy measures from me, saith the Lord;*s because thou hast forgotten me, and trusted in falsehood.
Therefore*p will I discover thy skirts upon thy face, that thy shame may appear.

I*p have seen thine adulteries, and thy neighings, the lewdness of thy whoredom, and thine abominations on the hills in the fields. Woe unto thee, O Jerusalem! wilt thou not be made clean? when shall it once be?
Jeremiah 14
The*p word of the Lord*s that came to Jeremiah concerning the dearth.
Judah*p mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up.

And*p their nobles have sent their little ones to the waters: they came to the pits, and found no water; they returned with their vessels empty; they were ashamed and confounded, and covered their heads.
Because*p the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the plowmen were ashamed, they covered their heads.
Yea,*p the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass.
And*p the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass.
O*p Lord,*s though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name's sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.
O*p the hope of Israel, the saviour thereof in time of trouble, why shouldest thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man that turneth aside to tarry for a night?
Why*p shouldest thou be as a man astonished, as a mighty man that cannot save? yet thou, O Lord,*s art in the midst of us, and we are called by thy name; leave us not.

Thus*p saith the Lord*s unto this people, Thus have they loved to wander, they have not refrained their feet, therefore the Lord*s doth not accept them; he will now remember their iniquity, and visit their sins.

When*p they fast, I will not hear their cry; and when they offer burnt offering and an oblation, I will not accept them: but I will consume them by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence.
Then*p said I, Ah, Lord God!*s behold, the prophets say unto them, Ye shall not see the sword, neither shall ye have famine; but I will give you assured peace in this place.

Then*p the Lord*s said unto me, The prophets prophesy lies in my name: I sent them not, neither have I commanded them, neither spake unto them: they prophesy unto you a false vision and divination, and a thing of nought, and the deceit of their heart.

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s concerning the prophets that prophesy in my name, and I sent them not, yet they say, Sword and famine shall not be in this land; By sword and famine shall those prophets be consumed.

Therefore*p thou shalt say this word unto them; Let mine eyes run down with tears night and day, and let them not cease: for the virgin daughter of my people is broken with a great breach, with a very grievous blow.

If*p I go forth into the field, then behold the slain with the sword! and if I enter into the city, then behold them that are sick with famine! yea, both the prophet and the priest go about into a land that they know not.

Hast*p thou utterly rejected Judah? hath thy soul lothed Zion? why hast thou smitten us, and there is no healing for us? we looked for peace, and there is no good; and for the time of healing, and behold trouble!
We*p acknowledge, O Lord,*s our wickedness, and the iniquity of our fathers: for we have sinned against thee.

Jeremiah 15
Then*p said the Lord*s unto me, Though Moses and Samuel stood before me, yet my mind could not be toward this people: cast them out of my sight, and let them go forth.

And*p I will appoint over them four kinds, saith the Lord:*s the sword to slay, and the dogs to tear, and the fowls of the heaven, and the beasts of the earth, to devour and destroy.

Thou*p hast forsaken me, saith the Lord,*s thou art gone backward: therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee; I am weary with repenting.

Their*p widows are increased to me above the sand of the seas: I have brought upon them against the mother of the young men a spoiler at noonday: I have caused him to fall upon it suddenly, and terrors upon the city.

She*p that hath borne seven languisheth: she hath given up the ghost; her sun is gone down while it was yet day: she hath been ashamed and confounded: and the residue of them will I deliver to the sword before their enemies, saith the Lord.*s

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord,*s If thou return, then will I bring thee again, and thou shalt stand before me: and if thou take forth the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth: let them return unto thee; but return not thou unto them.

And*p I will make thee unto this people a fenced brasen wall: and they shall fight against thee, but they shall not prevail against thee: for I am with thee to save thee and to deliver thee, saith the Lord.*s
And*p I will deliver thee out of the hand of the wicked, and I will redeem thee out of the hand of the terrible.
Jeremiah 16
The*p word of the Lord*s came also unto me, saying,
Thou*p shalt not take thee a wife, neither shalt thou have sons or daughters in this place.

They*p shall die of grievous deaths; they shall not be lamented; neither shall they be buried; but they shall be as dung upon the face of the earth: and they shall be consumed by the sword, and by famine; and their carcases shall be meat for the fowls of heaven, and for the beasts of the earth.

For*p thus saith the Lord,*s Enter not into the house of mourning, neither go to lament nor bemoan them: for I have taken away my peace from this people, saith the Lord,*s even lovingkindness and mercies.
Both*p the great and the small shall die in this land: they shall not be buried, neither shall men lament for them, nor cut themselves, nor make themselves bald for them:
Neither*p shall men tear themselves for them in mourning, to comfort them for the dead; neither shall men give them the cup of consolation to drink for their father or for their mother.
Thou*p shalt not also go into the house of feasting, to sit with them to eat and to drink.

For*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will cause to cease out of this place in your eyes, and in your days, the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride.

And*p it shall come to pass, when thou shalt shew this people all these words, and they shall say unto thee, Wherefore hath the Lord*s pronounced all this great evil against us? or what is our iniquity? or what is our sin that we have committed against the Lord*s our God?

Then*p shalt thou say unto them, Because your fathers have forsaken me, saith the Lord,*s and have walked after other gods, and have served them, and have worshipped them, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my law;
And*p ye have done worse than your fathers; for, behold, ye walk every one after the imagination of his evil heart, that they may not hearken unto me:
Therefore*p will I cast you out of this land into a land that ye know not, neither ye nor your fathers; and there shall ye serve other gods day and night; where I will not shew you favour.
Therefore,*p behold, the days come, saith the Lord,*s that it shall no more be said, The Lord*s liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt;

But,*p The Lord*s liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.

O*p Lord,*s my strength, and my fortress, and my refuge in the day of affliction, the Gentiles shall come unto thee from the ends of the earth, and shall say, Surely our fathers have inherited lies, vanity, and things wherein there is no profit.
Shall*p a man make gods unto himself, and they are no gods?
Therefore,*p behold, I will this once cause them to know, I will cause them to know mine hand and my might; and they shall know that my name is The Lord.*s

The*p sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond: it is graven upon the table of their heart, and upon the horns of your altars;
Whilst*p their children remember their altars and their groves by the green trees upon the high hills.

For*p he shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land and not inhabited.

For*p he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
The*p heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?
I*p the Lord*s search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.

A*p glorious high throne from the beginning is the place of our sanctuary.

O*p Lord,*s the hope of Israel, all that forsake thee shall be ashamed, and they that depart from me shall be written in the earth, because they have forsaken the Lord,*s the fountain of living waters.
Heal*p me, O Lord,*s and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved: for thou art my praise.
Behold,*p they say unto me, Where is the word of the Lord?*s let it come now.
As*p for me, I have not hastened from being a pastor to follow thee: neither have I desired the woeful day; thou knowest: that which came out of my lips was right before thee.
Be*p not a terror unto me: thou art my hope in the day of evil.
Let*p them be confounded that persecute me, but let not me be confounded: let them be dismayed, but let not me be dismayed: bring upon them the day of evil, and destroy them with double destruction.
Thus*p said the Lord*s unto me; Go and stand in the gate of the children of the people, whereby the kings of Judah come in, and by the which they go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem;
And*p say unto them, Hear ye the word of the Lord,*s ye kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that enter in by these gates:
Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem;
Neither*p carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.
But*p they obeyed not, neither inclined their ear, but made their neck stiff, that they might not hear, nor receive instruction.

And*p it shall come to pass, if ye diligently hearken unto me, saith the Lord,*s to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the sabbath day, but hallow the sabbath day, to do no work therein;

And*p they shall come from the cities of Judah, and from the places about Jerusalem, and from the land of Benjamin, and from the plain, and from the mountains, and from the south, bringing burnt offerings, and sacrifices, and meat offerings, and incense, and bringing sacrifices of praise, unto the house of the Lord.*s

Jeremiah 18
The*p word which came to Jeremiah from the Lord,*s saying,
Arise,*p and go down to the potter's house, and there I will cause thee to hear my words.
Then*p I went down to the potter's house, and, behold, he wrought a work on the wheels.
And*p the vessel that he made of clay was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
Then*p the word of the Lord*s came to me, saying,

If*p that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.
And*p at what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to build and to plant it;
If*p it do evil in my sight, that it obey not my voice, then I will repent of the good, wherewith I said I would benefit them.

Now*p therefore go to, speak to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, Thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, I frame evil against you, and devise a device against you: return ye now every one from his evil way, and make your ways and your doings good.
And*p they said, There is no hope: but we will walk after our own devices, and we will every one do the imagination of his evil heart.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord;*s Ask ye now among the heathen, who hath heard such things: the virgin of Israel hath done a very horrible thing.
Will*p a man leave the snow of Lebanon which cometh from the rock of the field? or shall the cold flowing waters that come from another place be forsaken?
Because*p my people hath forgotten me, they have burned incense to vanity, and they have caused them to stumble in their ways from the ancient paths, to walk in paths, in a way not cast up;
To*p make their land desolate, and a perpetual hissing; every one that passeth thereby shall be astonished, and wag his head.

Then*p said they, Come, and let us devise devices against Jeremiah; for the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, and let us smite him with the tongue, and let us not give heed to any of his words.
Give*p heed to me, O Lord,*s and hearken to the voice of them that contend with me.

Therefore*p deliver up their children to the famine, and pour out their blood by the force of the sword; and let their wives be bereaved of their children, and be widows; and let their men be put to death; let their young men be slain by the sword in battle.
Let*p a cry be heard from their houses, when thou shalt bring a troop suddenly upon them: for they have digged a pit to take me, and hid snares for my feet.

Yet,*p Lord,*s thou knowest all their counsel against me to slay me: forgive not their iniquity, neither blot out their sin from thy sight, but let them be overthrown before thee; deal thus with them in the time of thine anger.
Jeremiah 19
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s Go and get a potter's earthen bottle, and take of the ancients of the people, and of the ancients of the priests;
And*p go forth unto the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is by the entry of the east gate, and proclaim there the words that I shall tell thee,

Because*p they have forsaken me, and have estranged this place, and have burned incense in it unto other gods, whom neither they nor their fathers have known, nor the kings of Judah, and have filled this place with the blood of innocents;
They*p have built also the high places of Baal, to burn their sons with fire for burnt offerings unto Baal, which I commanded not, nor spake it, neither came it into my mind:

Thus*p will I do unto this place, saith the Lord,*s and to the inhabitants thereof, and even make this city as Topheth:

Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring upon this city and upon all her towns all the evil that I have pronounced against it, because they have hardened their necks, that they might not hear my words.
Jeremiah 20
Now*p Pashur the son of Immer the priest, who was also chief governor in the house of the Lord,*s heard that Jeremiah prophesied these things.
Then*p Pashur smote Jeremiah the prophet, and put him in the stocks that were in the high gate of Benjamin, which was by the house of the Lord.*s
And*p it came to pass on the morrow, that Pashur brought forth Jeremiah out of the stocks. Then said Jeremiah unto him, The Lord*s hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magor–missabib.

For*p thus saith the Lord,*s Behold, I will make thee a terror to thyself, and to all thy friends: and they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and thine eyes shall behold it: and I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall carry them captive into Babylon, and shall slay them with the sword.

Moreover*p I will deliver all the strength of this city, and all the labours thereof, and all the precious things thereof, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah will I give into the hand of their enemies, which shall spoil them, and take them, and carry them to Babylon.

And*p thou, Pashur, and all that dwell in thine house shall go into captivity: and thou shalt come to Babylon, and there thou shalt die, and shalt be buried there, thou, and all thy friends, to whom thou hast prophesied lies.
O*p Lord,*s thou hast deceived me, and I was deceived: thou art stronger than I, and hast prevailed: I am in derision daily, every one mocketh me.
For*p since I spake, I cried out, I cried violence and spoil; because the word of the Lord*s was made a reproach unto me, and a derision, daily.

Then*p I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.

For*p I heard the defaming of many, fear on every side. Report, say they, and we will report it. All my familiars watched for my halting, saying, Peradventure he will be enticed, and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.

But*p the Lord*s is with me as a mighty terrible one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not prevail: they shall be greatly ashamed; for they shall not prosper: their everlasting confusion shall never be forgotten.
But,*p O Lord*s of hosts, that triest the righteous, and seest the reins and the heart, let me see thy vengeance on them: for unto thee have I opened my cause.
Sing*p unto the Lord,*s praise ye the Lord:*s for he hath delivered the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers.
Cursed*p be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed.
Cursed*p be the man who brought tidings to my father, saying, A man child is born unto thee; making him very glad.
And*p let that man be as the cities which the Lord*s overthrew, and repented not: and let him hear the cry in the morning, and the shouting at noontide;
Because*p he slew me not from the womb; or that my mother might have been my grave, and her womb to be always great with me.
Wherefore*p came I forth out of the womb to see labour and sorrow, that my days should be consumed with shame?
Jeremiah 21
The*p word which came unto Jeremiah from the Lord,*s when king Zedekiah sent unto him Pashur the son of Malchijah, and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, saying,

Enquire,*p I pray thee, of the Lord*s for us; for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon maketh war against us; if so be that the Lord*s will deal with us according to all his wondrous works, that he may go up from us.
Then*p said Jeremiah unto them, Thus shall ye say to Zedekiah:

Thus*p saith the Lord*s God of Israel; Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands, wherewith ye fight against the king of Babylon, and against the Chaldeans, which besiege you without the walls, and I will assemble them into the midst of this city.
And*p I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and with a strong arm, even in anger, and in fury, and in great wrath.
And*p I will smite the inhabitants of this city, both man and beast: they shall die of a great pestilence.

And*p afterward, saith the Lord,*s I will deliver Zedekiah king of Judah, and his servants, and the people, and such as are left in this city from the pestilence, from the sword, and from the famine, into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those that seek their life: and he shall smite them with the edge of the sword; he shall not spare them, neither have pity, nor have mercy.
And*p unto this people thou shalt say, Thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death.

He*p that abideth in this city shall die by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence: but he that goeth out, and falleth to the Chaldeans that besiege you, he shall live, and his life shall be unto him for a prey.
For*p I have set my face against this city for evil, and not for good, saith the Lord:*s it shall be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire.
And*p touching the house of the king of Judah, say, Hear ye the word of the Lord;*s

O*p house of David, thus saith the Lord;*s Execute judgment in the morning, and deliver him that is spoiled out of the hand of the oppressor, lest my fury go out like fire, and burn that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.
Behold,*p I am against thee, O inhabitant of the valley, and rock of the plain, saith the Lord;*s which say, Who shall come down against us? or who shall enter into our habitations?
But*p I will punish you according to the fruit of your doings, saith the Lord:*s and I will kindle a fire in the forest thereof, and it shall devour all things round about it.
Jeremiah 22
Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Go down to the house of the king of Judah, and speak there this word,
And*p say, Hear the word of the Lord,*s O king of Judah, that sittest upon the throne of David, thou, and thy servants, and thy people that enter in by these gates:

Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Execute ye judgment and righteousness, and deliver the spoiled out of the hand of the oppressor: and do no wrong, do no violence to the stranger, the fatherless, nor the widow, neither shed innocent blood in this place.
For*p if ye do this thing indeed, then shall there enter in by the gates of this house kings sitting upon the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, he, and his servants, and his people.
But*p if ye will not hear these words, I swear by myself, saith the Lord,*s that this house shall become a desolation.
For*p thus saith the Lord*s unto the king's house of Judah; Thou art Gilead unto me, and the head of Lebanon: yet surely I will make thee a wilderness, and cities which are not inhabited.
And*p I will prepare destroyers against thee, every one with his weapons: and they shall cut down thy choice cedars, and cast them into the fire.
And*p many nations shall pass by this city, and they shall say every man to his neighbour, Wherefore hath the Lord*s done thus unto this great city?
Then*p they shall answer, Because they have forsaken the covenant of the Lord*s their God, and worshipped other gods, and served them.
Weep*p ye not for the dead, neither bemoan him: but weep sore for him that goeth away: for he shall return no more, nor see his native country.
For*p thus saith the Lord*s touching Shallum the son of Josiah king of Judah, which reigned instead of Josiah his father, which went forth out of this place; He shall not return thither any more:
But*p he shall die in the place whither they have led him captive, and shall see this land no more.
Woe*p unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong; that useth his neighbour's service without wages, and giveth him not for his work;
That*p saith, I will build me a wide house and large chambers, and cutteth him out windows; and it is ceiled with cedar, and painted with vermilion.
Shalt*p thou reign, because thou closest thyself in cedar? did not thy father eat and drink, and do judgment and justice, and then it was well with him?
He*p judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well with him: was not this to know me? saith the Lord.*s
But*p thine eyes and thine heart are not but for thy covetousness, and for to shed innocent blood, and for oppression, and for violence, to do it.

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s concerning Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah; They shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother! or, Ah sister! they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah lord! or, Ah his glory!
He*p shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Go*p up to Lebanon, and cry; and lift up thy voice in Bashan, and cry from the passages: for all thy lovers are destroyed.
I*p spake unto thee in thy prosperity; but thou saidst, I will not hear. This hath been thy manner from thy youth, that thou obeyedst not my voice.
The*p wind shall eat up all thy pastors, and thy lovers shall go into captivity: surely then shalt thou be ashamed and confounded for all thy wickedness.
O*p inhabitant of Lebanon, that makest thy nest in the cedars, how gracious shalt thou be when pangs come upon thee, the pain as of a woman in travail!
As*p I live, saith the Lord,*s though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence;

And*p I will give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life, and into the hand of them whose face thou fearest, even into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
And*p I will cast thee out, and thy mother that bare thee, into another country, where ye were not born; and there shall ye die.
But*p to the land whereunto they desire to return, thither shall they not return.
Is*p this man Coniah a despised broken idol? is he a vessel wherein is no pleasure? wherefore are they cast out, he and his seed, and are cast into a land which they know not?
O*p earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the Lord.*s
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s Write ye this man childless, a man that shall not prosper in his days: for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah.
Jeremiah 23
Woe*p be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.*s

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s God of Israel against the pastors that feed my people; Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the Lord.*s
And*p I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them, and will bring them again to their folds; and they shall be fruitful and increase.
And*p I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them: and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall they be lacking, saith the Lord.*s
Behold,*p the days come, saith the Lord,*s that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.
In*p his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE Lord*s OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.
Therefore,*p behold, the days come, saith the Lord,*s that they shall no more say, The Lord*s liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt;

But,*p The Lord*s liveth, which brought up and which led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country, and from all countries whither I had driven them; and they shall dwell in their own land.

Mine*p heart within me is broken because of the prophets; all my bones shake; I am like a drunken man, and like a man whom wine hath overcome, because of the Lord,*s and because of the words of his holiness.
For*p the land is full of adulterers; for because of swearing the land mourneth; the pleasant places of the wilderness are dried up, and their course is evil, and their force is not right.
For*p both prophet and priest are profane; yea, in my house have I found their wickedness, saith the Lord.*s

Wherefore*p their way shall be unto them as slippery ways in the darkness: they shall be driven on, and fall therein: for I will bring evil upon them, even the year of their visitation, saith the Lord.*s
And*p I have seen folly in the prophets of Samaria; they prophesied in Baal, and caused my people Israel to err.

I*p have seen also in the prophets of Jerusalem an horrible thing: they commit adultery, and walk in lies: they strengthen also the hands of evildoers, that none doth return from his wickedness: they are all of them unto me as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrah.

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts concerning the prophets; Behold, I will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink the water of gall: for from the prophets of Jerusalem is profaneness gone forth into all the land.

Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.*s
They*p say still unto them that despise me, The Lord*s hath said, Ye shall have peace; and they say unto every one that walketh after the imagination of his own heart, No evil shall come upon you.
For*p who hath stood in the counsel of the Lord,*s and hath perceived and heard his word? who hath marked his word, and heard it?
Behold,*p a whirlwind of the Lord*s is gone forth in fury, even a grievous whirlwind: it shall fall grievously upon the head of the wicked.
The*p anger of the Lord*s shall not return, until he have executed, and till he have performed the thoughts of his heart: in the latter days ye shall consider it perfectly.
I*p have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.
But*p if they had stood in my counsel, and had caused my people to hear my words, then they should have turned them from their evil way, and from the evil of their doings.
Am*p I a God at hand, saith the Lord,*s and not a God afar off?
Can*p any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the Lord.*s Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the Lord.*s
I*p have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.
How*p long shall this be in the heart of the prophets that prophesy lies? yea, they are prophets of the deceit of their own heart;
Which*p think to cause my people to forget my name by their dreams which they tell every man to his neighbour, as their fathers have forgotten my name for Baal.
The*p prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that hath my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat? saith the Lord.*s
Is*p not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord;*s and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?
Therefore,*p behold, I am against the prophets, saith the Lord,*s that steal my words every one from his neighbour.
Behold,*p I am against the prophets, saith the Lord,*s that use their tongues, and say, He saith.

Behold,*p I am against them that prophesy false dreams, saith the Lord,*s and do tell them, and cause my people to err by their lies, and by their lightness; yet I sent them not, nor commanded them: therefore they shall not profit this people at all, saith the Lord.*s
And*p when this people, or the prophet, or a priest, shall ask thee, saying, What is the burden of the Lord?*s thou shalt then say unto them, What burden? I will even forsake you, saith the Lord.*s
And*p as for the prophet, and the priest, and the people, that shall say, The burden of the Lord,*s I will even punish that man and his house.
Thus*p shall ye say every one to his neighbour, and every one to his brother, What hath the Lord*s answered? and, What hath the Lord*s spoken?
And*p the burden of the Lord*s shall ye mention no more: for every man's word shall be his burden; for ye have perverted the words of the living God, of the Lord*s of hosts our God.
Thus*p shalt thou say to the prophet, What hath the Lord*s answered thee? and, What hath the Lord*s spoken?

But*p since ye say, The burden of the Lord;*s therefore thus saith the Lord;*s Because ye say this word, The burden of the Lord,*s and I have sent unto you, saying, Ye shall not say, The burden of the Lord;*s
Therefore,*p behold, I, even I, will utterly forget you, and I will forsake you, and the city that I gave you and your fathers, and cast you out of my presence:
And*p I will bring an everlasting reproach upon you, and a perpetual shame, which shall not be forgotten.
Jeremiah 24

The*p Lord*s shewed me, and, behold, two baskets of figs were set before the temple of the Lord,*s after that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, and the princes of Judah, with the carpenters and smiths, from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon.
One*p basket had very good figs, even like the figs that are first ripe: and the other basket had very naughty figs, which could not be eaten, they were so bad.
Then*p said the Lord*s unto me, What seest thou, Jeremiah? And I said, Figs; the good figs, very good; and the evil, very evil, that cannot be eaten, they are so evil.
Again*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,

Thus*p saith the Lord,*s the God of Israel; Like these good figs, so will I acknowledge them that are carried away captive of Judah, whom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans for their good.
For*p I will set mine eyes upon them for good, and I will bring them again to this land: and I will build them, and not pull them down; and I will plant them, and not pluck them up.
And*p I will give them an heart to know me, that I am the Lord:*s and they shall be my people, and I will be their God: for they shall return unto me with their whole heart.

And*p as the evil figs, which cannot be eaten, they are so evil; surely thus saith the Lord,*s So will I give Zedekiah the king of Judah, and his princes, and the residue of Jerusalem, that remain in this land, and them that dwell in the land of Egypt:
And*p I will deliver them to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth for their hurt, to be a reproach and a proverb, a taunt and a curse, in all places whither I shall drive them.
And*p I will send the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, among them, till they be consumed from off the land that I gave unto them and to their fathers.
Jeremiah 25
The*p word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, that was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon;
The*p which Jeremiah the prophet spake unto all the people of Judah, and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying,

From*p the thirteenth year of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, even unto this day, that is the three and twentieth year, the word of the Lord*s hath come unto me, and I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye have not hearkened.
And*p the Lord*s hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; but ye have not hearkened, nor inclined your ear to hear.
They*p said, Turn ye again now every one from his evil way, and from the evil of your doings, and dwell in the land that the Lord*s hath given unto you and to your fathers for ever and ever:
And*p go not after other gods to serve them, and to worship them, and provoke me not to anger with the works of your hands; and I will do you no hurt.
Yet*p ye have not hearkened unto me, saith the Lord;*s that ye might provoke me to anger with the works of your hands to your own hurt.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts; Because ye have not heard my words,

Behold,*p I will send and take all the families of the north, saith the Lord,*s and Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will bring them against this land, and against the inhabitants thereof, and against all these nations round about, and will utterly destroy them, and make them an astonishment, and an hissing, and perpetual desolations.
Moreover*p I will take from them the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the candle.
And*p this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

And*p it shall come to pass, when seventy years are accomplished, that I will punish the king of Babylon, and that nation, saith the Lord,*s for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and will make it perpetual desolations.
And*p I will bring upon that land all my words which I have pronounced against it, even all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah hath prophesied against all the nations.
For*p many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of them also: and I will recompense them according to their deeds, and according to the works of their own hands.
For*p thus saith the Lord*s God of Israel unto me; Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.
And*p they shall drink, and be moved, and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them.
Then*p took I the cup at the Lord's*s hand, and made all the nations to drink, unto whom the Lord*s had sent me:
To*p wit, Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, and the kings thereof, and the princes thereof, to make them a desolation, an astonishment, an hissing, and a curse; as it is this day;
Pharaoh*p king of Egypt, and his servants, and his princes, and all his people;
And*p all the mingled people, and all the kings of the land of Uz, and all the kings of the land of the Philistines, and Ashkelon, and Gaza, and Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod,
Edom,*p and Moab, and the children of Ammon,
And*p all the kings of Tyre, and all the kings of Zidon, and the kings of the isles which are beyond the sea,
Dedan,*p and Tema, and Buz, and all that are in the utmost corners,
And*p all the kings of Arabia, and all the kings of the mingled people that dwell in the desert,
And*p all the kings of Zimri, and all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of the Medes,
And*p all the kings of the north, far and near, one with another, and all the kingdoms of the world, which are upon the face of the earth: and the king of Sheshach shall drink after them.

Therefore*p thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Drink ye, and be drunken, and spue, and fall, and rise no more, because of the sword which I will send among you.
And*p it shall be, if they refuse to take the cup at thine hand to drink, then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the Lord*s of hosts; Ye shall certainly drink.

For,*p lo, I begin to bring evil on the city which is called by my name, and should ye be utterly unpunished? Ye shall not be unpunished: for I will call for a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth, saith the Lord*s of hosts.

Therefore*p prophesy thou against them all these words, and say unto them, The Lord*s shall roar from on high, and utter his voice from his holy habitation; he shall mightily roar upon his habitation; he shall give a shout, as they that tread the grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth.
A*p noise shall come even to the ends of the earth; for the Lord*s hath a controversy with the nations, he will plead with all flesh; he will give them that are wicked to the sword, saith the Lord.*s
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, Behold, evil shall go forth from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind shall be raised up from the coasts of the earth.

And*p the slain of the Lord*s shall be at that day from one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth: they shall not be lamented, neither gathered, nor buried; they shall be dung upon the ground.

Howl,*p ye shepherds, and cry; and wallow yourselves in the ashes, ye principal of the flock: for the days of your slaughter and of your dispersions are accomplished; and ye shall fall like a pleasant vessel.
And*p the shepherds shall have no way to flee, nor the principal of the flock to escape.
A*p voice of the cry of the shepherds, and an howling of the principal of the flock, shall be heard: for the Lord*s hath spoiled their pasture.
And*p the peaceable habitations are cut down because of the fierce anger of the Lord.*s
He*p hath forsaken his covert, as the lion: for their land is desolate because of the fierceness of the oppressor, and because of his fierce anger.
Jeremiah 26
In*p the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah came this word from the Lord,*s saying,

Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Stand in the court of the Lord's*s house, and speak unto all the cities of Judah, which come to worship in the Lord's*s house, all the words that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a word:
If*p so be they will hearken, and turn every man from his evil way, that I may repent me of the evil, which I purpose to do unto them because of the evil of their doings.
And*p thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord;*s If ye will not hearken to me, to walk in my law, which I have set before you,
To*p hearken to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I sent unto you, both rising up early, and sending them, but ye have not hearkened;
Then*p will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.
So*p the priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the Lord.*s

Now*p it came to pass, when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking all that the Lord*s had commanded him to speak unto all the people, that the priests and the prophets and all the people took him, saying, Thou shalt surely die.

Why*p hast thou prophesied in the name of the Lord,*s saying, This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate without an inhabitant? And all the people were gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the Lord.*s
When*p the princes of Judah heard these things, then they came up from the king's house unto the house of the Lord,*s and sat down in the entry of the new gate of the Lord's*s house.
Then*p spake the priests and the prophets unto the princes and to all the people, saying, This man is worthy to die; for he hath prophesied against this city, as ye have heard with your ears.
Then*p spake Jeremiah unto all the princes and to all the people, saying, The Lord*s sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that ye have heard.
Therefore*p now amend your ways and your doings, and obey the voice of the Lord*s your God; and the Lord*s will repent him of the evil that he hath pronounced against you.
As*p for me, behold, I am in your hand: do with me as seemeth good and meet unto you.

But*p know ye for certain, that if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves, and upon this city, and upon the inhabitants thereof: for of a truth the Lord*s hath sent me unto you to speak all these words in your ears.
Then*p said the princes and all the people unto the priests and to the prophets; This man is not worthy to die: for he hath spoken to us in the name of the Lord*s our God.
Then*p rose up certain of the elders of the land, and spake to all the assembly of the people, saying,

Micah*p the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and spake to all the people of Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord*s of hosts; Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.
