Did*p Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him at all to death? did he not fear the Lord,*s and besought the Lord,*s and the Lord*s repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them? Thus might we procure great evil against our souls.

And*p there was also a man that prophesied in the name of the Lord,*s Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjath–jearim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah:

And*p when Jehoiakim the king, with all his mighty men, and all the princes, heard his words, the king sought to put him to death: but when Urijah heard it, he was afraid, and fled, and went into Egypt;
And*p Jehoiakim the king sent men into Egypt, namely, Elnathan the son of Achbor, and certain men with him into Egypt.
And*p they fetched forth Urijah out of Egypt, and brought him unto Jehoiakim the king; who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people.
Nevertheless*p the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.
Jeremiah 27
In*p the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah came this word unto Jeremiah from the Lord,*s saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord*s to me; Make thee bonds and yokes, and put them upon thy neck,

And*p send them to the king of Edom, and to the king of Moab, and to the king of the Ammonites, and to the king of Tyre, and to the king of Zidon, by the hand of the messengers which come to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah king of Judah;
And*p command them to say unto their masters, Thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Thus shall ye say unto your masters;
I*p have made the earth, the man and the beast that are upon the ground, by my great power and by my outstretched arm, and have given it unto whom it seemed meet unto me.
And*p now have I given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant; and the beasts of the field have I given him also to serve him.
And*p all nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son's son, until the very time of his land come: and then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him.

And*p it shall come to pass, that the nation and kingdom which will not serve the same Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, and that will not put their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, that nation will I punish, saith the Lord,*s with the sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence, until I have consumed them by his hand.

Therefore*p hearken not ye to your prophets, nor to your diviners, nor to your dreamers, nor to your enchanters, nor to your sorcerers, which speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon:
For*p they prophesy a lie unto you, to remove you far from your land; and that I should drive you out, and ye should perish.

But*p the nations that bring their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him, those will I let remain still in their own land, saith the Lord;*s and they shall till it, and dwell therein.
I*p spake also to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying, Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.
Why*p will ye die, thou and thy people, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, as the Lord*s hath spoken against the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
Therefore*p hearken not unto the words of the prophets that speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon: for they prophesy a lie unto you.
For*p I have not sent them, saith the Lord,*s yet they prophesy a lie in my name; that I might drive you out, and that ye might perish, ye, and the prophets that prophesy unto you.

Also*p I spake to the priests and to all this people, saying, Thus saith the Lord;*s Hearken not to the words of your prophets that prophesy unto you, saying, Behold, the vessels of the Lord's*s house shall now shortly be brought again from Babylon: for they prophesy a lie unto you.
Hearken*p not unto them; serve the king of Babylon, and live: wherefore should this city be laid waste?

But*p if they be prophets, and if the word of the Lord*s be with them, let them now make intercession to the Lord*s of hosts, that the vessels which are left in the house of the Lord,*s and in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem, go not to Babylon.
For*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the residue of the vessels that remain in this city,
Which*p Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took not, when he carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah from Jerusalem to Babylon, and all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem;
Yea,*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that remain in the house of the Lord,*s and in the house of the king of Judah and of Jerusalem;
They*p shall be carried to Babylon, and there shall they be until the day that I visit them, saith the Lord;*s then will I bring them up, and restore them to this place.
Jeremiah 28

And*p it came to pass the same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, and in the fifth month, that Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet, which was of Gibeon, spake unto me in the house of the Lord,*s in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying,
Thus*p speaketh the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within*p two full years will I bring again into this place all the vessels of the Lord's*s house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away from this place, and carried them to Babylon:

And*p I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, that went into Babylon, saith the Lord:*s for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Then*p the prophet Jeremiah said unto the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests, and in the presence of all the people that stood in the house of the Lord,*s

Even*p the prophet Jeremiah said, Amen: the Lord*s do so: the Lord*s perform thy words which thou hast prophesied, to bring again the vessels of the Lord's*s house, and all that is carried away captive, from Babylon into this place.
Nevertheless*p hear thou now this word that I speak in thine ears, and in the ears of all the people;
The*p prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.
The*p prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the Lord*s hath truly sent him.
Then*p Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from off the prophet Jeremiah's neck, and brake it.

And*p Hananiah spake in the presence of all the people, saying, Thus saith the Lord;*s Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all nations within the space of two full years. And the prophet Jeremiah went his way.
Then*p the word of the Lord*s came unto Jeremiah the prophet, after that Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke from off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, saying,
Go*p and tell Hananiah, saying, Thus saith the Lord;*s Thou hast broken the yokes of wood; but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron.

For*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; I have put a yoke of iron upon the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and they shall serve him: and I have given him the beasts of the field also.
Then*p said the prophet Jeremiah unto Hananiah the prophet, Hear now, Hananiah; The Lord*s hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the Lord.*s
So*p Hananiah the prophet died the same year in the seventh month.
Jeremiah 29

Now*p these are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem unto the residue of the elders which were carried away captives, and to the priests, and to the prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon;
(After*p that Jeconiah the king, and the queen, and the eunuchs, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the carpenters, and the smiths, were departed from Jerusalem;)
By*p the hand of Elasah the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, (whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent unto Babylon to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon) saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon;
Build*p ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them;

Take*p ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters; that ye may be increased there, and not diminished.
And*p seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the Lord*s for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.

For*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Let not your prophets and your diviners, that be in the midst of you, deceive you, neither hearken to your dreams which ye cause to be dreamed.
For*p they prophesy falsely unto you in my name: I have not sent them, saith the Lord.*s
For*p thus saith the Lord,*s That after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.
For*p I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord,*s thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
Then*p shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you.
And*p ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.

And*p I will be found of you, saith the Lord:*s and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places whither I have driven you, saith the Lord;*s and I will bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive.
Because*p ye have said, The Lord*s hath raised us up prophets in Babylon;

Know*p that thus saith the Lord*s of the king that sitteth upon the throne of David, and of all the people that dwelleth in this city, and of your brethren that are not gone forth with you into captivity;
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts; Behold, I will send upon them the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and will make them like vile figs, that cannot be eaten, they are so evil.

And*p I will persecute them with the sword, with the famine, and with the pestilence, and will deliver them to be removed to all the kingdoms of the earth, to be a curse, and an astonishment, and an hissing, and a reproach, among all the nations whither I have driven them:
Because*p they have not hearkened to my words, saith the Lord,*s which I sent unto them by my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them; but ye would not hear, saith the Lord.*s
Hear*p ye therefore the word of the Lord,*s all ye of the captivity, whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon:

Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel, of Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name; Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes;
And*p of them shall be taken up a curse by all the captivity of Judah which are in Babylon, saying, The Lord*s make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire;

Because*p they have committed villany in Israel, and have committed adultery with their neighbours' wives, and have spoken lying words in my name, which I have not commanded them; even I know, and am a witness, saith the Lord.*s
Thus*p shalt thou also speak to Shemaiah the Nehelamite, saying,

Thus*p speaketh the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, Because thou hast sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

The*p Lord*s hath made thee priest in the stead of Jehoiada the priest, that ye should be officers in the house of the Lord,*s for every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks.
Now*p therefore why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet to you?
For*p therefore he sent unto us in Babylon, saying, This captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.
And*p Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then*p came the word of the Lord*s unto Jeremiah, saying,

Send*p to all them of the captivity, saying, Thus saith the Lord*s concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite; Because that Shemaiah hath prophesied unto you, and I sent him not, and he caused you to trust in a lie:

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his seed: he shall not have a man to dwell among this people; neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people, saith the Lord;*s because he hath taught rebellion against the Lord.*s
Jeremiah 30
The*p word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord,*s saying,
Thus*p speaketh the Lord*s God of Israel, saying, Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book.

For,*p lo, the days come, saith the Lord,*s that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, saith the Lord:*s and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.
And*p these are the words that the Lord*s spake concerning Israel and concerning Judah.
For*p thus saith the Lord;*s We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.
Ask*p ye now, and see whether a man doth travail with child? wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness?
Alas!*p for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.
For*p it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord*s of hosts, that I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him:
But*p they shall serve the Lord*s their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.

Therefore*p fear thou not, O my servant Jacob, saith the Lord;*s neither be dismayed, O Israel: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.

For*p I am with thee, saith the Lord,*s to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.
For*p thus saith the Lord,*s Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous.
There*p is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines.

All*p thy lovers have forgotten thee; they seek thee not; for I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.
Why*p criest thou for thine affliction? thy sorrow is incurable for the multitude of thine iniquity: because thy sins were increased, I have done these things unto thee.

Therefore*p all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity; and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey.
For*p I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord;*s because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.

Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob's tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces; and the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.
And*p out of them shall proceed thanksgiving and the voice of them that make merry: and I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.
Their*p children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me, and I will punish all that oppress them.

And*p their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them; and I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me: for who is this that engaged his heart to approach unto me? saith the Lord.*s
And*p ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.
Behold,*p the whirlwind of the Lord*s goeth forth with fury, a continuing whirlwind: it shall fall with pain upon the head of the wicked.
The*p fierce anger of the Lord*s shall not return, until he have done it, and until he have performed the intents of his heart: in the latter days ye shall consider it.
Jeremiah 31
At*p the same time, saith the Lord,*s will I be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s The people which were left of the sword found grace in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.
The*p Lord*s hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.
Again*p I will build thee, and thou shalt be built, O virgin of Israel: thou shalt again be adorned with thy tabrets, and shalt go forth in the dances of them that make merry.
Thou*p shalt yet plant vines upon the mountains of Samaria: the planters shall plant, and shall eat them as common things.
For*p there shall be a day, that the watchmen upon the mount Ephraim shall cry, Arise ye, and let us go up to Zion unto the Lord*s our God.
For*p thus saith the Lord;*s Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations: publish ye, praise ye, and say, O Lord,*s save thy people, the remnant of Israel.

Behold,*p I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.

They*p shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Hear*p the word of the Lord,*s O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.
For*p the Lord*s hath redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he.

Therefore*p they shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow together to the goodness of the Lord,*s for wheat, and for wine, and for oil, and for the young of the flock and of the herd: and their soul shall be as a watered garden; and they shall not sorrow any more at all.
Then*p shall the virgin rejoice in the dance, both young men and old together: for I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
And*p I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people shall be satisfied with my goodness, saith the Lord.*s
Thus*p saith the Lord;*s A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rachel weeping for her children refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not.
Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Refrain thy voice from weeping, and thine eyes from tears: for thy work shall be rewarded, saith the Lord;*s and they shall come again from the land of the enemy.
And*p there is hope in thine end, saith the Lord,*s that thy children shall come again to their own border.

I*p have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning himself thus; Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke: turn thou me, and I shall be turned; for thou art the Lord*s my God.
Surely*p after that I was turned, I repented; and after that I was instructed, I smote upon my thigh: I was ashamed, yea, even confounded, because I did bear the reproach of my youth.

Is*p Ephraim my dear son? is he a pleasant child? for since I spake against him, I do earnestly remember him still: therefore my bowels are troubled for him; I will surely have mercy upon him, saith the Lord.*s
Set*p thee up waymarks, make thee high heaps: set thine heart toward the highway, even the way which thou wentest: turn again, O virgin of Israel, turn again to these thy cities.
How*p long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord*s hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.

Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; As yet they shall use this speech in the land of Judah and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring again their captivity; The Lord*s bless thee, O habitation of justice, and mountain of holiness.
And*p there shall dwell in Judah itself, and in all the cities thereof together, husbandmen, and they that go forth with flocks.
For*p I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.
Upon*p this I awaked, and beheld; and my sleep was sweet unto me.
Behold,*p the days come, saith the Lord,*s that I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man, and with the seed of beast.

And*p it shall come to pass, that like as I have watched over them, to pluck up, and to break down, and to throw down, and to destroy, and to afflict; so will I watch over them, to build, and to plant, saith the Lord.*s
In*p those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge.
But*p every one shall die for his own iniquity: every man that eateth the sour grape, his teeth shall be set on edge.
Behold,*p the days come, saith the Lord,*s that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah:

Not*p according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they brake, although I was an husband unto them, saith the Lord:*s

But*p this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord,*s I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.

And*p they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord:*s for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the Lord:*s for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.

Thus*p saith the Lord,*s which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord*s of hosts is his name:
If*p those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord,*s then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.

Thus*p saith the Lord;*s If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done, saith the Lord.*s
Behold,*p the days come, saith the Lord,*s that the city shall be built to the Lord*s from the tower of Hananeel unto the gate of the corner.
And*p the measuring line shall yet go forth over against it upon the hill Gareb, and shall compass about to Goath.

And*p the whole valley of the dead bodies, and of the ashes, and all the fields unto the brook of Kidron, unto the corner of the horse gate toward the east, shall be holy unto the Lord;*s it shall not be plucked up, nor thrown down any more for ever.
Jeremiah 32
The*p word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord*s in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar.
For*p then the king of Babylon's army besieged Jerusalem: and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah's house.

For*p Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, Wherefore dost thou prophesy, and say, Thus saith the Lord,*s Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it;

And*p Zedekiah king of Judah shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall behold his eyes;
And*p he shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon, and there shall he be until I visit him, saith the Lord:*s though ye fight with the Chaldeans, ye shall not prosper.
And*p Jeremiah said, The word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Behold,*p Hanameel the son of Shallum thine uncle shall come unto thee, saying, Buy thee my field that is in Anathoth: for the right of redemption is thine to buy it.

So*p Hanameel mine uncle's son came to me in the court of the prison according to the word of the Lord,*s and said unto me, Buy my field, I pray thee, that is in Anathoth, which is in the country of Benjamin: for the right of inheritance is thine, and the redemption is thine; buy it for thyself. Then I knew that this was the word of the Lord.*s
And*p I bought the field of Hanameel my uncle's son, that was in Anathoth, and weighed him the money, even seventeen shekels of silver.
And*p I subscribed the evidence, and sealed it, and took witnesses, and weighed him the money in the balances.
So*p I took the evidence of the purchase, both that which was sealed according to the law and custom, and that which was open:

And*p I gave the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, in the sight of Hanameel mine uncle's son, and in the presence of the witnesses that subscribed the book of the purchase, before all the Jews that sat in the court of the prison.
And*p I charged Baruch before them, saying,

Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Take these evidences, this evidence of the purchase, both which is sealed, and this evidence which is open; and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days.
For*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land.
Now*p when I had delivered the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, I prayed unto the Lord,*s saying,
Ah*p Lord God!*s behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:
Thou*p shewest lovingkindness unto thousands, and recompensest the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them: the Great, the Mighty God, the Lord*s of hosts, is his name,
Great*p in counsel, and mighty in work: for thine eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men: to give every one according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings:
Which*p hast set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, even unto this day, and in Israel, and among other men; and hast made thee a name, as at this day;
And*p hast brought forth thy people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs, and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with great terror;
And*p hast given them this land, which thou didst swear to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey;

And*p they came in, and possessed it; but they obeyed not thy voice, neither walked in thy law; they have done nothing of all that thou commandedst them to do: therefore thou hast caused all this evil to come upon them:

Behold*p the mounts, they are come unto the city to take it; and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans, that fight against it, because of the sword, and of the famine, and of the pestilence: and what thou hast spoken is come to pass; and, behold, thou seest it.
And*p thou hast said unto me, O Lord God,*s Buy thee the field for money, and take witnesses; for the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.
Then*p came the word of the Lord*s unto Jeremiah, saying,
Behold,*p I am the Lord,*s the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he shall take it:

And*p the Chaldeans, that fight against this city, shall come and set fire on this city, and burn it with the houses, upon whose roofs they have offered incense unto Baal, and poured out drink offerings unto other gods, to provoke me to anger.

For*p the children of Israel and the children of Judah have only done evil before me from their youth: for the children of Israel have only provoked me to anger with the work of their hands, saith the Lord.*s
For*p this city hath been to me as a provocation of mine anger and of my fury from the day that they built it even unto this day; that I should remove it from before my face,

Because*p of all the evil of the children of Israel and of the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And*p they have turned unto me the back, and not the face: though I taught them, rising up early and teaching them, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction.
But*p they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it.

And*p they built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.

And*p now therefore thus saith the Lord,*s the God of Israel, concerning this city, whereof ye say, It shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence;

Behold,*p I will gather them out of all countries, whither I have driven them in mine anger, and in my fury, and in great wrath; and I will bring them again unto this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely:
And*p they shall be my people, and I will be their God:
And*p I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever, for the good of them, and of their children after them:
And*p I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from them, to do them good; but I will put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me.
Yea,*p I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul.
For*p thus saith the Lord;*s Like as I have brought all this great evil upon this people, so will I bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.
And*p fields shall be bought in this land, whereof ye say, It is desolate without man or beast; it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

Men*p shall buy fields for money, and subscribe evidences, and seal them, and take witnesses in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the valley, and in the cities of the south: for I will cause their captivity to return, saith the Lord.*s
Jeremiah 33
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came unto Jeremiah the second time, while he was yet shut up in the court of the prison, saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord*s the maker thereof, the Lord*s that formed it, to establish it; the Lord*s is his name;
Call*p unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.
For*p thus saith the Lord,*s the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city, and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah, which are thrown down by the mounts, and by the sword;

They*p come to fight with the Chaldeans, but it is to fill them with the dead bodies of men, whom I have slain in mine anger and in my fury, and for all whose wickedness I have hid my face from this city.
Behold,*p I will bring it health and cure, and I will cure them, and will reveal unto them the abundance of peace and truth.
And*p I will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, and will build them, as at the first.

And*p I will cleanse them from all their iniquity, whereby they have sinned against me; and I will pardon all their iniquities, whereby they have sinned, and whereby they have transgressed against me.

And*p it shall be to me a name of joy, a praise and an honour before all the nations of the earth, which shall hear all the good that I do unto them: and they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness and for all the prosperity that I procure unto it.

Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Again there shall be heard in this place, which ye say shall be desolate without man and without beast, even in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, that are desolate, without man, and without inhabitant, and without beast,

The*p voice of joy, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the voice of them that shall say, Praise the Lord*s of hosts: for the Lord*s is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: and of them that shall bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the Lord.*s For I will cause to return the captivity of the land, as at the first, saith the Lord.*s

Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts; Again in this place, which is desolate without man and without beast, and in all the cities thereof, shall be an habitation of shepherds causing their flocks to lie down.

In*p the cities of the mountains, in the cities of the vale, and in the cities of the south, and in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, shall the flocks pass again under the hands of him that telleth them, saith the Lord.*s
Behold,*p the days come, saith the Lord,*s that I will perform that good thing which I have promised unto the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.
In*p those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.
In*p those days shall Judah be saved, and Jerusalem shall dwell safely: and this is the name wherewith she shall be called, The Lord*s our righteousness.
For*p thus saith the Lord;*s David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel;
Neither*p shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to kindle meat offerings, and to do sacrifice continually.
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto Jeremiah, saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord;*s If ye can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, and that there should not be day and night in their season;
Then*p may also my covenant be broken with David my servant, that he should not have a son to reign upon his throne; and with the Levites the priests, my ministers.
As*p the host of heaven cannot be numbered, neither the sand of the sea measured: so will I multiply the seed of David my servant, and the Levites that minister unto me.
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came to Jeremiah, saying,

Considerest*p thou not what this people have spoken, saying, The two families which the Lord*s hath chosen, he hath even cast them off? thus they have despised my people, that they should be no more a nation before them.
Thus*p saith the Lord;*s If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth;

Then*p will I cast away the seed of Jacob, and David my servant, so that I will not take any of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: for I will cause their captivity to return, and have mercy on them.
Jeremiah 34

The*p word which came unto Jeremiah from the Lord,*s when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth of his dominion, and all the people, fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities thereof, saying,

Thus*p saith the Lord,*s the God of Israel; Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and tell him, Thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire:

And*p thou shalt not escape out of his hand, but shalt surely be taken, and delivered into his hand; and thine eyes shall behold the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he shall speak with thee mouth to mouth, and thou shalt go to Babylon.
Yet*p hear the word of the Lord,*s O Zedekiah king of Judah; Thus saith the Lord*s of thee, Thou shalt not die by the sword:

But*p thou shalt die in peace: and with the burnings of thy fathers, the former kings which were before thee, so shall they burn odours for thee; and they will lament thee, saying, Ah lord! for I have pronounced the word, saith the Lord.*s
Then*p Jeremiah the prophet spake all these words unto Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

When*p the king of Babylon's army fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish, and against Azekah: for these defenced cities remained of the cities of Judah.
This*p is the word that came unto Jeremiah from the Lord,*s after that the king Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people which were at Jerusalem, to proclaim liberty unto them;
That*p every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.

Now*p when all the princes, and all the people, which had entered into the covenant, heard that every one should let his manservant, and every one his maidservant, go free, that none should serve themselves of them any more, then they obeyed, and let them go.
But*p afterward they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection for servants and for handmaids.
Therefore*p the word of the Lord*s came to Jeremiah from the Lord,*s saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s the God of Israel; I made a covenant with your fathers in the day that I brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondmen, saying,

At*p the end of seven years let ye go every man his brother an Hebrew, which hath been sold unto thee; and when he hath served thee six years, thou shalt let him go free from thee: but your fathers hearkened not unto me, neither inclined their ear.
And*p ye were now turned, and had done right in my sight, in proclaiming liberty every man to his neighbour; and ye had made a covenant before me in the house which is called by my name:

But*p ye turned and polluted my name, and caused every man his servant, and every man his handmaid, whom ye had set at liberty at their pleasure, to return, and brought them into subjection, to be unto you for servants and for handmaids.

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord;*s Ye have not hearkened unto me, in proclaiming liberty, every one to his brother, and every man to his neighbour: behold, I proclaim a liberty for you, saith the Lord,*s to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine; and I will make you to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.

And*p I will give the men that have transgressed my covenant, which have not performed the words of the covenant which they had made before me, when they cut the calf in twain, and passed between the parts thereof,
The*p princes of Judah, and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, and the priests, and all the people of the land, which passed between the parts of the calf;

I*p will even give them into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their life: and their dead bodies shall be for meat unto the fowls of the heaven, and to the beasts of the earth.

And*p Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes will I give into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their life, and into the hand of the king of Babylon's army, which are gone up from you.

Behold,*p I will command, saith the Lord,*s and cause them to return to this city; and they shall fight against it, and take it, and burn it with fire: and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without an inhabitant.
Jeremiah 35
The*p word which came unto Jeremiah from the Lord*s in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,
Go*p unto the house of the Rechabites, and speak unto them, and bring them into the house of the Lord,*s into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink.
Then*p I took Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habaziniah, and his brethren, and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites;

And*p I brought them into the house of the Lord,*s into the chamber of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, a man of God, which was by the chamber of the princes, which was above the chamber of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the door:
And*p I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pots full of wine, and cups, and I said unto them, Drink ye wine.
But*p they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, neither ye, nor your sons for ever:
Neither*p shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any: but all your days ye shall dwell in tents; that ye may live many days in the land where ye be strangers.
Thus*p have we obeyed the voice of Jehonadab the son of Rechab our father in all that he hath charged us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, nor our daughters;
Nor*p to build houses for us to dwell in: neither have we vineyard, nor field, nor seed:
But*p we have dwelt in tents, and have obeyed, and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.

But*p it came to pass, when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came up into the land, that we said, Come, and let us go to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians: so we dwell at Jerusalem.
Then*p came the word of the Lord*s unto Jeremiah, saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Go and tell the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Will ye not receive instruction to hearken to my words? saith the Lord.*s

The*p words of Jehonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed; for unto this day they drink none, but obey their father's commandment: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye hearkened not unto me.

I*p have sent also unto you all my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them, saying, Return ye now every man from his evil way, and amend your doings, and go not after other gods to serve them, and ye shall dwell in the land which I have given to you and to your fathers: but ye have not inclined your ear, nor hearkened unto me.
Because*p the sons of Jehonadab the son of Rechab have performed the commandment of their father, which he commanded them; but this people hath not hearkened unto me:

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s God of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring upon Judah and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evil that I have pronounced against them: because I have spoken unto them, but they have not heard; and I have called unto them, but they have not answered.

And*p Jeremiah said unto the house of the Rechabites, Thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Because ye have obeyed the commandment of Jehonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according unto all that he hath commanded you:
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever.
Jeremiah 36
And*p it came to pass in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, that this word came unto Jeremiah from the Lord,*s saying,

Take*p thee a roll of a book, and write therein all the words that I have spoken unto thee against Israel, and against Judah, and against all the nations, from the day I spake unto thee, from the days of Josiah, even unto this day.
It*p may be that the house of Judah will hear all the evil which I purpose to do unto them; that they may return every man from his evil way; that I may forgive their iniquity and their sin.
Then*p Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah: and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord,*s which he had spoken unto him, upon a roll of a book.
And*p Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, I am shut up; I cannot go into the house of the Lord:*s

Therefore*p go thou, and read in the roll, which thou hast written from my mouth, the words of the Lord*s in the ears of the people in the Lord's*s house upon the fasting day: and also thou shalt read them in the ears of all Judah that come out of their cities.

It*p may be they will present their supplication before the Lord,*s and will return every one from his evil way: for great is the anger and the fury that the Lord*s hath pronounced against this people.
And*p Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the book the words of the Lord*s in the Lord's*s house.

And*p it came to pass in the fifth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, in the ninth month, that they proclaimed a fast before the Lord*s to all the people in Jerusalem, and to all the people that came from the cities of Judah unto Jerusalem.

Then*p read Baruch in the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord,*s in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the higher court, at the entry of the new gate of the Lord's*s house, in the ears of all the people.
When*p Michaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, had heard out of the book all the words of the Lord,*s

Then*p he went down into the king's house, into the scribe's chamber: and, lo, all the princes sat there, even Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes.
Then*p Michaiah declared unto them all the words that he had heard, when Baruch read the book in the ears of the people.

Therefore*p all the princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, unto Baruch, saying, Take in thine hand the roll wherein thou hast read in the ears of the people, and come. So Baruch the son of Neriah took the roll in his hand, and came unto them.
And*p they said unto him, Sit down now, and read it in our ears. So Baruch read it in their ears.
Now*p it came to pass, when they had heard all the words, they were afraid both one and other, and said unto Baruch, We will surely tell the king of all these words.
And*p they asked Baruch, saying, Tell us now, How didst thou write all these words at his mouth?
Then*p Baruch answered them, He pronounced all these words unto me with his mouth, and I wrote them with ink in the book.
Then*p said the princes unto Baruch, Go, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah; and let no man know where ye be.
And*p they went in to the king into the court, but they laid up the roll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and told all the words in the ears of the king.

So*p the king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll: and he took it out of Elishama the scribe's chamber. And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes which stood beside the king.
Now*p the king sat in the winterhouse in the ninth month: and there was a fire on the hearth burning before him.

And*p it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth.
Yet*p they were not afraid, nor rent their garments, neither the king, nor any of his servants that heard all these words.
Nevertheless*p Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king that he would not burn the roll: but he would not hear them.
But*p the king commanded Jerahmeel the son of Hammelech, and Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel, to take Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet: but the Lord*s hid them.
Then*p the word of the Lord*s came to Jeremiah, after that the king had burned the roll, and the words which Baruch wrote at the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,
Take*p thee again another roll, and write in it all the former words that were in the first roll, which Jehoiakim the king of Judah hath burned.

And*p thou shalt say to Jehoiakim king of Judah, Thus saith the Lord;*s Thou hast burned this roll, saying, Why hast thou written therein, saying, The king of Babylon shall certainly come and destroy this land, and shall cause to cease from thence man and beast?

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of Jehoiakim king of Judah; He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David: and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost.

And*p I will punish him and his seed and his servants for their iniquity; and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them; but they hearkened not.

Then*p took Jeremiah another roll, and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah; who wrote therein from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire: and there were added besides unto them many like words.
Jeremiah 37
And*p king Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
But*p neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, did hearken unto the words of the Lord,*s which he spake by the prophet Jeremiah.
And*p Zedekiah the king sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest to the prophet Jeremiah, saying, Pray now unto the Lord*s our God for us.
Now*p Jeremiah came in and went out among the people: for they had not put him into prison.
Then*p Pharaoh's army was come forth out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans that besieged Jerusalem heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem.
Then*p came the word of the Lord*s unto the prophet Jeremiah, saying,

Thus*p saith the Lord,*s the God of Israel; Thus shall ye say to the king of Judah, that sent you unto me to enquire of me; Behold, Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land.
And*p the Chaldeans shall come again, and fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire.
Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Deceive not yourselves, saying, The Chaldeans shall surely depart from us: for they shall not depart.

For*p though ye had smitten the whole army of the Chaldeans that fight against you, and there remained but wounded men among them, yet should they rise up every man in his tent, and burn this city with fire.
And*p it came to pass, that when the army of the Chaldeans was broken up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army,
Then*p Jeremiah went forth out of Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to separate himself thence in the midst of the people.

And*p when he was in the gate of Benjamin, a captain of the ward was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he took Jeremiah the prophet, saying, Thou fallest away to the Chaldeans.
Then*p said Jeremiah, It is false; I fall not away to the Chaldeans. But he hearkened not to him: so Irijah took Jeremiah, and brought him to the princes.
Wherefore*p the princes were wroth with Jeremiah, and smote him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe: for they had made that the prison.
When*p Jeremiah was entered into the dungeon, and into the cabins, and Jeremiah had remained there many days;

Then*p Zedekiah the king sent, and took him out: and the king asked him secretly in his house, and said, Is there any word from the Lord?*s And Jeremiah said, There is: for, said he, thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.
Moreover*p Jeremiah said unto king Zedekiah, What have I offended against thee, or against thy servants, or against this people, that ye have put me in prison?
Where*p are now your prophets which prophesied unto you, saying, The king of Babylon shall not come against you, nor against this land?

Therefore*p hear now, I pray thee, O my lord the king: let my supplication, I pray thee, be accepted before thee; that thou cause me not to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there.

Then*p Zedekiah the king commanded that they should commit Jeremiah into the court of the prison, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread out of the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city were spent. Thus Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.
Jeremiah 38

Then*p Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchijah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken unto all the people, saying,

Thus*p saith the Lord,*s He that remaineth in this city shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: but he that goeth forth to the Chaldeans shall live; for he shall have his life for a prey, and shall live.
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s This city shall surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon's army, which shall take it.

Therefore*p the princes said unto the king, We beseech thee, let this man be put to death: for thus he weakeneth the hands of the men of war that remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words unto them: for this man seeketh not the welfare of this people, but the hurt.
Then*p Zedekiah the king said, Behold, he is in your hand: for the king is not he that can do any thing against you.

Then*p took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire.
Now*p when Ebed–melech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon; the king then sitting in the gate of Benjamin;
Ebed–melech*p went forth out of the king's house, and spake to the king, saying,

My*p lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have cast into the dungeon; and he is like to die for hunger in the place where he is: for there is no more bread in the city.
Then*p the king commanded Ebed–melech the Ethiopian, saying, Take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die.

So*p Ebed–melech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah.
And*p Ebed–melech the Ethiopian said unto Jeremiah, Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords. And Jeremiah did so.
So*p they drew up Jeremiah with cords, and took him up out of the dungeon: and Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.

Then*p Zedekiah the king sent, and took Jeremiah the prophet unto him into the third entry that is in the house of the Lord:*s and the king said unto Jeremiah, I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me.
Then*p Jeremiah said unto Zedekiah, If I declare it unto thee, wilt thou not surely put me to death? and if I give thee counsel, wilt thou not hearken unto me?

So*p Zedekiah the king sware secretly unto Jeremiah, saying, As the Lord*s liveth, that made us this soul, I will not put thee to death, neither will I give thee into the hand of these men that seek thy life.

Then*p said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith the Lord,*s the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house:

But*p if thou wilt not go forth to the king of Babylon's princes, then shall this city be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.
And*p Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me.
But*p Jeremiah said, They shall not deliver thee. Obey, I beseech thee, the voice of the Lord,*s which I speak unto thee: so it shall be well unto thee, and thy soul shall live.
But*p if thou refuse to go forth, this is the word that the Lord*s hath shewed me:

And,*p behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judah's house shall be brought forth to the king of Babylon's princes, and those women shall say, Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back.

So*p they shall bring out all thy wives and thy children to the Chaldeans: and thou shalt not escape out of their hand, but shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon: and thou shalt cause this city to be burned with fire.
Then*p said Zedekiah unto Jeremiah, Let no man know of these words, and thou shalt not die.

But*p if the princes hear that I have talked with thee, and they come unto thee, and say unto thee, Declare unto us now what thou hast said unto the king, hide it not from us, and we will not put thee to death; also what the king said unto thee:
Then*p thou shalt say unto them, I presented my supplication before the king, that he would not cause me to return to Jonathan's house, to die there.

Then*p came all the princes unto Jeremiah, and asked him: and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded. So they left off speaking with him; for the matter was not perceived.
So*p Jeremiah abode in the court of the prison until the day that Jerusalem was taken: and he was there when Jerusalem was taken.
Jeremiah 39
In*p the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, came Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army against Jerusalem, and they besieged it.
And*p in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, the city was broken up.

And*p all the princes of the king of Babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, even Nergal–sharezer, Samgar–nebo, Sarsechim, Rab–saris, Nergal–sharezer, Rab–mag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of Babylon.

And*p it came to pass, that when Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all the men of war, then they fled, and went forth out of the city by night, by the way of the king's garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain.

But*p the Chaldeans' army pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho: and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him.
Then*p the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes: also the king of Babylon slew all the nobles of Judah.
Moreover*p he put out Zedekiah's eyes, and bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon.
And*p the Chaldeans burned the king's house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem.

Then*p Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard carried away captive into Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to him, with the rest of the people that remained.
But*p Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.
Now*p Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gave charge concerning Jeremiah to Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard, saying,
Take*p him, and look well to him, and do him no harm; but do unto him even as he shall say unto thee.
So*p Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard sent, and Nebushasban, Rab–saris, and Nergal–sharezer, Rab–mag, and all the king of Babylon's princes;
Even*p they sent, and took Jeremiah out of the court of the prison, and committed him unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, that he should carry him home: so he dwelt among the people.
Now*p the word of the Lord*s came unto Jeremiah, while he was shut up in the court of the prison, saying,

Go*p and speak to Ebed–melech the Ethiopian, saying, Thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee.
But*p I will deliver thee in that day, saith the Lord:*s and thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid.
For*p I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, saith the Lord.*s
Jeremiah 40

The*p word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord,*s after that Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all that were carried away captive of Jerusalem and Judah, which were carried away captive unto Babylon.
And*p the captain of the guard took Jeremiah, and said unto him, The Lord*s thy God hath pronounced this evil upon this place.
Now*p the Lord*s hath brought it, and done according as he hath said: because ye have sinned against the Lord,*s and have not obeyed his voice, therefore this thing is come upon you.

And*p now, behold, I loose thee this day from the chains which were upon thine hand. If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon, come; and I will look well unto thee: but if it seem ill unto thee to come with me into Babylon, forbear: behold, all the land is before thee: whither it seemeth good and convenient for thee to go, thither go.

Now*p while he was not yet gone back, he said, Go back also to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon hath made governor over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him among the people: or go wheresoever it seemeth convenient unto thee to go. So the captain of the guard gave him victuals and a reward, and let him go.
Then*p went Jeremiah unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and dwelt with him among the people that were left in the land.

Now*p when all the captains of the forces which were in the fields, even they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor in the land, and had committed unto him men, and women, and children, and of the poor of the land, of them that were not carried away captive to Babylon;

Then*p they came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.

And*p Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan sware unto them and to their men, saying, Fear not to serve the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.

As*p for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah to serve the Chaldeans, which will come unto us: but ye, gather ye wine, and summer fruits, and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that ye have taken.

Likewise*p when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan;
Even*p all the Jews returned out of all places whither they were driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, unto Mizpah, and gathered wine and summer fruits very much.
Moreover*p Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were in the fields, came to Gedaliah to Mizpah,
And*p said unto him, Dost thou certainly know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites hath sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay thee? But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not.

Then*p Johanan the son of Kareah spake to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly, saying, Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it: wherefore should he slay thee, that all the Jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish?
But*p Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said unto Johanan the son of Kareah, Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael.
Jeremiah 41

Now*p it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, and the princes of the king, even ten men with him, came unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and there they did eat bread together in Mizpah.

Then*p arose Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and the ten men that were with him, and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and slew him, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
Ishmael*p also slew all the Jews that were with him, even with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans that were found there, and the men of war.
And*p it came to pass the second day after he had slain Gedaliah, and no man knew it,

That*p there came certain from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even fourscore men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the Lord.*s
And*p Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went forth from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went: and it came to pass, as he met them, he said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.
And*p it was so, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah slew them, and cast them into the midst of the pit, he, and the men that were with him.

But*p ten men were found among them that said unto Ishmael, Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey. So he forbare, and slew them not among their brethren.

Now*p the pit wherein Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men, whom he had slain because of Gedaliah, was it which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with them that were slain.

Then*p Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the king's daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the Ammonites.
But*p when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,
Then*p they took all the men, and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and found him by the great waters that are in Gibeon.
Now*p it came to pass, that when all the people which were with Ishmael saw Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, then they were glad.
So*p all the people that Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah cast about and returned, and went unto Johanan the son of Kareah.
But*p Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites.

Then*p took Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, all the remnant of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after that he had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, even mighty men of war, and the women, and the children, and the eunuchs, whom he had brought again from Gibeon:
And*p they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Beth–lehem, to go to enter into Egypt,
Because*p of the Chaldeans: for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon made governor in the land.
Jeremiah 42
Then*p all the captains of the forces, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest, came near,

And*p said unto Jeremiah the prophet, Let, we beseech thee, our supplication be accepted before thee, and pray for us unto the Lord*s thy God, even for all this remnant; (for we are left but a few of many, as thine eyes do behold us:)
That*p the Lord*s thy God may shew us the way wherein we may walk, and the thing that we may do.

Then*p Jeremiah the prophet said unto them, I have heard you; behold, I will pray unto the Lord*s your God according to your words; and it shall come to pass, that whatsoever thing the Lord*s shall answer you, I will declare it unto you; I will keep nothing back from you.
Then*p they said to Jeremiah, The Lord*s be a true and faithful witness between us, if we do not even according to all things for the which the Lord*s thy God shall send thee to us.
Whether*p it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the Lord*s our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the Lord*s our God.
And*p it came to pass after ten days, that the word of the Lord*s came unto Jeremiah.
Then*p called he Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces which were with him, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
And*p said unto them, Thus saith the Lord,*s the God of Israel, unto whom ye sent me to present your supplication before him;
If*p ye will still abide in this land, then will I build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up: for I repent me of the evil that I have done unto you.
Be*p not afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom ye are afraid; be not afraid of him, saith the Lord:*s for I am with you to save you, and to deliver you from his hand.
And*p I will shew mercies unto you, that he may have mercy upon you, and cause you to return to your own land.
But*p if ye say, We will not dwell in this land, neither obey the voice of the Lord*s your God,
Saying,*p No; but we will go into the land of Egypt, where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we dwell:
And*p now therefore hear the word of the Lord,*s ye remnant of Judah; Thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; If ye wholly set your faces to enter into Egypt, and go to sojourn there;

Then*p it shall come to pass, that the sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die.

So*p shall it be with all the men that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: and none of them shall remain or escape from the evil that I will bring upon them.

For*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; As mine anger and my fury hath been poured forth upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem; so shall my fury be poured forth upon you, when ye shall enter into Egypt: and ye shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach; and ye shall see this place no more.
The*p Lord*s hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day.

For*p ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the Lord*s your God, saying, Pray for us unto the Lord*s our God; and according unto all that the Lord*s our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it.
And*p now I have this day declared it to you; but ye have not obeyed the voice of the Lord*s your God, nor any thing for the which he hath sent me unto you.
Now*p therefore know certainly that ye shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, in the place whither ye desire to go and to sojourn.
Jeremiah 43

And*p it came to pass, that when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking unto all the people all the words of the Lord*s their God, for which the Lord*s their God had sent him to them, even all these words,

Then*p spake Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men, saying unto Jeremiah, Thou speakest falsely: the Lord*s our God hath not sent thee to say, Go not into Egypt to sojourn there:
But*p Baruch the son of Neriah setteth thee on against us, for to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they might put us to death, and carry us away captives into Babylon.
So*p Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, and all the people, obeyed not the voice of the Lord,*s to dwell in the land of Judah.
But*p Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, took all the remnant of Judah, that were returned from all nations, whither they had been driven, to dwell in the land of Judah;

Even*p men, and women, and children, and the king's daughters, and every person that Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah.
So*p they came into the land of Egypt: for they obeyed not the voice of the Lord:*s thus came they even to Tahpanhes.
Then*p came the word of the Lord*s unto Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
Take*p great stones in thine hand, and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln, which is at the entry of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah;

And*p say unto them, Thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will set his throne upon these stones that I have hid; and he shall spread his royal pavilion over them.
And*p when he cometh, he shall smite the land of Egypt, and deliver such as are for death to death; and such as are for captivity to captivity; and such as are for the sword to the sword.

And*p I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt; and he shall burn them, and carry them away captives: and he shall array himself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd putteth on his garment; and he shall go forth from thence in peace.
He*p shall break also the images of Beth–shemesh, that is in the land of Egypt; and the houses of the gods of the Egyptians shall he burn with fire.
Jeremiah 44
The*p word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews which dwell in the land of Egypt, which dwell at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Memphis, and in the country of Pathros, saying,

Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Ye have seen all the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, and upon all the cities of Judah; and, behold, this day they are a desolation, and no man dwelleth therein,
Because*p of their wickedness which they have committed to provoke me to anger, in that they went to burn incense, and to serve other gods, whom they knew not, neither they, ye, nor your fathers.
Howbeit*p I sent unto you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, Oh, do not this abominable thing that I hate.
But*p they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness, to burn no incense unto other gods.
Wherefore*p my fury and mine anger was poured forth, and was kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and they are wasted and desolate, as at this day.

Therefore*p now thus saith the Lord,*s the God of hosts, the God of Israel; Wherefore commit ye this great evil against your souls, to cut off from you man and woman, child and suckling, out of Judah, to leave you none to remain;

In*p that ye provoke me unto wrath with the works of your hands, burning incense unto other gods in the land of Egypt, whither ye be gone to dwell, that ye might cut yourselves off, and that ye might be a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?

Have*p ye forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, and the wickedness of the kings of Judah, and the wickedness of their wives, and your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives, which they have committed in the land of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?
They*p are not humbled even unto this day, neither have they feared, nor walked in my law, nor in my statutes, that I set before you and before your fathers.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will set my face against you for evil, and to cut off all Judah.

And*p I will take the remnant of Judah, that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they shall all be consumed, and fall in the land of Egypt; they shall even be consumed by the sword and by the famine: they shall die, from the least even unto the greatest, by the sword and by the famine: and they shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach.
For*p I will punish them that dwell in the land of Egypt, as I have punished Jerusalem, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence:

So*p that none of the remnant of Judah, which are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall escape or remain, that they should return into the land of Judah, to the which they have a desire to return to dwell there: for none shall return but such as shall escape.

Then*p all the men which knew that their wives had burned incense unto other gods, and all the women that stood by, a great multitude, even all the people that dwelt in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,
As*p for the word that thou hast spoken unto us in the name of the Lord,*s we will not hearken unto thee.

But*p we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, as we have done, we, and our fathers, our kings, and our princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem: for then had we plenty of victuals, and were well, and saw no evil.
But*p since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine.
And*p when we burned incense to the queen of heaven, and poured out drink offerings unto her, did we make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings unto her, without our men?
Then*p Jeremiah said unto all the people, to the men, and to the women, and to all the people which had given him that answer, saying,

The*p incense that ye burned in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, ye, and your fathers, your kings, and your princes, and the people of the land, did not the Lord*s remember them, and came it not into his mind?
