So*p that the Lord*s could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings, and because of the abominations which ye have committed; therefore is your land a desolation, and an astonishment, and a curse, without an inhabitant, as at this day.

Because*p ye have burned incense, and because ye have sinned against the Lord,*s and have not obeyed the voice of the Lord,*s nor walked in his law, nor in his statutes, nor in his testimonies; therefore this evil is happened unto you, as at this day.
Moreover*p Jeremiah said unto all the people, and to all the women, Hear the word of the Lord,*s all Judah that are in the land of Egypt:

Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel, saying; Ye and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and fulfilled with your hand, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her: ye will surely accomplish your vows, and surely perform your vows.

Therefore*p hear ye the word of the Lord,*s all Judah that dwell in the land of Egypt; Behold, I have sworn by my great name, saith the Lord,*s that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, The Lord God*s liveth.
Behold,*p I will watch over them for evil, and not for good: and all the men of Judah that are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until there be an end of them.

Yet*p a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, that are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs.
And*p this shall be a sign unto you, saith the Lord,*s that I will punish you in this place, that ye may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil:

Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Behold, I will give Pharaoh–hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.
Jeremiah 45

The*p word that Jeremiah the prophet spake unto Baruch the son of Neriah, when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord,*s the God of Israel, unto thee, O Baruch;
Thou*p didst say, Woe is me now! for the Lord*s hath added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest.
Thus*p shalt thou say unto him, The Lord*s saith thus; Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land.

And*p seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the Lord:*s but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest.
Jeremiah 46
The*p word of the Lord*s which came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Gentiles;

Against*p Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh–neco king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah.
Order*p ye the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle.
Harness*p the horses; and get up, ye horsemen, and stand forth with your helmets; furbish the spears, and put on the brigandines.
Wherefore*p have I seen them dismayed and turned away back? and their mighty ones are beaten down, and are fled apace, and look not back: for fear was round about, saith the Lord.*s
Let*p not the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape; they shall stumble, and fall toward the north by the river Euphrates.
Who*p is this that cometh up as a flood, whose waters are moved as the rivers?
Egypt*p riseth up like a flood, and his waters are moved like the rivers; and he saith, I will go up, and will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and the inhabitants thereof.
Come*p up, ye horses; and rage, ye chariots; and let the mighty men come forth; the Ethiopians and the Libyans, that handle the shield; and the Ludim, that handle and bend the bow.

For*p this is the day of the Lord God*s of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be satiate and made drunk with their blood: for the Lord God*s of hosts hath a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
Go*p up into Gilead, and take balm, O virgin, the daughter of Egypt: in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured.
The*p nations have heard of thy shame, and thy cry hath filled the land: for the mighty man hath stumbled against the mighty, and they are fallen both together.
The*p word that the Lord*s spake to Jeremiah the prophet, how Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt.
Declare*p ye in Egypt, and publish in Migdol, and publish in Memphis and in Tahpanhes: say ye, Stand fast, and prepare thee; for the sword shall devour round about thee.
Why*p are thy valiant men swept away? they stood not, because the Lord*s did drive them.
He*p made many to fall, yea, one fell upon another: and they said, Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity, from the oppressing sword.
They*p did cry there, Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he hath passed the time appointed.
As*p I live, saith the King, whose name is the Lord*s of hosts, Surely as Tabor is among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.
O*p thou daughter dwelling in Egypt, furnish thyself to go into captivity: for Memphis shall be waste and desolate without an inhabitant.
Egypt*p is like a very fair heifer, but destruction cometh; it cometh out of the north.

Also*p her hired men are in the midst of her like fatted bullocks; for they also are turned back, and are fled away together: they did not stand, because the day of their calamity was come upon them, and the time of their visitation.
The*p voice thereof shall go like a serpent; for they shall march with an army, and come against her with axes, as hewers of wood.
They*p shall cut down her forest, saith the Lord,*s though it cannot be searched; because they are more than the grasshoppers, and are innumerable.
The*p daughter of Egypt shall be confounded; she shall be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.
The*p Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel, saith; Behold, I will punish the multitude of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings; even Pharaoh, and all them that trust in him:

And*p I will deliver them into the hand of those that seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants: and afterward it shall be inhabited, as in the days of old, saith the Lord.*s

But*p fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.

Fear*p thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the Lord:*s for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished.
Jeremiah 47
The*p word of the Lord*s that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza.

Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all that is therein; the city, and them that dwell therein: then the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall howl.

At*p the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong horses, at the rushing of his chariots, and at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands;

Because*p of the day that cometh to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyre and Zidon every helper that remaineth: for the Lord*s will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor.
Baldness*p is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself?
O*p thou sword of the Lord,*s how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still.
How*p can it be quiet, seeing the Lord*s hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it.
Jeremiah 48
Against*p Moab thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Woe unto Nebo! for it is spoiled: Kiriathaim is confounded and taken: Misgab is confounded and dismayed.

There*p shall be no more praise of Moab: in Heshbon they have devised evil against it; come, and let us cut it off from being a nation. Also thou shalt be cut down, O Madmen; the sword shall pursue thee.
A*p voice of crying shall be from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction.
Moab*p is destroyed; her little ones have caused a cry to be heard.
For*p in the going up of Luhith continual weeping shall go up; for in the going down of Horonaim the enemies have heard a cry of destruction.
Flee,*p save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness.
For*p because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken: and Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and his princes together.
And*p the spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape: the valley also shall perish, and the plain shall be destroyed, as the Lord*s hath spoken.
Give*p wings unto Moab, that it may flee and get away: for the cities thereof shall be desolate, without any to dwell therein.
Cursed*p be he that doeth the work of the Lord*s deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood.

Moab*p hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed.
Therefore,*p behold, the days come, saith the Lord,*s that I will send unto him wanderers, that shall cause him to wander, and shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles.
And*p Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth–el their confidence.
How*p say ye, We are mighty and strong men for the war?
Moab*p is spoiled, and gone up out of her cities, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the Lord*s of hosts.
The*p calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hasteth fast.
All*p ye that are about him, bemoan him; and all ye that know his name, say, How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!
Thou*p daughter that dost inhabit Dibon, come down from thy glory, and sit in thirst; for the spoiler of Moab shall come upon thee, and he shall destroy thy strong holds.
O*p inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that fleeth, and her that escapeth, and say, What is done?
Moab*p is confounded; for it is broken down: howl and cry; tell ye it in Arnon, that Moab is spoiled,
And*p judgment is come upon the plain country; upon Holon, and upon Jahzah, and upon Mephaath,
And*p upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon Beth–diblathaim,
And*p upon Kiriathaim, and upon Beth–gamul, and upon Beth–meon,
And*p upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.
The*p horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, saith the Lord.*s
Make*p ye him drunken: for he magnified himself against the Lord:*s Moab also shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.
For*p was not Israel a derision unto thee? was he found among thieves? for since thou spakest of him, thou skippedst for joy.
O*p ye that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole's mouth.
We*p have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart.
I*p know his wrath, saith the Lord;*s but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it.
Therefore*p will I howl for Moab, and I will cry out for all Moab; mine heart shall mourn for the men of Kir–heres.

O*p vine of Sibmah, I will weep for thee with the weeping of Jazer: thy plants are gone over the sea, they reach even to the sea of Jazer: the spoiler is fallen upon thy summer fruits and upon thy vintage.

And*p joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field, and from the land of Moab; and I have caused wine to fail from the winepresses: none shall tread with shouting; their shouting shall be no shouting.

From*p the cry of Heshbon even unto Elealeh, and even unto Jahaz, have they uttered their voice, from Zoar even unto Horonaim, as an heifer of three years old: for the waters also of Nimrim shall be desolate.
Moreover*p I will cause to cease in Moab, saith the Lord,*s him that offereth in the high places, and him that burneth incense to his gods.
Therefore*p mine heart shall sound for Moab like pipes, and mine heart shall sound like pipes for the men of Kir–heres: because the riches that he hath gotten are perished.

They*p shall howl, saying, How is it broken down! how hath Moab turned the back with shame! so shall Moab be a derision and a dismaying to all them about him.
For*p thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab.
Kerioth*p is taken, and the strong holds are surprised, and the mighty men's hearts in Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.

He*p that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, saith the Lord.*s

They*p that fled stood under the shadow of Heshbon because of the force: but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and shall devour the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
Woe*p be unto thee, O Moab! the people of Chemosh perisheth: for thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives.
Yet*p will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the Lord.*s Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
Jeremiah 49
Concerning*p the Ammonites, thus saith the Lord;*s Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?

Therefore,*p behold, the days come, saith the Lord,*s that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the Ammonites; and it shall be a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.*s

Howl,*p O Heshbon, for Ai is spoiled: cry, ye daughters of Rabbah, gird you with sackcloth; lament, and run to and fro by the hedges; for their king shall go into captivity, and his priests and his princes together.
Wherefore*p gloriest thou in the valleys, thy flowing valley, O backsliding daughter? that trusted in her treasures, saying, Who shall come unto me?

Behold,*p I will bring a fear upon thee, saith the Lord God*s of hosts, from all those that be about thee; and ye shall be driven out every man right forth; and none shall gather up him that wandereth.
And*p afterward I will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon, saith the Lord.*s
Concerning*p Edom, thus saith the Lord*s of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?
Flee*p ye, turn back, dwell deep, O inhabitants of Dedan; for I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time that I will visit him.
If*p grapegatherers come to thee, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? if thieves by night, they will destroy till they have enough.
But*p I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is spoiled, and his brethren, and his neighbours, and he is not.
Leave*p thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me.

For*p thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken; and art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink of it.
For*p I have sworn by myself, saith the Lord,*s that Bozrah shall become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all the cities thereof shall be perpetual wastes.
I*p have heard a rumour from the Lord,*s and an ambassador is sent unto the heathen, saying, Gather ye together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle.
For,*p lo, I will make thee small among the heathen, and despised among men.

Thy*p terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the Lord.*s
Also*p Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.
As*p in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the Lord,*s no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.

Behold,*p he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan against the habitation of the strong: but I will suddenly make him run away from her: and who is a chosen man, that I may appoint over her? for who is like me? and who will appoint me the time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me?

Therefore*p hear the counsel of the Lord,*s that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.
The*p earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.
Behold,*p he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah: and at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
Concerning*p Damascus. Hamath is confounded, and Arpad: for they have heard evil tidings: they are fainthearted; there is sorrow on the sea; it cannot be quiet.
Damascus*p is waxed feeble, and turneth herself to flee, and fear hath seized on her: anguish and sorrows have taken her, as a woman in travail.
How*p is the city of praise not left, the city of my joy!
Therefore*p her young men shall fall in her streets, and all the men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the Lord*s of hosts.
And*p I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall consume the palaces of Ben–hadad.
Concerning*p Kedar, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon shall smite, thus saith the Lord;*s Arise ye, go up to Kedar, and spoil the men of the east.
Their*p tents and their flocks shall they take away: they shall take to themselves their curtains, and all their vessels, and their camels; and they shall cry unto them, Fear is on every side.
Flee,*p get you far off, dwell deep, O ye inhabitants of Hazor, saith the Lord;*s for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath taken counsel against you, and hath conceived a purpose against you.
Arise,*p get you up unto the wealthy nation, that dwelleth without care, saith the Lord,*s which have neither gates nor bars, which dwell alone.

And*p their camels shall be a booty, and the multitude of their cattle a spoil: and I will scatter into all winds them that are in the utmost corners; and I will bring their calamity from all sides thereof, saith the Lord.*s
And*p Hazor shall be a dwelling for dragons, and a desolation for ever: there shall no man abide there, nor any son of man dwell in it.
The*p word of the Lord*s that came to Jeremiah the prophet against Elam in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying,
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts; Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.
And*p upon Elam will I bring the four winds from the four quarters of heaven, and will scatter them toward all those winds; and there shall be no nation whither the outcasts of Elam shall not come.

For*p I will cause Elam to be dismayed before their enemies, and before them that seek their life: and I will bring evil upon them, even my fierce anger, saith the Lord;*s and I will send the sword after them, till I have consumed them:
And*p I will set my throne in Elam, and will destroy from thence the king and the princes, saith the Lord.*s
But*p it shall come to pass in the latter days, that I will bring again the captivity of Elam, saith the Lord.*s
Jeremiah 50
The*p word that the Lord*s spake against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans by Jeremiah the prophet.

Declare*p ye among the nations, and publish, and set up a standard; publish, and conceal not: say, Babylon is taken, Bel is confounded, Merodach is broken in pieces; her idols are confounded, her images are broken in pieces.
For*p out of the north there cometh up a nation against her, which shall make her land desolate, and none shall dwell therein: they shall remove, they shall depart, both man and beast.
In*p those days, and in that time, saith the Lord,*s the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together, going and weeping: they shall go, and seek the Lord*s their God.
They*p shall ask the way to Zion with their faces thitherward, saying, Come, and let us join ourselves to the Lord*s in a perpetual covenant that shall not be forgotten.

My*p people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their restingplace.

All*p that found them have devoured them: and their adversaries said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord,*s the habitation of justice, even the Lord,*s the hope of their fathers.
Remove*p out of the midst of Babylon, and go forth out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be as the he goats before the flocks.

For,*p lo, I will raise and cause to come up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the north country: and they shall set themselves in array against her; from thence she shall be taken: their arrows shall be as of a mighty expert man; none shall return in vain.
And*p Chaldea shall be a spoil: all that spoil her shall be satisfied, saith the Lord.*s
Because*p ye were glad, because ye rejoiced, O ye destroyers of mine heritage, because ye are grown fat as the heifer at grass, and bellow as bulls;
Your*p mother shall be sore confounded; she that bare you shall be ashamed: behold, the hindermost of the nations shall be a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
Because*p of the wrath of the Lord*s it shall not be inhabited, but it shall be wholly desolate: every one that goeth by Babylon shall be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.
Put*p yourselves in array against Babylon round about: all ye that bend the bow, shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she hath sinned against the Lord.*s

Shout*p against her round about: she hath given her hand: her foundations are fallen, her walls are thrown down: for it is the vengeance of the Lord:*s take vengeance upon her; as she hath done, do unto her.

Cut*p off the sower from Babylon, and him that handleth the sickle in the time of harvest: for fear of the oppressing sword they shall turn every one to his people, and they shall flee every one to his own land.
Israel*p is a scattered sheep; the lions have driven him away: first the king of Assyria hath devoured him; and last this Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath broken his bones.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord*s of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I have punished the king of Assyria.
And*p I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.

In*p those days, and in that time, saith the Lord,*s the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.

Go*p up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod: waste and utterly destroy after them, saith the Lord,*s and do according to all that I have commanded thee.
A*p sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction.
How*p is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations!
I*p have laid a snare for thee, and thou art also taken, O Babylon, and thou wast not aware: thou art found, and also caught, because thou hast striven against the Lord.*s
The*p Lord*s hath opened his armoury, and hath brought forth the weapons of his indignation: for this is the work of the Lord God*s of hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come*p against her from the utmost border, open her storehouses: cast her up as heaps, and destroy her utterly: let nothing of her be left.
Slay*p all her bullocks; let them go down to the slaughter: woe unto them! for their day is come, the time of their visitation.
The*p voice of them that flee and escape out of the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the Lord*s our God, the vengeance of his temple.

Call*p together the archers against Babylon: all ye that bend the bow, camp against it round about; let none thereof escape: recompense her according to her work; according to all that she hath done, do unto her: for she hath been proud against the Lord,*s against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore*p shall her young men fall in the streets, and all her men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the Lord.*s
Behold,*p I am against thee, O thou most proud, saith the Lord God*s of hosts: for thy day is come, the time that I will visit thee.
And*p the most proud shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up: and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all round about him.
Thus*p saith the Lord*s of hosts; The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together: and all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go.
Their*p Redeemer is strong; the Lord*s of hosts is his name: he shall thoroughly plead their cause, that he may give rest to the land, and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.
A*p sword is upon the Chaldeans, saith the Lord,*s and upon the inhabitants of Babylon, and upon her princes, and upon her wise men.
A*p sword is upon the liars; and they shall dote: a sword is upon her mighty men; and they shall be dismayed.

A*p sword is upon their horses, and upon their chariots, and upon all the mingled people that are in the midst of her; and they shall become as women: a sword is upon her treasures; and they shall be robbed.
A*p drought is upon her waters; and they shall be dried up: for it is the land of graven images, and they are mad upon their idols.

Therefore*p the wild beasts of the desert with the wild beasts of the islands shall dwell there, and the owls shall dwell therein: and it shall be no more inhabited for ever; neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation.

Behold,*p a people shall come from the north, and a great nation, and many kings shall be raised up from the coasts of the earth.

They*p shall hold the bow and the lance: they are cruel, and will not shew mercy: their voice shall roar like the sea, and they shall ride upon horses, every one put in array, like a man to the battle, against thee, O daughter of Babylon.
The*p king of Babylon hath heard the report of them, and his hands waxed feeble: anguish took hold of him, and pangs as of a woman in travail.

Behold,*p he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan unto the habitation of the strong: but I will make them suddenly run away from her: and who is a chosen man, that I may appoint over her? for who is like me? and who will appoint me the time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me?

Therefore*p hear ye the counsel of the Lord,*s that he hath taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: surely he shall make their habitation desolate with them.
At*p the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved, and the cry is heard among the nations.
Jeremiah 51
Thus*p saith the Lord;*s Behold, I will raise up against Babylon, and against them that dwell in the midst of them that rise up against me, a destroying wind;
And*p will send unto Babylon fanners, that shall fan her, and shall empty her land: for in the day of trouble they shall be against her round about.

For*p Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord*s of hosts; though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.

Babylon*p hath been a golden cup in the Lord's*s hand, that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.
Babylon*p is suddenly fallen and destroyed: howl for her; take balm for her pain, if so be she may be healed.

Make*p bright the arrows; gather the shields: the Lord*s hath raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes: for his device is against Babylon, to destroy it; because it is the vengeance of the Lord,*s the vengeance of his temple.

Set*p up the standard upon the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set up the watchmen, prepare the ambushes: for the Lord*s hath both devised and done that which he spake against the inhabitants of Babylon.
O*p thou that dwellest upon many waters, abundant in treasures, thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness.

Every*p man is brutish by his knowledge; every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They*p are vanity, the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish.
The*p portion of Jacob is not like them; for he is the former of all things: and Israel is the rod of his inheritance: the Lord*s of hosts is his name.
Thou*p art my battle axe and weapons of war: for with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms;
And*p with thee will I break in pieces the horse and his rider; and with thee will I break in pieces the chariot and his rider;
With*p thee also will I break in pieces man and woman; and with thee will I break in pieces old and young; and with thee will I break in pieces the young man and the maid;
I*p will also break in pieces with thee the shepherd and his flock; and with thee will I break in pieces the husbandman and his yoke of oxen; and with thee will I break in pieces captains and rulers.

Set*p ye up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, prepare the nations against her, call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz; appoint a captain against her; cause the horses to come up as the rough caterpillers.

Though*p Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from me shall spoilers come unto her, saith the Lord.*s
A*p sound of a cry cometh from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans:

Jeremiah 52
Zedekiah*p was one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

But*p thou, O son of man, behold, they shall put bands upon thee, and shall bind thee with them, and thou shalt not go out among them:
And*p I will make thy tongue cleave to the roof of thy mouth, that thou shalt be dumb, and shalt not be to them a reprover: for they are a rebellious house.

But*p when I speak with thee, I will open thy mouth, and thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s He that heareth, let him hear; and he that forbeareth, let him forbear: for they are a rebellious house.
Ezekiel 4
Thou*p also, son of man, take thee a tile, and lay it before thee, and portray upon it the city, even Jerusalem:
And*p lay siege against it, and build a fort against it, and cast a mount against it; set the camp also against it, and set battering rams against it round about.

Moreover*p take thou unto thee an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between thee and the city: and set thy face against it, and it shall be besieged, and thou shalt lay siege against it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.
Lie*p thou also upon thy left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it: according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon it thou shalt bear their iniquity.
For*p I have laid upon thee the years of their iniquity, according to the number of the days, three hundred and ninety days: so shalt thou bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
And*p when thou hast accomplished them, lie again on thy right side, and thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days: I have appointed thee each day for a year.
Therefore*p thou shalt set thy face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and thine arm shall be uncovered, and thou shalt prophesy against it.
And,*p behold, I will lay bands upon thee, and thou shalt not turn thee from one side to another, till thou hast ended the days of thy siege.

Take*p thou also unto thee wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentiles, and millet, and fitches, and put them in one vessel, and make thee bread thereof, according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon thy side, three hundred and ninety days shalt thou eat thereof.
And*p thy meat which thou shalt eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day: from time to time shalt thou eat it.
Thou*p shalt drink also water by measure, the sixth part of an hin: from time to time shalt thou drink.
And*p thou shalt eat it as barley cakes, and thou shalt bake it with dung that cometh out of man, in their sight.
And*p the Lord*s said, Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.

Then*p said I, Ah Lord God!*s behold, my soul hath not been polluted: for from my youth up even till now have I not eaten of that which dieth of itself, or is torn in pieces; neither came there abominable flesh into my mouth.
Then*p he said unto me, Lo, I have given thee cow's dung for man's dung, and thou shalt prepare thy bread therewith.

Moreover*p he said unto me, Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight, and with care; and they shall drink water by measure, and with astonishment:
That*p they may want bread and water, and be astonished one with another, and consume away for their iniquity.
Ezekiel 5
And*p thou, son of man, take thee a sharp knife, take thee a barber's razor, and cause it to pass upon thine head and upon thy beard: then take thee balances to weigh, and divide the hair.

Thou*p shalt burn with fire a third part in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled: and thou shalt take a third part, and smite about it with a knife: and a third part thou shalt scatter in the wind; and I will draw out a sword after them.
Thou*p shalt also take thereof a few in number, and bind them in thy skirts.
Then*p take of them again, and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire; for thereof shall a fire come forth into all the house of Israel.
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations and countries that are round about her.

And*p she hath changed my judgments into wickedness more than the nations, and my statutes more than the countries that are round about her: for they have refused my judgments and my statutes, they have not walked in them.

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Because ye multiplied more than the nations that are round about you, and have not walked in my statutes, neither have kept my judgments, neither have done according to the judgments of the nations that are round about you;
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I, even I, am against thee, and will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the nations.
And*p I will do in thee that which I have not done, and whereunto I will not do any more the like, because of all thine abominations.

Therefore*p the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of thee, and the sons shall eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments in thee, and the whole remnant of thee will I scatter into all the winds.

Wherefore,*p as I live, saith the Lord God;*s Surely, because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also diminish thee; neither shall mine eye spare, neither will I have any pity.

A*p third part of thee shall die with the pestilence, and with famine shall they be consumed in the midst of thee: and a third part shall fall by the sword round about thee; and I will scatter a third part into all the winds, and I will draw out a sword after them.

Thus*p shall mine anger be accomplished, and I will cause my fury to rest upon them, and I will be comforted: and they shall know that I the Lord*s have spoken it in my zeal, when I have accomplished my fury in them.
Moreover*p I will make thee waste, and a reproach among the nations that are round about thee, in the sight of all that pass by.

So*p it shall be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment unto the nations that are round about thee, when I shall execute judgments in thee in anger and in fury and in furious rebukes. I the Lord*s have spoken it.

When*p I shall send upon them the evil arrows of famine, which shall be for their destruction, and which I will send to destroy you: and I will increase the famine upon you, and will break your staff of bread:
So*p will I send upon you famine and evil beasts, and they shall bereave thee; and pestilence and blood shall pass through thee; and I will bring the sword upon thee. I the Lord*s have spoken it.
Ezekiel 6
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, set thy face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them,

And*p say, Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God;*s Thus saith the Lord God*s to the mountains, and to the hills, to the rivers, and to the valleys; Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.
And*p your altars shall be desolate, and your images shall be broken: and I will cast down your slain men before your idols.
And*p I will lay the dead carcases of the children of Israel before their idols; and I will scatter your bones round about your altars.

In*p all your dwellingplaces the cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be desolate; that your altars may be laid waste and made desolate, and your idols may be broken and cease, and your images may be cut down, and your works may be abolished.
And*p the slain shall fall in the midst of you, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Yet*p will I leave a remnant, that ye may have some that shall escape the sword among the nations, when ye shall be scattered through the countries.

And*p they that escape of you shall remember me among the nations whither they shall be carried captives, because I am broken with their whorish heart, which hath departed from me, and with their eyes, which go a whoring after their idols: and they shall lothe themselves for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations.
And*p they shall know that I am the Lord,*s and that I have not said in vain that I would do this evil unto them.

Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Smite with thine hand, and stamp with thy foot, and say, Alas for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel! for they shall fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence.
He*p that is far off shall die of the pestilence; and he that is near shall fall by the sword; and he that remaineth and is besieged shall die by the famine: thus will I accomplish my fury upon them.

Then*p shall ye know that I am the Lord,*s when their slain men shall be among their idols round about their altars, upon every high hill, in all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols.
So*p will I stretch out my hand upon them, and make the land desolate, yea, more desolate than the wilderness toward Diblath, in all their habitations: and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Ezekiel 7
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Also,*p thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God*s unto the land of Israel; An end, the end is come upon the four corners of the land.
Now*p is the end come upon thee, and I will send mine anger upon thee, and will judge thee according to thy ways, and will recompense upon thee all thine abominations.
And*p mine eye shall not spare thee, neither will I have pity: but I will recompense thy ways upon thee, and thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s An evil, an only evil, behold, is come.
An*p end is come, the end is come: it watcheth for thee; behold, it is come.
The*p morning is come unto thee, O thou that dwellest in the land: the time is come, the day of trouble is near, and not the sounding again of the mountains.
Now*p will I shortly pour out my fury upon thee, and accomplish mine anger upon thee: and I will judge thee according to thy ways, and will recompense thee for all thine abominations.

And*p mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: I will recompense thee according to thy ways and thine abominations that are in the midst of thee; and ye shall know that I am the Lord*s that smiteth.
Behold*p the day, behold, it is come: the morning is gone forth; the rod hath blossomed, pride hath budded.
Violence*p is risen up into a rod of wickedness: none of them shall remain, nor of their multitude, nor of any of theirs: neither shall there be wailing for them.
The*p time is come, the day draweth near: let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn: for wrath is upon all the multitude thereof.

For*p the seller shall not return to that which is sold, although they were yet alive: for the vision is touching the whole multitude thereof, which shall not return; neither shall any strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life.
They*p have blown the trumpet, even to make all ready; but none goeth to the battle: for my wrath is upon all the multitude thereof.
The*p sword is without, and the pestilence and the famine within: he that is in the field shall die with the sword; and he that is in the city, famine and pestilence shall devour him.
But*p they that escape of them shall escape, and shall be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them mourning, every one for his iniquity.
All*p hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall be weak as water.
They*p shall also gird themselves with sackcloth, and horror shall cover them; and shame shall be upon all faces, and baldness upon all their heads.

They*p shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be removed: their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord:*s they shall not satisfy their souls, neither fill their bowels: because it is the stumblingblock of their iniquity.
As*p for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty: but they made the images of their abominations and of their detestable things therein: therefore have I set it far from them.
And*p I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil; and they shall pollute it.
My*p face will I turn also from them, and they shall pollute my secret place: for the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it.
Make*p a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.
Wherefore*p I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses: I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled.
Destruction*p cometh; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none.
Mischief*p shall come upon mischief, and rumour shall be upon rumour; then shall they seek a vision of the prophet; but the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the ancients.

The*p king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled: I will do unto them after their way, and according to their deserts will I judge them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Ezekiel 8

And*p it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I sat in mine house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, that the hand of the Lord God*s fell there upon me.

Then*p I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, as the colour of amber.

And*p he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looketh toward the north; where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.
And,*p behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the vision that I saw in the plain.

Then*p said he unto me, Son of man, lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north. So I lifted up mine eyes the way toward the north, and behold northward at the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry.

He*p said furthermore unto me, Son of man, seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? but turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations.
And*p he brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold a hole in the wall.
Then*p said he unto me, Son of man, dig now in the wall: and when I had digged in the wall, behold a door.
And*p he said unto me, Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they do here.
So*p I went in and saw; and behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, portrayed upon the wall round about.

And*p there stood before them seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel, and in the midst of them stood Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, with every man his censer in his hand; and a thick cloud of incense went up.

Then*p said he unto me, Son of man, hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord*s seeth us not; the Lord*s hath forsaken the earth.
He*p said also unto me, Turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations that they do.
Then*p he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord's*s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.
Then*p said he unto me, Hast thou seen this, O son of man? turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations than these.

And*p he brought me into the inner court of the Lord's*s house, and, behold, at the door of the temple of the Lord,*s between the porch and the altar, were about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the Lord,*s and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east.

Then*p he said unto me, Hast thou seen this, O son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? for they have filled the land with violence, and have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose.
Therefore*p will I also deal in fury: mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: and though they cry in mine ears with a loud voice, yet will I not hear them.
Ezekiel 9
He*p cried also in mine ears with a loud voice, saying, Cause them that have charge over the city to draw near, even every man with his destroying weapon in his hand.

And,*p behold, six men came from the way of the higher gate, which lieth toward the north, and every man a slaughter weapon in his hand; and one man among them was clothed with linen, with a writer's inkhorn by his side: and they went in, and stood beside the brasen altar.

And*p the glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub, whereupon he was, to the threshold of the house. And he called to the man clothed with linen, which had the writer's inkhorn by his side;

And*p the Lord*s said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.
And*p to the others he said in mine hearing, Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity:

Slay*p utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house.
And*p he said unto them, Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain: go ye forth. And they went forth, and slew in the city.

And*p it came to pass, while they were slaying them, and I was left, that I fell upon my face, and cried, and said, Ah Lord God!*s wilt thou destroy all the residue of Israel in thy pouring out of thy fury upon Jerusalem?

Then*p said he unto me, The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceeding great, and the land is full of blood, and the city full of perverseness: for they say, The Lord*s hath forsaken the earth, and the Lord*s seeth not.
And*p as for me also, mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity, but I will recompense their way upon their head.
And,*p behold, the man clothed with linen, which had the inkhorn by his side, reported the matter, saying, I have done as thou hast commanded me.
Ezekiel 10
Then*p I looked, and, behold, in the firmament that was above the head of the cherubims there appeared over them as it were a sapphire stone, as the appearance of the likeness of a throne.

And*p he spake unto the man clothed with linen, and said, Go in between the wheels, even under the cherub, and fill thine hand with coals of fire from between the cherubims, and scatter them over the city. And he went in in my sight.
Now*p the cherubims stood on the right side of the house, when the man went in; and the cloud filled the inner court.

Then*p the glory of the Lord*s went up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the Lord's*s glory.
And*p the sound of the cherubims' wings was heard even to the outer court, as the voice of the Almighty God when he speaketh.
And*p it came to pass, that when he had commanded the man clothed with linen, saying, Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubims; then he went in, and stood beside the wheels.

And*p one cherub stretched forth his hand from between the cherubims unto the fire that was between the cherubims, and took thereof, and put it into the hands of him that was clothed with linen: who took it, and went out.
And*p there appeared in the cherubims the form of a man's hand under their wings.
And*p when I looked, behold the four wheels by the cherubims, one wheel by one cherub, and another wheel by another cherub: and the appearance of the wheels was as the colour of a beryl stone.
And*p as for their appearances, they four had one likeness, as if a wheel had been in the midst of a wheel.
When*p they went, they went upon their four sides; they turned not as they went, but to the place whither the head looked they followed it; they turned not as they went.
And*p their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about, even the wheels that they four had.
As*p for the wheels, it was cried unto them in my hearing, O wheel.
And*p every one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
And*p the cherubims were lifted up. This is the living creature that I saw by the river of Chebar.
And*p when the cherubims went, the wheels went by them: and when the cherubims lifted up their wings to mount up from the earth, the same wheels also turned not from beside them.
When*p they stood, these stood; and when they were lifted up, these lifted up themselves also: for the spirit of the living creature was in them.
Then*p the glory of the Lord*s departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims.

And*p the cherubims lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight: when they went out, the wheels also were beside them, and every one stood at the door of the east gate of the Lord's*s house; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
This*p is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel by the river of Chebar; and I knew that they were the cherubims.
Every*p one had four faces apiece, and every one four wings; and the likeness of the hands of a man was under their wings.
And*p the likeness of their faces was the same faces which I saw by the river of Chebar, their appearances and themselves: they went every one straight forward.
Ezekiel 11

Moreover*p the spirit lifted me up, and brought me unto the east gate of the Lord's*s house, which looketh eastward: and behold at the door of the gate five and twenty men; among whom I saw Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people.
Then*p said he unto me, Son of man, these are the men that devise mischief, and give wicked counsel in this city:
Which*p say, It is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh.
Therefore*p prophesy against them, prophesy, O son of man.
And*p the Spirit of the Lord*s fell upon me, and said unto me, Speak; Thus saith the Lord;*s Thus have ye said, O house of Israel: for I know the things that come into your mind, every one of them.
Ye*p have multiplied your slain in this city, and ye have filled the streets thereof with the slain.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Your slain whom ye have laid in the midst of it, they are the flesh, and this city is the caldron: but I will bring you forth out of the midst of it.
Ye*p have feared the sword; and I will bring a sword upon you, saith the Lord God.*s
And*p I will bring you out of the midst thereof, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you.
Ye*p shall fall by the sword; I will judge you in the border of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
This*p city shall not be your caldron, neither shall ye be the flesh in the midst thereof; but I will judge you in the border of Israel:
And*p ye shall know that I am the Lord:*s for ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen that are round about you.

And*p it came to pass, when I prophesied, that Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. Then fell I down upon my face, and cried with a loud voice, and said, Ah Lord God!*s wilt thou make a full end of the remnant of Israel?
Again*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,

Son*p of man, thy brethren, even thy brethren, the men of thy kindred, and all the house of Israel wholly, are they unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, Get you far from the Lord:*s unto us is this land given in possession.

Therefore*p say, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.
Therefore*p say, Thus saith the Lord God;*s I will even gather you from the people, and assemble you out of the countries where ye have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
And*p they shall come thither, and they shall take away all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof from thence.
And*p I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh:
That*p they may walk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.
But*p as for them whose heart walketh after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their way upon their own heads, saith the Lord God.*s
Then*p did the cherubims lift up their wings, and the wheels beside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
And*p the glory of the Lord*s went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city.
Afterwards*p the spirit took me up, and brought me in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to them of the captivity. So the vision that I had seen went up from me.
Then*p I spake unto them of the captivity all the things that the Lord*s had shewed me.
Ezekiel 12
The*p word of the Lord*s also came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, thou dwellest in the midst of a rebellious house, which have eyes to see, and see not; they have ears to hear, and hear not: for they are a rebellious house.

Therefore,*p thou son of man, prepare thee stuff for removing, and remove by day in their sight; and thou shalt remove from thy place to another place in their sight: it may be they will consider, though they be a rebellious house.
Then*p shalt thou bring forth thy stuff by day in their sight, as stuff for removing: and thou shalt go forth at even in their sight, as they that go forth into captivity.
Dig*p thou through the wall in their sight, and carry out thereby.

In*p their sight shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulders, and carry it forth in the twilight: thou shalt cover thy face, that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.

And*p I did so as I was commanded: I brought forth my stuff by day, as stuff for captivity, and in the even I digged through the wall with mine hand; I brought it forth in the twilight, and I bare it upon my shoulder in their sight.
And*p in the morning came the word of the Lord*s unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, hath not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said unto thee, What doest thou?
Say*p thou unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s This burden concerneth the prince in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel that are among them.
Say,*p I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity.

And*p the prince that is among them shall bear upon his shoulder in the twilight, and shall go forth: they shall dig through the wall to carry out thereby: he shall cover his face, that he see not the ground with his eyes.
My*p net also will I spread upon him, and he shall be taken in my snare: and I will bring him to Babylon to the land of the Chaldeans; yet shall he not see it, though he shall die there.
And*p I will scatter toward every wind all that are about him to help him, and all his bands; and I will draw out the sword after them.
And*p they shall know that I am the Lord,*s when I shall scatter them among the nations, and disperse them in the countries.

But*p I will leave a few men of them from the sword, from the famine, and from the pestilence; that they may declare all their abominations among the heathen whither they come; and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came to me, saying,
Son*p of man, eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and with carefulness;

And*p say unto the people of the land, Thus saith the Lord God*s of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and of the land of Israel; They shall eat their bread with carefulness, and drink their water with astonishment, that her land may be desolate from all that is therein, because of the violence of all them that dwell therein.
And*p the cities that are inhabited shall be laid waste, and the land shall be desolate; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, what is that proverb that ye have in the land of Israel, saying, The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth?

Tell*p them therefore, Thus saith the Lord God;*s I will make this proverb to cease, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel; but say unto them, The days are at hand, and the effect of every vision.
For*p there shall be no more any vain vision nor flattering divination within the house of Israel.

For*p I am the Lord:*s I will speak, and the word that I shall speak shall come to pass; it shall be no more prolonged: for in your days, O rebellious house, will I say the word, and will perform it, saith the Lord God.*s
Again*p the word of the Lord*s came to me, saying,
Son*p of man, behold, they of the house of Israel say, The vision that he seeth is for many days to come, and he prophesieth of the times that are far off.
Therefore*p say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s There shall none of my words be prolonged any more, but the word which I have spoken shall be done, saith the Lord God.*s
Ezekiel 13
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy, and say thou unto them that prophesy out of their own hearts, Hear ye the word of the Lord;*s
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Woe unto the foolish prophets, that follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!
O*p Israel, thy prophets are like the foxes in the deserts.
Ye*p have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the Lord.*s
They*p have seen vanity and lying divination, saying, The Lord*s saith: and the Lord*s hath not sent them: and they have made others to hope that they would confirm the word.
Have*p ye not seen a vain vision, and have ye not spoken a lying divination, whereas ye say, The Lord*s saith it; albeit I have not spoken?
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Because ye have spoken vanity, and seen lies, therefore, behold, I am against you, saith the Lord God.*s

And*p mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies: they shall not be in the assembly of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the Lord God.*s
Because,*p even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered mortar:
Say*p unto them which daub it with untempered mortar, that it shall fall: there shall be an overflowing shower; and ye, O great hailstones, shall fall; and a stormy wind shall rend it.
Lo,*p when the wall is fallen, shall it not be said unto you, Where is the daubing wherewith ye have daubed it?
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s I will even rend it with a stormy wind in my fury; and there shall be an overflowing shower in mine anger, and great hailstones in my fury to consume it.

So*p will I break down the wall that ye have daubed with untempered mortar, and bring it down to the ground, so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall, and ye shall be consumed in the midst thereof: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Thus*p will I accomplish my wrath upon the wall, and upon them that have daubed it with untempered mortar, and will say unto you, The wall is no more, neither they that daubed it;
To*p wit, the prophets of Israel which prophesy concerning Jerusalem, and which see visions of peace for her, and there is no peace, saith the Lord God.*s
Likewise,*p thou son of man, set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesy out of their own heart; and prophesy thou against them,

And*p say, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Woe to the women that sew pillows to all armholes, and make kerchiefs upon the head of every stature to hunt souls! Will ye hunt the souls of my people, and will ye save the souls alive that come unto you?

And*p will ye pollute me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to slay the souls that should not die, and to save the souls alive that should not live, by your lying to my people that hear your lies?

Wherefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I am against your pillows, wherewith ye there hunt the souls to make them fly, and I will tear them from your arms, and will let the souls go, even the souls that ye hunt to make them fly.
Your*p kerchiefs also will I tear, and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand to be hunted; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s

Because*p with lies ye have made the heart of the righteous sad, whom I have not made sad; and strengthened the hands of the wicked, that he should not return from his wicked way, by promising him life:
Therefore*p ye shall see no more vanity, nor divine divinations: for I will deliver my people out of your hand: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Ezekiel 14
Then*p came certain of the elders of Israel unto me, and sat before me.
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, these men have set up their idols in their heart, and put the stumblingblock of their iniquity before their face: should I be enquired of at all by them?

Therefore*p speak unto them, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Every man of the house of Israel that setteth up his idols in his heart, and putteth the stumblingblock of his iniquity before his face, and cometh to the prophet; I the Lord*s will answer him that cometh according to the multitude of his idols;
That*p I may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from me through their idols.
Therefore*p say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols; and turn away your faces from all your abominations.

For*p every one of the house of Israel, or of the stranger that sojourneth in Israel, which separateth himself from me, and setteth up his idols in his heart, and putteth the stumblingblock of his iniquity before his face, and cometh to a prophet to enquire of him concerning me; I the Lord*s will answer him by myself:
And*p I will set my face against that man, and will make him a sign and a proverb, and I will cut him off from the midst of my people; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s

And*p if the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, I the Lord*s have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand upon him, and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel.
And*p they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity: the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him;
That*p the house of Israel may go no more astray from me, neither be polluted any more with all their transgressions; but that they may be my people, and I may be their God, saith the Lord God.*s
The*p word of the Lord*s came again to me, saying,

Son*p of man, when the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and will cut off man and beast from it:
Though*p these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord God.*s
If*p I cause noisome beasts to pass through the land, and they spoil it, so that it be desolate, that no man may pass through because of the beasts:
Though*p these three men were in it, as I live, saith the Lord God,*s they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered, but the land shall be desolate.
Or*p if I bring a sword upon that land, and say, Sword, go through the land; so that I cut off man and beast from it:
Though*p these three men were in it, as I live, saith the Lord God,*s they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they only shall be delivered themselves.
Or*p if I send a pestilence into that land, and pour out my fury upon it in blood, to cut off from it man and beast:
Though*p Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, as I live, saith the Lord God,*s they shall deliver neither son nor daughter; they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness.

For*p thus saith the Lord God;*s How much more when I send my four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, and the famine, and the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast?

Yet,*p behold, therein shall be left a remnant that shall be brought forth, both sons and daughters: behold, they shall come forth unto you, and ye shall see their way and their doings: and ye shall be comforted concerning the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, even concerning all that I have brought upon it.
And*p they shall comfort you, when ye see their ways and their doings: and ye shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, saith the Lord God.*s
Ezekiel 15
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, What is the vine tree more than any tree, or than a branch which is among the trees of the forest?
Shall*p wood be taken thereof to do any work? or will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon?
Behold,*p it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire devoureth both the ends of it, and the midst of it is burned. Is it meet for any work?
Behold,*p when it was whole, it was meet for no work: how much less shall it be meet yet for any work, when the fire hath devoured it, and it is burned?
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s As the vine tree among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so will I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And*p I will set my face against them; they shall go out from one fire, and another fire shall devour them; and ye shall know that I am the Lord,*s when I set my face against them.
And*p I will make the land desolate, because they have committed a trespass, saith the Lord God.*s
Ezekiel 16
Again*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations,
And*p say, Thus saith the Lord God*s unto Jerusalem; Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan; thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite.
And*p as for thy nativity, in the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all.
None*p eye pitied thee, to do any of these unto thee, to have compassion upon thee; but thou wast cast out in the open field, to the lothing of thy person, in the day that thou wast born.
And*p when I passed by thee, and saw thee polluted in thine own blood, I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live; yea, I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live.

I*p have caused thee to multiply as the bud of the field, and thou hast increased and waxen great, and thou art come to excellent ornaments: thy breasts are fashioned, and thine hair is grown, whereas thou wast naked and bare.

Now*p when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was the time of love; and I spread my skirt over thee, and covered thy nakedness: yea, I sware unto thee, and entered into a covenant with thee, saith the Lord God,*s and thou becamest mine.
Then*p washed I thee with water; yea, I thoroughly washed away thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee with oil.
I*p clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers' skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk.
I*p decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck.
And*p I put a jewel on thy forehead, and earrings in thine ears, and a beautiful crown upon thine head.

Thus*p wast thou decked with gold and silver; and thy raiment was of fine linen, and silk, and broidered work; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil: and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom.
And*p thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord God.*s
But*p thou didst trust in thine own beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renown, and pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by; his it was.
And*p of thy garments thou didst take, and deckedst thy high places with divers colours, and playedst the harlot thereupon: the like things shall not come, neither shall it be so.
Thou*p hast also taken thy fair jewels of my gold and of my silver, which I had given thee, and madest to thyself images of men, and didst commit whoredom with them,
And*p tookest thy broidered garments, and coveredst them: and thou hast set mine oil and mine incense before them.
My*p meat also which I gave thee, fine flour, and oil, and honey, wherewith I fed thee, thou hast even set it before them for a sweet savour: and thus it was, saith the Lord God.*s
Moreover*p thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured. Is this of thy whoredoms a small matter,
That*p thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them?
And*p in all thine abominations and thy whoredoms thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, when thou wast naked and bare, and wast polluted in thy blood.
And*p it came to pass after all thy wickedness, (woe, woe unto thee! saith the Lord God;)*s
That*p thou hast also built unto thee an eminent place, and hast made thee an high place in every street.
Thou*p hast built thy high place at every head of the way, and hast made thy beauty to be abhorred, and hast opened thy feet to every one that passed by, and multiplied thy whoredoms.
Thou*p hast also committed fornication with the Egyptians thy neighbours, great of flesh; and hast increased thy whoredoms, to provoke me to anger.

Behold,*p therefore I have stretched out my hand over thee, and have diminished thine ordinary food, and delivered thee unto the will of them that hate thee, the daughters of the Philistines, which are ashamed of thy lewd way.
Thou*p hast played the whore also with the Assyrians, because thou wast unsatiable; yea, thou hast played the harlot with them, and yet couldest not be satisfied.
Thou*p hast moreover multiplied thy fornication in the land of Canaan unto Chaldea; and yet thou wast not satisfied herewith.
How*p weak is thine heart, saith the Lord God,*s seeing thou doest all these things, the work of an imperious whorish woman;
In*p that thou buildest thine eminent place in the head of every way, and makest thine high place in every street; and hast not been as an harlot, in that thou scornest hire;
But*p as a wife that committeth adultery, which taketh strangers instead of her husband!
They*p give gifts to all whores: but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and hirest them, that they may come unto thee on every side for thy whoredom.

And*p the contrary is in thee from other women in thy whoredoms, whereas none followeth thee to commit whoredoms: and in that thou givest a reward, and no reward is given unto thee, therefore thou art contrary.
Wherefore,*p O harlot, hear the word of the Lord:*s

Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Because thy filthiness was poured out, and thy nakedness discovered through thy whoredoms with thy lovers, and with all the idols of thy abominations, and by the blood of thy children, which thou didst give unto them;

Behold,*p therefore I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, with all them that thou hast hated; I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy nakedness unto them, that they may see all thy nakedness.
And*p I will judge thee, as women that break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will give thee blood in fury and jealousy.

And*p I will also give thee into their hand, and they shall throw down thine eminent place, and shall break down thy high places: they shall strip thee also of thy clothes, and shall take thy fair jewels, and leave thee naked and bare.
They*p shall also bring up a company against thee, and they shall stone thee with stones, and thrust thee through with their swords.

And*p they shall burn thine houses with fire, and execute judgments upon thee in the sight of many women: and I will cause thee to cease from playing the harlot, and thou also shalt give no hire any more.
So*p will I make my fury toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry.

Because*p thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, but hast fretted me in all these things; behold, therefore I also will recompense thy way upon thine head, saith the Lord God:*s and thou shalt not commit this lewdness above all thine abominations.
Behold,*p every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.

Thou*p art thy mother's daughter, that lotheth her husband and her children; and thou art the sister of thy sisters, which lothed their husbands and their children: your mother was an Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
And*p thine elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters that dwell at thy left hand: and thy younger sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters.
Yet*p hast thou not walked after their ways, nor done after their abominations: but, as if that were a very little thing, thou wast corrupted more than they in all thy ways.
As*p I live, saith the Lord God,*s Sodom thy sister hath not done, she nor her daughters, as thou hast done, thou and thy daughters.
Behold,*p this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
And*p they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good.
Neither*p hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters in all thine abominations which thou hast done.

Thou*p also, which hast judged thy sisters, bear thine own shame for thy sins that thou hast committed more abominable than they: they are more righteous than thou: yea, be thou confounded also, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters.

When*p I shall bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, then will I bring again the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them:
That*p thou mayest bear thine own shame, and mayest be confounded in all that thou hast done, in that thou art a comfort unto them.

When*p thy sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate, then thou and thy daughters shall return to your former estate.
For*p thy sister Sodom was not mentioned by thy mouth in the day of thy pride,
