Before*p thy wickedness was discovered, as at the time of thy reproach of the daughters of Syria, and all that are round about her, the daughters of the Philistines, which despise thee round about.
Thou*p hast borne thy lewdness and thine abominations, saith the Lord.*s
For*p thus saith the Lord God;*s I will even deal with thee as thou hast done, which hast despised the oath in breaking the covenant.
Nevertheless*p I will remember my covenant with thee in the days of thy youth, and I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant.
Then*p thou shalt remember thy ways, and be ashamed, when thou shalt receive thy sisters, thine elder and thy younger: and I will give them unto thee for daughters, but not by thy covenant.
And*p I will establish my covenant with thee; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord:*s
That*p thou mayest remember, and be confounded, and never open thy mouth any more because of thy shame, when I am pacified toward thee for all that thou hast done, saith the Lord God.*s
Ezekiel 17
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, put forth a riddle, and speak a parable unto the house of Israel;
And*p say, Thus saith the Lord God;*s A great eagle with great wings, longwinged, full of feathers, which had divers colours, came unto Lebanon, and took the highest branch of the cedar:
He*p cropped off the top of his young twigs, and carried it into a land of traffick; he set it in a city of merchants.
He*p took also of the seed of the land, and planted it in a fruitful field; he placed it by great waters, and set it as a willow tree.

And*p it grew, and became a spreading vine of low stature, whose branches turned toward him, and the roots thereof were under him: so it became a vine, and brought forth branches, and shot forth sprigs.

There*p was also another great eagle with great wings and many feathers: and, behold, this vine did bend her roots toward him, and shot forth her branches toward him, that he might water it by the furrows of her plantation.
It*p was planted in a good soil by great waters, that it might bring forth branches, and that it might bear fruit, that it might be a goodly vine.

Say*p thou, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Shall it prosper? shall he not pull up the roots thereof, and cut off the fruit thereof, that it wither? it shall wither in all the leaves of her spring, even without great power or many people to pluck it up by the roots thereof.
Yea,*p behold, being planted, shall it prosper? shall it not utterly wither, when the east wind toucheth it? it shall wither in the furrows where it grew.
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,

Say*p now to the rebellious house, Know ye not what these things mean? tell them, Behold, the king of Babylon is come to Jerusalem, and hath taken the king thereof, and the princes thereof, and led them with him to Babylon;
And*p hath taken of the king's seed, and made a covenant with him, and hath taken an oath of him: he hath also taken the mighty of the land:
That*p the kingdom might be base, that it might not lift itself up, but that by keeping of his covenant it might stand.

But*p he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and much people. Shall he prosper? shall he escape that doeth such things? or shall he break the covenant, and be delivered?

As*p I live, saith the Lord God,*s surely in the place where the king dwelleth that made him king, whose oath he despised, and whose covenant he brake, even with him in the midst of Babylon he shall die.
Neither*p shall Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company make for him in the war, by casting up mounts, and building forts, to cut off many persons:
Seeing*p he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, lo, he had given his hand, and hath done all these things, he shall not escape.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s As I live, surely mine oath that he hath despised, and my covenant that he hath broken, even it will I recompense upon his own head.
And*p I will spread my net upon him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon, and will plead with him there for his trespass that he hath trespassed against me.
And*p all his fugitives with all his bands shall fall by the sword, and they that remain shall be scattered toward all winds: and ye shall know that I the Lord*s have spoken it.

Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent:

In*p the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing; in the shadow of the branches thereof shall they dwell.

And*p all the trees of the field shall know that I the Lord*s have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish: I the Lord*s have spoken and have done it.
Ezekiel 18
The*p word of the Lord*s came unto me again, saying,
What*p mean ye, that ye use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge?
As*p I live, saith the Lord God,*s ye shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Israel.
Behold,*p all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.
But*p if a man be just, and do that which is lawful and right,
And*p hath not eaten upon the mountains, neither hath lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, neither hath defiled his neighbour's wife, neither hath come near to a menstruous woman,
And*p hath not oppressed any, but hath restored to the debtor his pledge, hath spoiled none by violence, hath given his bread to the hungry, and hath covered the naked with a garment;
He*p that hath not given forth upon usury, neither hath taken any increase, that hath withdrawn his hand from iniquity, hath executed true judgment between man and man,
Hath*p walked in my statutes, and hath kept my judgments, to deal truly; he is just, he shall surely live, saith the Lord God.*s
If*p he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, and that doeth the like to any one of these things,
And*p that doeth not any of those duties, but even hath eaten upon the mountains, and defiled his neighbour's wife,
Hath*p oppressed the poor and needy, hath spoiled by violence, hath not restored the pledge, and hath lifted up his eyes to the idols, hath committed abomination,
Hath*p given forth upon usury, and hath taken increase: shall he then live? he shall not live: he hath done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him.
Now,*p lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father's sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like,
That*p hath not eaten upon the mountains, neither hath lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, hath not defiled his neighbour's wife,
Neither*p hath oppressed any, hath not withholden the pledge, neither hath spoiled by violence, but hath given his bread to the hungry, and hath covered the naked with a garment,

That*p hath taken off his hand from the poor, that hath not received usury nor increase, hath executed my judgments, hath walked in my statutes; he shall not die for the iniquity of his father, he shall surely live.
As*p for his father, because he cruelly oppressed, spoiled his brother by violence, and did that which is not good among his people, lo, even he shall die in his iniquity.
Yet*p say ye, Why? doth not the son bear the iniquity of the father? When the son hath done that which is lawful and right, and hath kept all my statutes, and hath done them, he shall surely live.

The*p soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.
But*p if the wicked will turn from all his sins that he hath committed, and keep all my statutes, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live, he shall not die.
All*p his transgressions that he hath committed, they shall not be mentioned unto him: in his righteousness that he hath done he shall live.
Have*p I any pleasure at all that the wicked should die? saith the Lord God:*s and not that he should return from his ways, and live?

But*p when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and doeth according to all the abominations that the wicked man doeth, shall he live? All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned: in his trespass that he hath trespassed, and in his sin that he hath sinned, in them shall he die.
Yet*p ye say, The way of the Lord is not equal. Hear now, O house of Israel; Is not my way equal? are not your ways unequal?
When*p a righteous man turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and dieth in them; for his iniquity that he hath done shall he die.
Again,*p when the wicked man turneth away from his wickedness that he hath committed, and doeth that which is lawful and right, he shall save his soul alive.
Because*p he considereth, and turneth away from all his transgressions that he hath committed, he shall surely live, he shall not die.
Yet*p saith the house of Israel, The way of the Lord is not equal. O house of Israel, are not my ways equal? are not your ways unequal?
Therefore*p I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways, saith the Lord God.*s Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.
Cast*p away from you all your transgressions, whereby ye have transgressed; and make you a new heart and a new spirit: for why will ye die, O house of Israel?
For*p I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord God:*s wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.
Ezekiel 19
Moreover*p take thou up a lamentation for the princes of Israel,
And*p say, What is thy mother? A lioness: she lay down among lions, she nourished her whelps among young lions.
And*p she brought up one of her whelps: it became a young lion, and it learned to catch the prey; it devoured men.
The*p nations also heard of him; he was taken in their pit, and they brought him with chains unto the land of Egypt.
Now*p when she saw that she had waited, and her hope was lost, then she took another of her whelps, and made him a young lion.
And*p he went up and down among the lions, he became a young lion, and learned to catch the prey, and devoured men.
And*p he knew their desolate palaces, and he laid waste their cities; and the land was desolate, and the fulness thereof, by the noise of his roaring.
Then*p the nations set against him on every side from the provinces, and spread their net over him: he was taken in their pit.
And*p they put him in ward in chains, and brought him to the king of Babylon: they brought him into holds, that his voice should no more be heard upon the mountains of Israel.
Thy*p mother is like a vine in thy blood, planted by the waters: she was fruitful and full of branches by reason of many waters.
And*p she had strong rods for the sceptres of them that bare rule, and her stature was exalted among the thick branches, and she appeared in her height with the multitude of her branches.
But*p she was plucked up in fury, she was cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried up her fruit: her strong rods were broken and withered; the fire consumed them.
And*p now she is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty ground.
And*p fire is gone out of a rod of her branches, which hath devoured her fruit, so that she hath no strong rod to be a sceptre to rule. This is a lamentation, and shall be for a lamentation.
Ezekiel 20
And*p it came to pass in the seventh year, in the fifth month, the tenth day of the month, that certain of the elders of Israel came to enquire of the Lord,*s and sat before me.
Then*p came the word of the Lord*s unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, speak unto the elders of Israel, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Are ye come to enquire of me? As I live, saith the Lord God,*s I will not be enquired of by you.
Wilt*p thou judge them, son of man, wilt thou judge them? cause them to know the abominations of their fathers:

And*p say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s In the day when I chose Israel, and lifted up mine hand unto the seed of the house of Jacob, and made myself known unto them in the land of Egypt, when I lifted up mine hand unto them, saying, I am the Lord*s your God;
In*p the day that I lifted up mine hand unto them, to bring them forth of the land of Egypt into a land that I had espied for them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands:
Then*p said I unto them, Cast ye away every man the abominations of his eyes, and defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt: I am the Lord*s your God.

But*p they rebelled against me, and would not hearken unto me: they did not every man cast away the abominations of their eyes, neither did they forsake the idols of Egypt: then I said, I will pour out my fury upon them, to accomplish my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.

But*p I wrought for my name's sake, that it should not be polluted before the heathen, among whom they were, in whose sight I made myself known unto them, in bringing them forth out of the land of Egypt.
Wherefore*p I caused them to go forth out of the land of Egypt, and brought them into the wilderness.
And*p I gave them my statutes, and shewed them my judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them.
Moreover*p also I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the Lord*s that sanctify them.

But*p the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness: they walked not in my statutes, and they despised my judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them; and my sabbaths they greatly polluted: then I said, I would pour out my fury upon them in the wilderness, to consume them.
But*p I wrought for my name's sake, that it should not be polluted before the heathen, in whose sight I brought them out.
Yet*p also I lifted up my hand unto them in the wilderness, that I would not bring them into the land which I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands;
Because*p they despised my judgments, and walked not in my statutes, but polluted my sabbaths: for their heart went after their idols.
Nevertheless*p mine eye spared them from destroying them, neither did I make an end of them in the wilderness.
But*p I said unto their children in the wilderness, Walk ye not in the statutes of your fathers, neither observe their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols:
I*p am the Lord*s your God; walk in my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them;
And*p hallow my sabbaths; and they shall be a sign between me and you, that ye may know that I am the Lord*s your God.

Notwithstanding*p the children rebelled against me: they walked not in my statutes, neither kept my judgments to do them, which if a man do, he shall even live in them; they polluted my sabbaths: then I said, I would pour out my fury upon them, to accomplish my anger against them in the wilderness.
Nevertheless*p I withdrew mine hand, and wrought for my name's sake, that it should not be polluted in the sight of the heathen, in whose sight I brought them forth.
I*p lifted up mine hand unto them also in the wilderness, that I would scatter them among the heathen, and disperse them through the countries;
Because*p they had not executed my judgments, but had despised my statutes, and had polluted my sabbaths, and their eyes were after their fathers' idols.
Wherefore*p I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live;

And*p I polluted them in their own gifts, in that they caused to pass through the fire all that openeth the womb, that I might make them desolate, to the end that they might know that I am the Lord.*s
Therefore,*p son of man, speak unto the house of Israel, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Yet in this your fathers have blasphemed me, in that they have committed a trespass against me.

For*p when I had brought them into the land, for the which I lifted up mine hand to give it to them, then they saw every high hill, and all the thick trees, and they offered there their sacrifices, and there they presented the provocation of their offering: there also they made their sweet savour, and poured out there their drink offerings.
Then*p I said unto them, What is the high place whereunto ye go? And the name thereof is called Bamah unto this day.
Wherefore*p say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers? and commit ye whoredom after their abominations?

For*p when ye offer your gifts, when ye make your sons to pass through the fire, ye pollute yourselves with all your idols, even unto this day: and shall I be enquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, saith the Lord God,*s I will not be enquired of by you.
And*p that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.
As*p I live, saith the Lord God,*s surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you:
And*p I will bring you out from the people, and will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered, with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out.
And*p I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.
Like*p as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you, saith the Lord God.*s
And*p I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant:

And*p I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me: I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s

As*p for you, O house of Israel, thus saith the Lord God;*s Go ye, serve ye every one his idols, and hereafter also, if ye will not hearken unto me: but pollute ye my holy name no more with your gifts, and with your idols.

For*p in mine holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord God,*s there shall all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offerings, and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all your holy things.

I*p will accept you with your sweet savour, when I bring you out from the people, and gather you out of the countries wherein ye have been scattered; and I will be sanctified in you before the heathen.
And*p ye shall know that I am the Lord,*s when I shall bring you into the land of Israel, into the country for the which I lifted up mine hand to give it to your fathers.
And*p there shall ye remember your ways, and all your doings, wherein ye have been defiled; and ye shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for all your evils that ye have committed.

And*p ye shall know that I am the Lord,*s when I have wrought with you for my name's sake, not according to your wicked ways, nor according to your corrupt doings, O ye house of Israel, saith the Lord God.*s
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, set thy face toward the south, and drop thy word toward the south, and prophesy against the forest of the south field;

And*p say to the forest of the south, Hear the word of the Lord;*s Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I will kindle a fire in thee, and it shall devour every green tree in thee, and every dry tree: the flaming flame shall not be quenched, and all faces from the south to the north shall be burned therein.
And*p all flesh shall see that I the Lord*s have kindled it: it shall not be quenched.
Then*p said I, Ah Lord God!*s they say of me, Doth he not speak parables?
Ezekiel 21
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, set thy face toward Jerusalem, and drop thy word toward the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel,
And*p say to the land of Israel, Thus saith the Lord;*s Behold, I am against thee, and will draw forth my sword out of his sheath, and will cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked.
Seeing*p then that I will cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked, therefore shall my sword go forth out of his sheath against all flesh from the south to the north:
That*p all flesh may know that I the Lord*s have drawn forth my sword out of his sheath: it shall not return any more.
Sigh*p therefore, thou son of man, with the breaking of thy loins; and with bitterness sigh before their eyes.

And*p it shall be, when they say unto thee, Wherefore sighest thou? that thou shalt answer, For the tidings; because it cometh: and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water: behold, it cometh, and shall be brought to pass, saith the Lord God.*s
Again*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, prophesy, and say, Thus saith the Lord;*s Say, A sword, a sword is sharpened, and also furbished:
It*p is sharpened to make a sore slaughter; it is furbished that it may glitter: should we then make mirth? it contemneth the rod of my son, as every tree.
And*p he hath given it to be furbished, that it may be handled: this sword is sharpened, and it is furbished, to give it into the hand of the slayer.
Cry*p and howl, son of man: for it shall be upon my people, it shall be upon all the princes of Israel: terrors by reason of the sword shall be upon my people: smite therefore upon thy thigh.
Because*p it is a trial, and what if the sword contemn even the rod? it shall be no more, saith the Lord God.*s

Thou*p therefore, son of man, prophesy, and smite thine hands together, and let the sword be doubled the third time, the sword of the slain: it is the sword of the great men that are slain, which entereth into their privy chambers.
I*p have set the point of the sword against all their gates, that their heart may faint, and their ruins be multiplied: ah! it is made bright, it is wrapped up for the slaughter.
Go*p thee one way or other, either on the right hand, or on the left, whithersoever thy face is set.
I*p will also smite mine hands together, and I will cause my fury to rest: I the Lord*s have said it.
The*p word of the Lord*s came unto me again, saying,

Also,*p thou son of man, appoint thee two ways, that the sword of the king of Babylon may come: both twain shall come forth out of one land: and choose thou a place, choose it at the head of the way to the city.
Appoint*p a way, that the sword may come to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and to Judah in Jerusalem the defenced.
For*p the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination: he made his arrows bright, he consulted with images, he looked in the liver.

At*p his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem, to appoint captains, to open the mouth in the slaughter, to lift up the voice with shouting, to appoint battering rams against the gates, to cast a mount, and to build a fort.
And*p it shall be unto them as a false divination in their sight, to them that have sworn oaths: but he will call to remembrance the iniquity, that they may be taken.

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Because ye have made your iniquity to be remembered, in that your transgressions are discovered, so that in all your doings your sins do appear; because, I say, that ye are come to remembrance, ye shall be taken with the hand.
And*p thou, profane wicked prince of Israel, whose day is come, when iniquity shall have an end,
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Remove the diadem, and take off the crown: this shall not be the same: exalt him that is low, and abase him that is high.
I*p will overturn, overturn, overturn, it: and it shall be no more, until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him.

And*p thou, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus saith the Lord God*s concerning the Ammonites, and concerning their reproach; even say thou, The sword, the sword is drawn: for the slaughter it is furbished, to consume because of the glittering:
Whiles*p they see vanity unto thee, whiles they divine a lie unto thee, to bring thee upon the necks of them that are slain, of the wicked, whose day is come, when their iniquity shall have an end.
Shall*p I cause it to return into his sheath? I will judge thee in the place where thou wast created, in the land of thy nativity.
And*p I will pour out mine indignation upon thee, I will blow against thee in the fire of my wrath, and deliver thee into the hand of brutish men, and skilful to destroy.
Thou*p shalt be for fuel to the fire; thy blood shall be in the midst of the land; thou shalt be no more remembered: for I the Lord*s have spoken it.
Ezekiel 22
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Now,*p thou son of man, wilt thou judge, wilt thou judge the bloody city? yea, thou shalt shew her all her abominations.
Then*p say thou, Thus saith the Lord God,*s The city sheddeth blood in the midst of it, that her time may come, and maketh idols against herself to defile herself.

Thou*p art become guilty in thy blood that thou hast shed; and hast defiled thyself in thine idols which thou hast made; and thou hast caused thy days to draw near, and art come even unto thy years: therefore have I made thee a reproach unto the heathen, and a mocking to all countries.
Those*p that be near, and those that be far from thee, shall mock thee, which art infamous and much vexed.
Behold,*p the princes of Israel, every one were in thee to their power to shed blood.
In*p thee have they set light by father and mother: in the midst of thee have they dealt by oppression with the stranger: in thee have they vexed the fatherless and the widow.
Thou*p hast despised mine holy things, and hast profaned my sabbaths.
In*p thee are men that carry tales to shed blood: and in thee they eat upon the mountains: in the midst of thee they commit lewdness.
In*p thee have they discovered their fathers' nakedness: in thee have they humbled her that was set apart for pollution.
And*p one hath committed abomination with his neighbour's wife; and another hath lewdly defiled his daughter in law; and another in thee hath humbled his sister, his father's daughter.
In*p thee have they taken gifts to shed blood; thou hast taken usury and increase, and thou hast greedily gained of thy neighbours by extortion, and hast forgotten me, saith the Lord God.*s
Behold,*p therefore I have smitten mine hand at thy dishonest gain which thou hast made, and at thy blood which hath been in the midst of thee.
Can*p thine heart endure, or can thine hands be strong, in the days that I shall deal with thee? I the Lord*s have spoken it, and will do it.
And*p I will scatter thee among the heathen, and disperse thee in the countries, and will consume thy filthiness out of thee.
And*p thou shalt take thine inheritance in thyself in the sight of the heathen, and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.*s
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, the house of Israel is to me become dross: all they are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead, in the midst of the furnace; they are even the dross of silver.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Because ye are all become dross, behold, therefore I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem.

As*p they gather silver, and brass, and iron, and lead, and tin, into the midst of the furnace, to blow the fire upon it, to melt it; so will I gather you in mine anger and in my fury, and I will leave you there, and melt you.
Yea,*p I will gather you, and blow upon you in the fire of my wrath, and ye shall be melted in the midst thereof.
As*p silver is melted in the midst of the furnace, so shall ye be melted in the midst thereof; and ye shall know that I the Lord*s have poured out my fury upon you.
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, say unto her, Thou art the land that is not cleansed, nor rained upon in the day of indignation.

There*p is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion ravening the prey; they have devoured souls; they have taken the treasure and precious things; they have made her many widows in the midst thereof.

Her*p priests have violated my law, and have profaned mine holy things: they have put no difference between the holy and profane, neither have they shewed difference between the unclean and the clean, and have hid their eyes from my sabbaths, and I am profaned among them.
Her*p princes in the midst thereof are like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain.
And*p her prophets have daubed them with untempered mortar, seeing vanity, and divining lies unto them, saying, Thus saith the Lord God,*s when the Lord*s hath not spoken.
The*p people of the land have used oppression, and exercised robbery, and have vexed the poor and needy: yea, they have oppressed the stranger wrongfully.
And*p I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none.
Therefore*p have I poured out mine indignation upon them; I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath: their own way have I recompensed upon their heads, saith the Lord God.*s
Ezekiel 23
The*p word of the Lord*s came again unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother:
And*p they committed whoredoms in Egypt; they committed whoredoms in their youth: there were their breasts pressed, and there they bruised the teats of their virginity.
And*p the names of them were Aholah the elder, and Aholibah her sister: and they were mine, and they bare sons and daughters. Thus were their names; Samaria is Aholah, and Jerusalem Aholibah.
And*p Aholah played the harlot when she was mine; and she doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians her neighbours,
Which*p were clothed with blue, captains and rulers, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding upon horses.
Thus*p she committed her whoredoms with them, with all them that were the chosen men of Assyria, and with all on whom she doted: with all their idols she defiled herself.
Neither*p left she her whoredoms brought from Egypt: for in her youth they lay with her, and they bruised the breasts of her virginity, and poured their whoredom upon her.
Wherefore*p I have delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians, upon whom she doted.
These*p discovered her nakedness: they took her sons and her daughters, and slew her with the sword: and she became famous among women; for they had executed judgment upon her.
And*p when her sister Aholibah saw this, she was more corrupt in her inordinate love than she, and in her whoredoms more than her sister in her whoredoms.
She*p doted upon the Assyrians her neighbours, captains and rulers clothed most gorgeously, horsemen riding upon horses, all of them desirable young men.
Then*p I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way,
And*p that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men portrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans portrayed with vermilion,
Girded*p with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea, the land of their nativity:
And*p as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.
And*p the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her with their whoredom, and she was polluted with them, and her mind was alienated from them.
So*p she discovered her whoredoms, and discovered her nakedness: then my mind was alienated from her, like as my mind was alienated from her sister.
Yet*p she multiplied her whoredoms, in calling to remembrance the days of her youth, wherein she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt.
For*p she doted upon their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.
Thus*p thou calledst to remembrance the lewdness of thy youth, in bruising thy teats by the Egyptians for the paps of thy youth.
Therefore,*p O Aholibah, thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I will raise up thy lovers against thee, from whom thy mind is alienated, and I will bring them against thee on every side;

The*p Babylonians, and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, and Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them: all of them desirable young men, captains and rulers, great lords and renowned, all of them riding upon horses.

And*p they shall come against thee with chariots, wagons, and wheels, and with an assembly of people, which shall set against thee buckler and shield and helmet round about: and I will set judgment before them, and they shall judge thee according to their judgments.

And*p I will set my jealousy against thee, and they shall deal furiously with thee: they shall take away thy nose and thine ears; and thy remnant shall fall by the sword: they shall take thy sons and thy daughters; and thy residue shall be devoured by the fire.
They*p shall also strip thee out of thy clothes, and take away thy fair jewels.
Thus*p will I make thy lewdness to cease from thee, and thy whoredom brought from the land of Egypt: so that thou shalt not lift up thine eyes unto them, nor remember Egypt any more.
For*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I will deliver thee into the hand of them whom thou hatest, into the hand of them from whom thy mind is alienated:

And*p they shall deal with thee hatefully, and shall take away all thy labour, and shall leave thee naked and bare: and the nakedness of thy whoredoms shall be discovered, both thy lewdness and thy whoredoms.
I*p will do these things unto thee, because thou hast gone a whoring after the heathen, and because thou art polluted with their idols.
Thou*p hast walked in the way of thy sister; therefore will I give her cup into thine hand.
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Thou shalt drink of thy sister's cup deep and large: thou shalt be laughed to scorn and had in derision; it containeth much.
Thou*p shalt be filled with drunkenness and sorrow, with the cup of astonishment and desolation, with the cup of thy sister Samaria.
Thou*p shalt even drink it and suck it out, and thou shalt break the sherds thereof, and pluck off thine own breasts: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord God.*s
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Because thou hast forgotten me, and cast me behind thy back, therefore bear thou also thy lewdness and thy whoredoms.
The*p Lord*s said moreover unto me; Son of man, wilt thou judge Aholah and Aholibah? yea, declare unto them their abominations;

That*p they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands, and with their idols have they committed adultery, and have also caused their sons, whom they bare unto me, to pass for them through the fire, to devour them.
Moreover*p this they have done unto me: they have defiled my sanctuary in the same day, and have profaned my sabbaths.
For*p when they had slain their children to their idols, then they came the same day into my sanctuary to profane it; and, lo, thus have they done in the midst of mine house.

And*p furthermore, that ye have sent for men to come from far, unto whom a messenger was sent; and, lo, they came: for whom thou didst wash thyself, paintedst thy eyes, and deckedst thyself with ornaments,
And*p satest upon a stately bed, and a table prepared before it, whereupon thou hast set mine incense and mine oil.

And*p a voice of a multitude being at ease was with her: and with the men of the common sort were brought Sabeans from the wilderness, which put bracelets upon their hands, and beautiful crowns upon their heads.
Then*p said I unto her that was old in adulteries, Will they now commit whoredoms with her, and she with them?
Yet*p they went in unto her, as they go in unto a woman that playeth the harlot: so went they in unto Aholah and unto Aholibah, the lewd women.
And*p the righteous men, they shall judge them after the manner of adulteresses, and after the manner of women that shed blood; because they are adulteresses, and blood is in their hands.
For*p thus saith the Lord God;*s I will bring up a company upon them, and will give them to be removed and spoiled.
And*p the company shall stone them with stones, and dispatch them with their swords; they shall slay their sons and their daughters, and burn up their houses with fire.
Thus*p will I cause lewdness to cease out of the land, that all women may be taught not to do after your lewdness.
And*p they shall recompense your lewdness upon you, and ye shall bear the sins of your idols: and ye shall know that I am the Lord God.*s
Ezekiel 24
Again*p in the ninth year, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, write thee the name of the day, even of this same day: the king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem this same day.
And*p utter a parable unto the rebellious house, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Set on a pot, set it on, and also pour water into it:
Gather*p the pieces thereof into it, even every good piece, the thigh, and the shoulder; fill it with the choice bones.
Take*p the choice of the flock, and burn also the bones under it, and make it boil well, and let them seethe the bones of it therein.
Wherefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose scum is therein, and whose scum is not gone out of it! bring it out piece by piece; let no lot fall upon it.
For*p her blood is in the midst of her; she set it upon the top of a rock; she poured it not upon the ground, to cover it with dust;
That*p it might cause fury to come up to take vengeance; I have set her blood upon the top of a rock, that it should not be covered.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Woe to the bloody city! I will even make the pile for fire great.
Heap*p on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh, and spice it well, and let the bones be burned.
Then*p set it empty upon the coals thereof, that the brass of it may be hot, and may burn, and that the filthiness of it may be molten in it, that the scum of it may be consumed.
She*p hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her: her scum shall be in the fire.
In*p thy filthiness is lewdness: because I have purged thee, and thou wast not purged, thou shalt not be purged from thy filthiness any more, till I have caused my fury to rest upon thee.

I*p the Lord*s have spoken it: it shall come to pass, and I will do it; I will not go back, neither will I spare, neither will I repent; according to thy ways, and according to thy doings, shall they judge thee, saith the Lord God.*s
Also*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, behold, I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes with a stroke: yet neither shalt thou mourn nor weep, neither shall thy tears run down.
Forbear*p to cry, make no mourning for the dead, bind the tire of thine head upon thee, and put on thy shoes upon thy feet, and cover not thy lips, and eat not the bread of men.
So*p I spake unto the people in the morning: and at even my wife died; and I did in the morning as I was commanded.
And*p the people said unto me, Wilt thou not tell us what these things are to us, that thou doest so?
Then*p I answered them, The word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,

Speak*p unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the excellency of your strength, the desire of your eyes, and that which your soul pitieth; and your sons and your daughters whom ye have left shall fall by the sword.
And*p ye shall do as I have done: ye shall not cover your lips, nor eat the bread of men.
And*p your tires shall be upon your heads, and your shoes upon your feet: ye shall not mourn nor weep; but ye shall pine away for your iniquities, and mourn one toward another.
Thus*p Ezekiel is unto you a sign: according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord God.*s

Also,*p thou son of man, shall it not be in the day when I take from them their strength, the joy of their glory, the desire of their eyes, and that whereupon they set their minds, their sons and their daughters,
That*p he that escapeth in that day shall come unto thee, to cause thee to hear it with thine ears?
In*p that day shall thy mouth be opened to him which is escaped, and thou shalt speak, and be no more dumb: and thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Ezekiel 25
The*p word of the Lord*s came again unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them;

And*p say unto the Ammonites, Hear the word of the Lord God;*s Thus saith the Lord God;*s Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity;

Behold,*p therefore I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and they shall set their palaces in thee, and make their dwellings in thee: they shall eat thy fruit, and they shall drink thy milk.
And*p I will make Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couchingplace for flocks: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
For*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Because thou hast clapped thine hands, and stamped with the feet, and rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel;

Behold,*p therefore I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and will deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen; and I will cut thee off from the people, and I will cause thee to perish out of the countries: I will destroy thee; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.*s
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen;
Therefore,*p behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on his frontiers, the glory of the country, Beth–jeshimoth, Baal–meon, and Kiriathaim,
Unto*p the men of the east with the Ammonites, and will give them in possession, that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations.
And*p I will execute judgments upon Moab; and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them;

Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Because the Philistines have dealt by revenge, and have taken vengeance with a despiteful heart, to destroy it for the old hatred;
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I will stretch out mine hand upon the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethims, and destroy the remnant of the sea coast.
And*p I will execute great vengeance upon them with furious rebukes; and they shall know that I am the Lord,*s when I shall lay my vengeance upon them.
Ezekiel 26
And*p it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first day of the month, that the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, because that Tyre hath said against Jerusalem, Aha, she is broken that was the gates of the people: she is turned unto me: I shall be replenished, now she is laid waste:

For*p thus saith the Lord God;*s When I shall make thee a desolate city, like the cities that are not inhabited; when I shall bring up the deep upon thee, and great waters shall cover thee;

Ezekiel 27
The*p word of the Lord*s came again unto me, saying,
Now,*p thou son of man, take up a lamentation for Tyre;

Thy*p borders are in the midst of the seas, thy builders have perfected thy beauty.
They*p have made all thy ship boards of fir trees of Senir: they have taken cedars from Lebanon to make masts for thee.

The*p inhabitants of Zidon and Arvad were thy mariners: thy wise men, O Tyre, that were in thee, were thy pilots.

Tarshish*p was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of all kind of riches; with silver, iron, tin, and lead, they traded in thy fairs.

Syria*p was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of the wares of thy making: they occupied in thy fairs with emeralds, purple, and broidered work, and fine linen, and coral, and agate.
Judah,*p and the land of Israel, they were thy merchants: they traded in thy market wheat of Minnith, and Pannag, and honey, and oil, and balm.
Damascus*p was thy merchant in the multitude of the wares of thy making, for the multitude of all riches; in the wine of Helbon, and white wool.

Thy*p riches, and thy fairs, thy merchandise, thy mariners, and thy pilots, thy calkers, and the occupiers of thy merchandise, and all thy men of war, that are in thee, and in all thy company which is in the midst of thee, shall fall into the midst of the seas in the day of thy ruin.

Ezekiel 28
The*p word of the Lord*s came again unto me, saying,

Son*p of man, say unto the prince of Tyre, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God:
Behold,*p thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee:
With*p thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures:
By*p thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches:
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God;

Wilt*p thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? but thou shalt be a man, and no God, in the hand of him that slayeth thee.

Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, take up a lamentation upon the king of Tyre, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty.

Thou*p hast been in Eden the garden of God; every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the emerald, and the carbuncle, and gold: the workmanship of thy tabrets and of thy pipes was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created.

By*p the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned: therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God: and I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire.

Thou*p hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee.
All*p they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never shalt thou be any more.
Again*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, set thy face against Zidon, and prophesy against it,

And*p say, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I am against thee, O Zidon; and I will be glorified in the midst of thee: and they shall know that I am the Lord,*s when I shall have executed judgments in her, and shall be sanctified in her.

Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered, and shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the heathen, then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant Jacob.

And*p they shall dwell safely therein, and shall build houses, and plant vineyards; yea, they shall dwell with confidence, when I have executed judgments upon all those that despise them round about them; and they shall know that I am the Lord*s their God.
Ezekiel 29

Ezekiel 31

There*p be the princes of the north, all of them, and all the Zidonians, which are gone down with the slain; with their terror they are ashamed of their might; and they lie uncircumcised with them that be slain by the sword, and bear their shame with them that go down to the pit.
Pharaoh*p shall see them, and shall be comforted over all his multitude, even Pharaoh and all his army slain by the sword, saith the Lord God.*s

For*p I have caused my terror in the land of the living: and he shall be laid in the midst of the uncircumcised with them that are slain with the sword, even Pharaoh and all his multitude, saith the Lord God.*s
Ezekiel 33
Again*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, speak to the children of thy people, and say unto them, When I bring the sword upon a land, if the people of the land take a man of their coasts, and set him for their watchman:
If*p when he seeth the sword come upon the land, he blow the trumpet, and warn the people;
Then*p whosoever heareth the sound of the trumpet, and taketh not warning; if the sword come, and take him away, his blood shall be upon his own head.
He*p heard the sound of the trumpet, and took not warning; his blood shall be upon him. But he that taketh warning shall deliver his soul.

But*p if the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet, and the people be not warned; if the sword come, and take any person from among them, he is taken away in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at the watchman's hand.
So*p thou, O son of man, I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; therefore thou shalt hear the word at my mouth, and warn them from me.

When*p I say unto the wicked, O wicked man, thou shalt surely die; if thou dost not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.
Nevertheless,*p if thou warn the wicked of his way to turn from it; if he do not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul.
Therefore,*p O thou son of man, speak unto the house of Israel; Thus ye speak, saying, If our transgressions and our sins be upon us, and we pine away in them, how should we then live?

Say*p unto them, As I live, saith the Lord God,*s I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?

Therefore,*p thou son of man, say unto the children of thy people, The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression: as for the wickedness of the wicked, he shall not fall thereby in the day that he turneth from his wickedness; neither shall the righteous be able to live for his righteousness in the day that he sinneth.

When*p I shall say to the righteous, that he shall surely live; if he trust to his own righteousness, and commit iniquity, all his righteousnesses shall not be remembered; but for his iniquity that he hath committed, he shall die for it.
Again,*p when I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; if he turn from his sin, and do that which is lawful and right;
If*p the wicked restore the pledge, give again that he had robbed, walk in the statutes of life, without committing iniquity; he shall surely live, he shall not die.
None*p of his sins that he hath committed shall be mentioned unto him: he hath done that which is lawful and right; he shall surely live.
Yet*p the children of thy people say, The way of the Lord is not equal: but as for them, their way is not equal.
When*p the righteous turneth from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, he shall even die thereby.
But*p if the wicked turn from his wickedness, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall live thereby.
Yet*p ye say, The way of the Lord is not equal. O ye house of Israel, I will judge you every one after his ways.
And*p it came to pass in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month, in the fifth day of the month, that one that had escaped out of Jerusalem came unto me, saying, The city is smitten.
Now*p the hand of the Lord*s was upon me in the evening, afore he that was escaped came; and had opened my mouth, until he came to me in the morning; and my mouth was opened, and I was no more dumb.
Then*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, they that inhabit those wastes of the land of Israel speak, saying, Abraham was one, and he inherited the land: but we are many; the land is given us for inheritance.
Wherefore*p say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Ye eat with the blood, and lift up your eyes toward your idols, and shed blood: and shall ye possess the land?
Ye*p stand upon your sword, ye work abomination, and ye defile every one his neighbour's wife: and shall ye possess the land?

Say*p thou thus unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s As I live, surely they that are in the wastes shall fall by the sword, and him that is in the open field will I give to the beasts to be devoured, and they that be in the forts and in the caves shall die of the pestilence.
For*p I will lay the land most desolate, and the pomp of her strength shall cease; and the mountains of Israel shall be desolate, that none shall pass through.
Then*p shall they know that I am the Lord,*s when I have laid the land most desolate because of all their abominations which they have committed.

Also,*p thou son of man, the children of thy people still are talking against thee by the walls and in the doors of the houses, and speak one to another, every one to his brother, saying, Come, I pray you, and hear what is the word that cometh forth from the Lord.*s

And*p they come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness.
And,*p lo, thou art unto them as a very lovely song of one that hath a pleasant voice, and can play well on an instrument: for they hear thy words, but they do them not.
And*p when this cometh to pass, (lo, it will come,) then shall they know that a prophet hath been among them.
Ezekiel 34
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,

Son*p of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel, prophesy, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God*s unto the shepherds; Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?
Ye*p eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock.

The*p diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick, neither have ye bound up that which was broken, neither have ye brought again that which was driven away, neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them.
And*p they were scattered, because there is no shepherd: and they became meat to all the beasts of the field, when they were scattered.
My*p sheep wandered through all the mountains, and upon every high hill: yea, my flock was scattered upon all the face of the earth, and none did search or seek after them.
Therefore,*p ye shepherds, hear the word of the Lord;*s

As*p I live, saith the Lord God,*s surely because my flock became a prey, and my flock became meat to every beast of the field, because there was no shepherd, neither did my shepherds search for my flock, but the shepherds fed themselves, and fed not my flock;
Therefore,*p O ye shepherds, hear the word of the Lord;*s

Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand, and cause them to cease from feeding the flock; neither shall the shepherds feed themselves any more; for I will deliver my flock from their mouth, that they may not be meat for them.
For*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.

As*p a shepherd seeketh out his flock in the day that he is among his sheep that are scattered; so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day.

And*p I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries, and will bring them to their own land, and feed them upon the mountains of Israel by the rivers, and in all the inhabited places of the country.

I*p will feed them in a good pasture, and upon the high mountains of Israel shall their fold be: there shall they lie in a good fold, and in a fat pasture shall they feed upon the mountains of Israel.
I*p will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord God.*s

I*p will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment.
And*p as for you, O my flock, thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I judge between cattle and cattle, between the rams and the he goats.

Seemeth*p it a small thing unto you to have eaten up the good pasture, but ye must tread down with your feet the residue of your pastures? and to have drunk of the deep waters, but ye must foul the residue with your feet?
And*p as for my flock, they eat that which ye have trodden with your feet; and they drink that which ye have fouled with your feet.
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God*s unto them; Behold, I, even I, will judge between the fat cattle and between the lean cattle.
Because*p ye have thrust with side and with shoulder, and pushed all the diseased with your horns, till ye have scattered them abroad;
Therefore*p will I save my flock, and they shall no more be a prey; and I will judge between cattle and cattle.
And*p I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.
And*p I the Lord*s will be their God, and my servant David a prince among them; I the Lord*s have spoken it.
And*p I will make with them a covenant of peace, and will cause the evil beasts to cease out of the land: and they shall dwell safely in the wilderness, and sleep in the woods.
And*p I will make them and the places round about my hill a blessing; and I will cause the shower to come down in his season; there shall be showers of blessing.

And*p the tree of the field shall yield her fruit, and the earth shall yield her increase, and they shall be safe in their land, and shall know that I am the Lord,*s when I have broken the bands of their yoke, and delivered them out of the hand of those that served themselves of them.
And*p they shall no more be a prey to the heathen, neither shall the beast of the land devour them; but they shall dwell safely, and none shall make them afraid.
And*p I will raise up for them a plant of renown, and they shall be no more consumed with hunger in the land, neither bear the shame of the heathen any more.
Thus*p shall they know that I the Lord*s their God am with them, and that they, even the house of Israel, are my people, saith the Lord God.*s
And*p ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God.*s
Ezekiel 35
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it,
And*p say unto it, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, O mount Seir, I am against thee, and I will stretch out mine hand against thee, and I will make thee most desolate.
I*p will lay thy cities waste, and thou shalt be desolate, and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.*s
Because*p thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:
Therefore,*p as I live, saith the Lord God,*s I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee: sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.
Thus*p will I make mount Seir most desolate, and cut off from it him that passeth out and him that returneth.
And*p I will fill his mountains with his slain men: in thy hills, and in thy valleys, and in all thy rivers, shall they fall that are slain with the sword.
I*p will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Because*p thou hast said, These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it; whereas the Lord*s was there:

Therefore,*p as I live, saith the Lord God,*s I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them; and I will make myself known among them, when I have judged thee.

And*p thou shalt know that I am the Lord,*s and that I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume.
Thus*p with your mouth ye have boasted against me, and have multiplied your words against me: I have heard them.
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate.

As*p thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Edom, even all of it: and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Ezekiel 36
Also,*p thou son of man, prophesy unto the mountains of Israel, and say, Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord:*s
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Because the enemy hath said against you, Aha, even the ancient high places are ours in possession:

Therefore*p prophesy and say, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Because they have made you desolate, and swallowed you up on every side, that ye might be a possession unto the residue of the heathen, and ye are taken up in the lips of talkers, and are an infamy of the people:

Therefore,*p ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God;*s Thus saith the Lord God*s to the mountains, and to the hills, to the rivers, and to the valleys, to the desolate wastes, and to the cities that are forsaken, which became a prey and derision to the residue of the heathen that are round about;

Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Edom, which have appointed my land into their possession with the joy of all their heart, with despiteful minds, to cast it out for a prey.

Prophesy*p therefore concerning the land of Israel, and say unto the mountains, and to the hills, to the rivers, and to the valleys, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my fury, because ye have borne the shame of the heathen:
Therefore*p thus saith the Lord God;*s I have lifted up mine hand, Surely the heathen that are about you, they shall bear their shame.
But*p ye, O mountains of Israel, ye shall shoot forth your branches, and yield your fruit to my people of Israel; for they are at hand to come.
For,*p behold, I am for you, and I will turn unto you, and ye shall be tilled and sown:
And*p I will multiply men upon you, all the house of Israel, even all of it: and the cities shall be inhabited, and the wastes shall be builded:

And*p I will multiply upon you man and beast; and they shall increase and bring fruit: and I will settle you after your old estates, and will do better unto you than at your beginnings: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Yea,*p I will cause men to walk upon you, even my people Israel; and they shall possess thee, and thou shalt be their inheritance, and thou shalt no more henceforth bereave them of men.
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Because they say unto you, Thou land devourest up men, and hast bereaved thy nations;
Therefore*p thou shalt devour men no more, neither bereave thy nations any more, saith the Lord God.*s

Neither*p will I cause men to hear in thee the shame of the heathen any more, neither shalt thou bear the reproach of the people any more, neither shalt thou cause thy nations to fall any more, saith the Lord God.*s
Moreover*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings: their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman.
Wherefore*p I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it:
And*p I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.
And*p when they entered unto the heathen, whither they went, they profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the Lord,*s and are gone forth out of his land.
But*p I had pity for mine holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the heathen, whither they went.

Therefore*p say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord God;*s I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went.

And*p I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the heathen, which ye have profaned in the midst of them; and the heathen shall know that I am the Lord,*s saith the Lord God,*s when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes.
For*p I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land.
Then*p will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.
A*p new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
And*p I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.
And*p ye shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.
I*p will also save you from all your uncleannesses: and I will call for the corn, and will increase it, and lay no famine upon you.
And*p I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that ye shall receive no more reproach of famine among the heathen.
Then*p shall ye remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.
Not*p for your sakes do I this, saith the Lord God,*s be it known unto you: be ashamed and confounded for your own ways, O house of Israel.
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded.
And*p the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by.
And*p they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden; and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited.
Then*p the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the Lord*s build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the Lord*s have spoken it, and I will do it.
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s I will yet for this be enquired of by the house of Israel, to do it for them; I will increase them with men like a flock.
As*p the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men: and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Ezekiel 37
The*p hand of the Lord*s was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the Lord,*s and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones,
And*p caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry.
And*p he said unto me, Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord God,*s thou knowest.
Again*p he said unto me, Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord.*s
Thus*p saith the Lord God*s unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live:
And*p I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and ye shall live; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.*s
So*p I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone.
And*p when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them.

Then*p said he unto me, Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.
So*p I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.
Then*p he said unto me, Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts.
Therefore*p prophesy and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel.
And*p ye shall know that I am the Lord,*s when I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves,
And*p shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live, and I shall place you in your own land: then shall ye know that I the Lord*s have spoken it, and performed it, saith the Lord.*s
The*p word of the Lord*s came again unto me, saying,

Moreover,*p thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions:
And*p join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.
And*p when the children of thy people shall speak unto thee, saying, Wilt thou not shew us what thou meanest by these?

Say*p unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand.
And*p the sticks whereon thou writest shall be in thine hand before their eyes.

And*p say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

And*p I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all:

Neither*p shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions: but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.
And*p David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd: they shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them.

And*p they shall dwell in the land that I have given unto Jacob my servant, wherein your fathers have dwelt; and they shall dwell therein, even they, and their children, and their children's children for ever: and my servant David shall be their prince for ever.

Moreover*p I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.
My*p tabernacle also shall be with them: yea, I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
And*p the heathen shall know that I the Lord*s do sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them for evermore.
Ezekiel 38
And*p the word of the Lord*s came unto me, saying,
Son*p of man, set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him,
And*p say, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal:

And*p I will turn thee back, and put hooks into thy jaws, and I will bring thee forth, and all thine army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed with all sorts of armour, even a great company with bucklers and shields, all of them handling swords:
Persia,*p Ethiopia, and Libya with them; all of them with shield and helmet:
Gomer,*p and all his bands; the house of Togarmah of the north quarters, and all his bands: and many people with thee.
Be*p thou prepared, and prepare for thyself, thou, and all thy company that are assembled unto thee, and be thou a guard unto them.

After*p many days thou shalt be visited: in the latter years thou shalt come into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people, against the mountains of Israel, which have been always waste: but it is brought forth out of the nations, and they shall dwell safely all of them.
Thou*p shalt ascend and come like a storm, thou shalt be like a cloud to cover the land, thou, and all thy bands, and many people with thee.
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s It shall also come to pass, that at the same time shall things come into thy mind, and thou shalt think an evil thought:
And*p thou shalt say, I will go up to the land of unwalled villages; I will go to them that are at rest, that dwell safely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates,

To*p take a spoil, and to take a prey; to turn thine hand upon the desolate places that are now inhabited, and upon the people that are gathered out of the nations, which have gotten cattle and goods, that dwell in the midst of the land.

Sheba,*p and Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish, with all the young lions thereof, shall say unto thee, Art thou come to take a spoil? hast thou gathered thy company to take a prey? to carry away silver and gold, to take away cattle and goods, to take a great spoil?
Therefore,*p son of man, prophesy and say unto Gog, Thus saith the Lord God;*s In that day when my people of Israel dwelleth safely, shalt thou not know it?
And*p thou shalt come from thy place out of the north parts, thou, and many people with thee, all of them riding upon horses, a great company, and a mighty army:

And*p thou shalt come up against my people of Israel, as a cloud to cover the land; it shall be in the latter days, and I will bring thee against my land, that the heathen may know me, when I shall be sanctified in thee, O Gog, before their eyes.
Thus*p saith the Lord God;*s Art thou he of whom I have spoken in old time by my servants the prophets of Israel, which prophesied in those days many years that I would bring thee against them?
And*p it shall come to pass at the same time when Gog shall come against the land of Israel, saith the Lord God,*s that my fury shall come up in my face.
For*p in my jealousy and in the fire of my wrath have I spoken, Surely in that day there shall be a great shaking in the land of Israel;

So*p that the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the heaven, and the beasts of the field, and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, and all the men that are upon the face of the earth, shall shake at my presence, and the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall, and every wall shall fall to the ground.
And*p I will call for a sword against him throughout all my mountains, saith the Lord God:*s every man's sword shall be against his brother.

And*p I will plead against him with pestilence and with blood; and I will rain upon him, and upon his bands, and upon the many people that are with him, an overflowing rain, and great hailstones, fire, and brimstone.
Thus*p will I magnify myself, and sanctify myself; and I will be known in the eyes of many nations, and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
Ezekiel 39
Therefore,*p thou son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, Thus saith the Lord God;*s Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal:
And*p I will turn thee back, and leave but the sixth part of thee, and will cause thee to come up from the north parts, and will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel:
And*p I will smite thy bow out of thy left hand, and will cause thine arrows to fall out of thy right hand.

Thou*p shalt fall upon the mountains of Israel, thou, and all thy bands, and the people that is with thee: I will give thee unto the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the beasts of the field to be devoured.
Thou*p shalt fall upon the open field: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord God.*s
And*p I will send a fire on Magog, and among them that dwell carelessly in the isles: and they shall know that I am the Lord.*s
So*p will I make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel; and I will not let them pollute my holy name any more: and the heathen shall know that I am the Lord,*s the Holy One in Israel.
Behold,*p it is come, and it is done, saith the Lord God;*s this is the day whereof I have spoken.

And*p they that dwell in the cities of Israel shall go forth, and shall set on fire and burn the weapons, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears, and they shall burn them with fire seven years:

So*p that they shall take no wood out of the field, neither cut down any out of the forests; for they shall burn the weapons with fire: and they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them, saith the Lord God.*s

And*p it shall come to pass in that day, that I will give unto Gog a place there of graves in Israel, the valley of the passengers on the east of the sea: and it shall stop the noses of the passengers: and there shall they bury Gog and all his multitude: and they shall call it The valley of Hamon–gog.
And*p seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them, that they may cleanse the land.
Yea,*p all the people of the land shall bury them; and it shall be to them a renown the day that I shall be glorified, saith the Lord God.*s

And*p they shall sever out men of continual employment, passing through the land to bury with the passengers those that remain upon the face of the earth, to cleanse it: after the end of seven months shall they search.
And*p the passengers that pass through the land, when any seeth a man's bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamon–gog.
And*p also the name of the city shall be Hamonah. Thus shall they cleanse the land.

And,*p thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God;*s Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood.
Ye*p shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs, and of goats, of bullocks, all of them fatlings of Bashan.
