And*p when he came to the den, he cried with a lamentable voice unto Daniel: and the king spake and said to Daniel, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God, whom thou servest continually, able to deliver thee from the lions?
Then*p said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever.
My*p God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

Then*p was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.

And*p the king commanded, and they brought those men which had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions had the mastery of them, and brake all their bones in pieces or ever they came at the bottom of the den.
Then*p king Darius wrote unto all people, nations, and languages, that dwell in all the earth; Peace be multiplied unto you.

I*p make a decree, That in every dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: for he is the living God, and stedfast for ever, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed, and his dominion shall be even unto the end.
He*p delivereth and rescueth, and he worketh signs and wonders in heaven and in earth, who hath delivered Daniel from the power of the lions.
So*p this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
Daniel 7
In*p the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head upon his bed: then he wrote the dream, and told the sum of the matters.
Daniel*p spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea.
And*p four great beasts came up from the sea, diverse one from another.

The*p first was like a lion, and had eagle's wings: I beheld till the wings thereof were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made stand upon the feet as a man, and a man's heart was given to it.

And*p behold another beast, a second, like to a bear, and it raised up itself on one side, and it had three ribs in the mouth of it between the teeth of it: and they said thus unto it, Arise, devour much flesh.
After*p this I beheld, and lo another, like a leopard, which had upon the back of it four wings of a fowl; the beast had also four heads; and dominion was given to it.

After*p this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns.

I*p considered the horns, and, behold, there came up among them another little horn, before whom there were three of the first horns plucked up by the roots: and, behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of man, and a mouth speaking great things.

I*p beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.
A*p fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
I*p beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame.
As*p concerning the rest of the beasts, they had their dominion taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time.
I*p saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.

And*p there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
I*p Daniel was grieved in my spirit in the midst of my body, and the visions of my head troubled me.
I*p came near unto one of them that stood by, and asked him the truth of all this. So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things.
These*p great beasts, which are four, are four kings, which shall arise out of the earth.
But*p the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.

Then*p I would know the truth of the fourth beast, which was diverse from all the others, exceeding dreadful, whose teeth were of iron, and his nails of brass; which devoured, brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with his feet;

And*p of the ten horns that were in his head, and of the other which came up, and before whom three fell; even of that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spake very great things, whose look was more stout than his fellows.
I*p beheld, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them;
Until*p the Ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom.
Thus*p he said, The fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be diverse from all kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces.
And*p the ten horns out of this kingdom are ten kings that shall arise: and another shall rise after them; and he shall be diverse from the first, and he shall subdue three kings.

And*p he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.
But*p the judgment shall sit, and they shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it unto the end.

And*p the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.
Hitherto*p is the end of the matter. As for me Daniel, my cogitations much troubled me, and my countenance changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.
Daniel 8
In*p the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar a vision appeared unto me, even unto me Daniel, after that which appeared unto me at the first.
And*p I saw in a vision; and it came to pass, when I saw, that I was at Shushan in the palace, which is in the province of Elam; and I saw in a vision, and I was by the river of Ulai.

Then*p I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, there stood before the river a ram which had two horns: and the two horns were high; but one was higher than the other, and the higher came up last.

I*p saw the ram pushing westward, and northward, and southward; so that no beasts might stand before him, neither was there any that could deliver out of his hand; but he did according to his will, and became great.
And*p as I was considering, behold, an he goat came from the west on the face of the whole earth, and touched not the ground: and the goat had a notable horn between his eyes.
And*p he came to the ram that had two horns, which I had seen standing before the river, and ran unto him in the fury of his power.

And*p I saw him come close unto the ram, and he was moved with choler against him, and smote the ram, and brake his two horns: and there was no power in the ram to stand before him, but he cast him down to the ground, and stamped upon him: and there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand.
Therefore*p the he goat waxed very great: and when he was strong, the great horn was broken; and for it came up four notable ones toward the four winds of heaven.
And*p out of one of them came forth a little horn, which waxed exceeding great, toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the pleasant land.
And*p it waxed great, even to the host of heaven; and it cast down some of the host and of the stars to the ground, and stamped upon them.
Yea,*p he magnified himself even to the prince of the host, and by him the daily sacrifice was taken away, and the place of his sanctuary was cast down.
And*p an host was given him against the daily sacrifice by reason of transgression, and it cast down the truth to the ground; and it practised, and prospered.

Then*p I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot?
And*p he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.
And*p it came to pass, when I, even I Daniel, had seen the vision, and sought for the meaning, then, behold, there stood before me as the appearance of a man.
And*p I heard a man's voice between the banks of Ulai, which called, and said, Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision.
So*p he came near where I stood: and when he came, I was afraid, and fell upon my face: but he said unto me, Understand, O son of man: for at the time of the end shall be the vision.
Now*p as he was speaking with me, I was in a deep sleep on my face toward the ground: but he touched me, and set me upright.
And*p he said, Behold, I will make thee know what shall be in the last end of the indignation: for at the time appointed the end shall be.
The*p ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia.
And*p the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king.
Now*p that being broken, whereas four stood up for it, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power.
And*p in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full, a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.
And*p his power shall be mighty, but not by his own power: and he shall destroy wonderfully, and shall prosper, and practise, and shall destroy the mighty and the holy people.

And*p through his policy also he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand; and he shall magnify himself in his heart, and by peace shall destroy many: he shall also stand up against the Prince of princes; but he shall be broken without hand.
And*p the vision of the evening and the morning which was told is true: wherefore shut thou up the vision; for it shall be for many days.
And*p I Daniel fainted, and was sick certain days; afterward I rose up, and did the king's business; and I was astonished at the vision, but none understood it.
Daniel 9
In*p the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, which was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans;

In*p the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord*s came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.
And*p I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes:

And*p I prayed unto the Lord*s my God, and made my confession, and said, O Lord, the great and dreadful God, keeping the covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to them that keep his commandments;
We*p have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments:
Neither*p have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets, which spake in thy name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.

O*p Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.
O*p Lord, to us belongeth confusion of face, to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against thee.
To*p the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against him;
Neither*p have we obeyed the voice of the Lord*s our God, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.

Yea,*p all Israel have transgressed thy law, even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him.

And*p he hath confirmed his words, which he spake against us, and against our judges that judged us, by bringing upon us a great evil: for under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.
As*p it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil is come upon us: yet made we not our prayer before the Lord*s our God, that we might turn from our iniquities, and understand thy truth.
Therefore*p hath the Lord*s watched upon the evil, and brought it upon us: for the Lord*s our God is righteous in all his works which he doeth: for we obeyed not his voice.
And*p now, O Lord our God, that hast brought thy people forth out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and hast gotten thee renown, as at this day; we have sinned, we have done wickedly.

O*p Lord, according to all thy righteousness, I beseech thee, let thine anger and thy fury be turned away from thy city Jerusalem, thy holy mountain: because for our sins, and for the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and thy people are become a reproach to all that are about us.
Now*p therefore, O our God, hear the prayer of thy servant, and his supplications, and cause thy face to shine upon thy sanctuary that is desolate, for the Lord's sake.

O*p my God, incline thine ear, and hear; open thine eyes, and behold our desolations, and the city which is called by thy name: for we do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies.
O*p Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, hearken and do; defer not, for thine own sake, O my God: for thy city and thy people are called by thy name.
And*p whiles I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the Lord*s my God for the holy mountain of my God;
Yea,*p whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation.
And*p he informed me, and talked with me, and said, O Daniel, I am now come forth to give thee skill and understanding.
At*p the beginning of thy supplications the commandment came forth, and I am come to shew thee; for thou art greatly beloved: therefore understand the matter, and consider the vision.

Seventy*p weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.

Know*p therefore and understand, that from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks: the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times.

And*p after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.

And*p he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate.
Daniel 10

In*p the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the thing was true, but the time appointed was long: and he understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision.
In*p those days I Daniel was mourning three full weeks.
I*p ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine in my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled.
And*p in the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel;
Then*p I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz:

His*p body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire, and his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
And*p I Daniel alone saw the vision: for the men that were with me saw not the vision; but a great quaking fell upon them, so that they fled to hide themselves.
Therefore*p I was left alone, and saw this great vision, and there remained no strength in me: for my comeliness was turned in me into corruption, and I retained no strength.
Yet*p heard I the voice of his words: and when I heard the voice of his words, then was I in a deep sleep on my face, and my face toward the ground.
And,*p behold, an hand touched me, which set me upon my knees and upon the palms of my hands.

And*p he said unto me, O Daniel, a man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak unto thee, and stand upright: for unto thee am I now sent. And when he had spoken this word unto me, I stood trembling.

Then*p said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words.
But*p the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days: but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia.
Now*p I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days.
And*p when he had spoken such words unto me, I set my face toward the ground, and I became dumb.

And,*p behold, one like the similitude of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spake, and said unto him that stood before me, O my lord, by the vision my sorrows are turned upon me, and I have retained no strength.
For*p how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? for as for me, straightway there remained no strength in me, neither is there breath left in me.
Then*p there came again and touched me one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened me,

And*p said, O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace be unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong. And when he had spoken unto me, I was strengthened, and said, Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me.
Then*p said he, Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee? and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come.
But*p I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture of truth: and there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael your prince.
Daniel 11
Also*p I in the first year of Darius the Mede, even I, stood to confirm and to strengthen him.

And*p now will I shew thee the truth. Behold, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all: and by his strength through his riches he shall stir up all against the realm of Grecia.
And*p a mighty king shall stand up, that shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will.

And*p when he shall stand up, his kingdom shall be broken, and shall be divided toward the four winds of heaven; and not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion which he ruled: for his kingdom shall be plucked up, even for others beside those.
And*p the king of the south shall be strong, and one of his princes; and he shall be strong above him, and have dominion; his dominion shall be a great dominion.

And*p in the end of years they shall join themselves together; for the king's daughter of the south shall come to the king of the north to make an agreement: but she shall not retain the power of the arm; neither shall he stand, nor his arm: but she shall be given up, and they that brought her, and he that begat her, and he that strengthened her in these times.

But*p out of a branch of her roots shall one stand up in his estate, which shall come with an army, and shall enter into the fortress of the king of the north, and shall deal against them, and shall prevail:
And*p shall also carry captives into Egypt their gods, with their princes, and with their precious vessels of silver and of gold; and he shall continue more years than the king of the north.
So*p the king of the south shall come into his kingdom, and shall return into his own land.

But*p his sons shall be stirred up, and shall assemble a multitude of great forces: and one shall certainly come, and overflow, and pass through: then shall he return, and be stirred up, even to his fortress.

And*p the king of the south shall be moved with choler, and shall come forth and fight with him, even with the king of the north: and he shall set forth a great multitude; but the multitude shall be given into his hand.
And*p when he hath taken away the multitude, his heart shall be lifted up; and he shall cast down many ten thousands: but he shall not be strengthened by it.
For*p the king of the north shall return, and shall set forth a multitude greater than the former, and shall certainly come after certain years with a great army and with much riches.
And*p in those times there shall many stand up against the king of the south: also the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision; but they shall fall.

So*p the king of the north shall come, and cast up a mount, and take the most fenced cities: and the arms of the south shall not withstand, neither his chosen people, neither shall there be any strength to withstand.
But*p he that cometh against him shall do according to his own will, and none shall stand before him: and he shall stand in the glorious land, which by his hand shall be consumed.

He*p shall also set his face to enter with the strength of his whole kingdom, and upright ones with him; thus shall he do: and he shall give him the daughter of women, corrupting her: but she shall not stand on his side, neither be for him.

After*p this shall he turn his face unto the isles, and shall take many: but a prince for his own behalf shall cause the reproach offered by him to cease; without his own reproach he shall cause it to turn upon him.
Then*p he shall turn his face toward the fort of his own land: but he shall stumble and fall, and not be found.
Then*p shall stand up in his estate a raiser of taxes in the glory of the kingdom: but within few days he shall be destroyed, neither in anger, nor in battle.
And*p in his estate shall stand up a vile person, to whom they shall not give the honour of the kingdom: but he shall come in peaceably, and obtain the kingdom by flatteries.
And*p with the arms of a flood shall they be overflown from before him, and shall be broken; yea, also the prince of the covenant.
And*p after the league made with him he shall work deceitfully: for he shall come up, and shall become strong with a small people.

He*p shall enter peaceably even upon the fattest places of the province; and he shall do that which his fathers have not done, nor his fathers' fathers; he shall scatter among them the prey, and spoil, and riches: yea, and he shall forecast his devices against the strong holds, even for a time.

And*p he shall stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall be stirred up to battle with a very great and mighty army; but he shall not stand: for they shall forecast devices against him.
Yea,*p they that feed of the portion of his meat shall destroy him, and his army shall overflow: and many shall fall down slain.
And*p both these kings' hearts shall be to do mischief, and they shall speak lies at one table; but it shall not prosper: for yet the end shall be at the time appointed.
Then*p shall he return into his land with great riches; and his heart shall be against the holy covenant; and he shall do exploits, and return to his own land.
At*p the time appointed he shall return, and come toward the south; but it shall not be as the former, or as the latter.

For*p the ships of Kittim shall come against him: therefore he shall be grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant.
And*p arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate.
And*p such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he corrupt by flatteries: but the people that do know their God shall be strong, and do exploits.
And*p they that understand among the people shall instruct many: yet they shall fall by the sword, and by flame, by captivity, and by spoil, many days.
Now*p when they shall fall, they shall be holpen with a little help: but many shall cleave to them with flatteries.
And*p some of them of understanding shall fall, to try them, and to purge, and to make them white, even to the time of the end: because it is yet for a time appointed.

And*p the king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvellous things against the God of gods, and shall prosper till the indignation be accomplished: for that that is determined shall be done.
Neither*p shall he regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god: for he shall magnify himself above all.
But*p in his estate shall he honour the God of forces: and a god whom his fathers knew not shall he honour with gold, and silver, and with precious stones, and pleasant things.
Thus*p shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory: and he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain.

And*p at the time of the end shall the king of the south push at him: and the king of the north shall come against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall enter into the countries, and shall overflow and pass over.
He*p shall enter also into the glorious land, and many countries shall be overthrown: but these shall escape out of his hand, even Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.
He*p shall stretch forth his hand also upon the countries: and the land of Egypt shall not escape.
But*p he shall have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt: and the Libyans and the Ethiopians shall be at his steps.
But*p tidings out of the east and out of the north shall trouble him: therefore he shall go forth with great fury to destroy, and utterly to make away many.
And*p he shall plant the tabernacles of his palace between the seas in the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and none shall help him.
Daniel 12

And*p at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.
And*p many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
And*p they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.
But*p thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased.
Then*p I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river.
And*p one said to the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?

And*p I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.
And*p I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things?
And*p he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end.
Many*p shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.
And*p from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.
Blessed*p is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days.
But*p go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.
Hosea 1
The*p word of the Lord*s that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

The*p beginning of the word of the Lord*s by Hosea. And the Lord*s said to Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the Lord.*s
So*p he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; which conceived, and bare him a son.

And*p the Lord*s said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.
And*p it shall come to pass at that day, that I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.
And*p she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And God said unto him, Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.
But*p I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord*s their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.
Now*p when she had weaned Lo–ruhamah, she conceived, and bare a son.
Then*p said God, Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.

Yet*p the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
Then*p shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.
Hosea 2
Say*p ye unto your brethren, Ammi; and to your sisters, Ru–hamah.
Plead*p with your mother, plead: for she is not my wife, neither am I her husband: let her therefore put away her whoredoms out of her sight, and her adulteries from between her breasts;
Lest*p I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she was born, and make her as a wilderness, and set her like a dry land, and slay her with thirst.
And*p I will not have mercy upon her children; for they be the children of whoredoms.

For*p their mother hath played the harlot: she that conceived them hath done shamefully: for she said, I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oil and my drink.
Therefore,*p behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and make a wall, that she shall not find her paths.

And*p she shall follow after her lovers, but she shall not overtake them; and she shall seek them, but shall not find them: then shall she say, I will go and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than now.
For*p she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal.
Therefore*p will I return, and take away my corn in the time thereof, and my wine in the season thereof, and will recover my wool and my flax given to cover her nakedness.
And*p now will I discover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and none shall deliver her out of mine hand.
I*p will also cause all her mirth to cease, her feast days, her new moons, and her sabbaths, and all her solemn feasts.
And*p I will destroy her vines and her fig trees, whereof she hath said, These are my rewards that my lovers have given me: and I will make them a forest, and the beasts of the field shall eat them.

And*p I will visit upon her the days of Baalim, wherein she burned incense to them, and she decked herself with her earrings and her jewels, and she went after her lovers, and forgat me, saith the Lord.*s
Therefore,*p behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her.

And*p I will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope: and she shall sing there, as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
And*p it shall be at that day, saith the Lord,*s that thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali.
For*p I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth, and they shall no more be remembered by their name.

And*p in that day will I make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven, and with the creeping things of the ground: and I will break the bow and the sword and the battle out of the earth, and will make them to lie down safely.
And*p I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.
I*p will even betroth thee unto me in faithfulness: and thou shalt know the Lord.*s
And*p it shall come to pass in that day, I will hear, saith the Lord,*s I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth;
And*p the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oil; and they shall hear Jezreel.

And*p I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.
Hosea 3

Then*p said the Lord*s unto me, Go yet, love a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress, according to the love of the Lord*s toward the children of Israel, who look to other gods, and love flagons of wine.
So*p I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley:
And*p I said unto her, Thou shalt abide for me many days; thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt not be for another man: so will I also be for thee.
For*p the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim:
Afterward*p shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord*s their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord*s and his goodness in the latter days.
Hosea 4
Hear*p the word of the Lord,*s ye children of Israel: for the Lord*s hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.
By*p swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.
Therefore*p shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away.
Yet*p let no man strive, nor reprove another: for thy people are as they that strive with the priest.
Therefore*p shalt thou fall in the day, and the prophet also shall fall with thee in the night, and I will destroy thy mother.

My*p people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
As*p they were increased, so they sinned against me: therefore will I change their glory into shame.
They*p eat up the sin of my people, and they set their heart on their iniquity.
And*p there shall be, like people, like priest: and I will punish them for their ways, and reward them their doings.
For*p they shall eat, and not have enough: they shall commit whoredom, and shall not increase: because they have left off to take heed to the Lord.*s
Whoredom*p and wine and new wine take away the heart.
My*p people ask counsel at their stocks, and their staff declareth unto them: for the spirit of whoredoms hath caused them to err, and they have gone a whoring from under their God.

They*p sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills, under oaks and poplars and elms, because the shadow thereof is good: therefore your daughters shall commit whoredom, and your spouses shall commit adultery.

I*p will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom, nor your spouses when they commit adultery: for themselves are separated with whores, and they sacrifice with harlots: therefore the people that doth not understand shall fall.
Though*p thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah offend; and come not ye unto Gilgal, neither go ye up to Beth–aven, nor swear, The Lord*s liveth.
For*p Israel slideth back as a backsliding heifer: now the Lord*s will feed them as a lamb in a large place.
Ephraim*p is joined to idols: let him alone.
Their*p drink is sour: they have committed whoredom continually: her rulers with shame do love, Give ye.
The*p wind hath bound her up in her wings, and they shall be ashamed because of their sacrifices.
Hosea 5
Hear*p ye this, O priests; and hearken, ye house of Israel; and give ye ear, O house of the king; for judgment is toward you, because ye have been a snare on Mizpah, and a net spread upon Tabor.
And*p the revolters are profound to make slaughter, though I have been a rebuker of them all.
I*p know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me: for now, O Ephraim, thou committest whoredom, and Israel is defiled.
They*p will not frame their doings to turn unto their God: for the spirit of whoredoms is in the midst of them, and they have not known the Lord.*s
And*p the pride of Israel doth testify to his face: therefore shall Israel and Ephraim fall in their iniquity; Judah also shall fall with them.
They*p shall go with their flocks and with their herds to seek the Lord;*s but they shall not find him; he hath withdrawn himself from them.
They*p have dealt treacherously against the Lord:*s for they have begotten strange children: now shall a month devour them with their portions.
Blow*p ye the cornet in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah: cry aloud at Beth–aven, after thee, O Benjamin.
Ephraim*p shall be desolate in the day of rebuke: among the tribes of Israel have I made known that which shall surely be.
The*p princes of Judah were like them that remove the bound: therefore I will pour out my wrath upon them like water.
Ephraim*p is oppressed and broken in judgment, because he willingly walked after the commandment.
Therefore*p will I be unto Ephraim as a moth, and to the house of Judah as rottenness.
When*p Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah saw his wound, then went Ephraim to the Assyrian, and sent to king Jareb: yet could he not heal you, nor cure you of your wound.
For*p I will be unto Ephraim as a lion, and as a young lion to the house of Judah: I, even I, will tear and go away; I will take away, and none shall rescue him.
I*p will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.
Hosea 6
Come,*p and let us return unto the Lord:*s for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up.
After*p two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.
Then*p shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord:*s his going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.
O*p Ephraim, what shall I do unto thee? O Judah, what shall I do unto thee? for your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the early dew it goeth away.
Therefore*p have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and thy judgments are as the light that goeth forth.
For*p I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
But*p they like men have transgressed the covenant: there have they dealt treacherously against me.
Gilead*p is a city of them that work iniquity, and is polluted with blood.
And*p as troops of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murder in the way by consent: for they commit lewdness.
I*p have seen an horrible thing in the house of Israel: there is the whoredom of Ephraim, Israel is defiled.
Also,*p O Judah, he hath set an harvest for thee, when I returned the captivity of my people.
Hosea 7

When*p I would have healed Israel, then the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered, and the wickedness of Samaria: for they commit falsehood; and the thief cometh in, and the troop of robbers spoileth without.
And*p they consider not in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness: now their own doings have beset them about; they are before my face.
They*p make the king glad with their wickedness, and the princes with their lies.
They*p are all adulterers, as an oven heated by the baker, who ceaseth from raising after he hath kneaded the dough, until it be leavened.
In*p the day of our king the princes have made him sick with bottles of wine; he stretched out his hand with scorners.
For*p they have made ready their heart like an oven, whiles they lie in wait: their baker sleepeth all the night; in the morning it burneth as a flaming fire.
They*p are all hot as an oven, and have devoured their judges; all their kings are fallen: there is none among them that calleth unto me.
Ephraim,*p he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned.
Strangers*p have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not: yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not.
And*p the pride of Israel testifieth to his face: and they do not return to the Lord*s their God, nor seek him for all this.
Ephraim*p also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.
When*p they shall go, I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven; I will chastise them, as their congregation hath heard.
Woe*p unto them! for they have fled from me: destruction unto them! because they have transgressed against me: though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me.
And*p they have not cried unto me with their heart, when they howled upon their beds: they assemble themselves for corn and wine, and they rebel against me.
Though*p I have bound and strengthened their arms, yet do they imagine mischief against me.
They*p return, but not to the most High: they are like a deceitful bow: their princes shall fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue: this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt.
Hosea 8
Set*p the trumpet to thy mouth. He shall come as an eagle against the house of the Lord,*s because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law.
Israel*p shall cry unto me, My God, we know thee.
Israel*p hath cast off the thing that is good: the enemy shall pursue him.
They*p have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not: of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.
Thy*p calf, O Samaria, hath cast thee off; mine anger is kindled against them: how long will it be ere they attain to innocency?
For*p from Israel was it also: the workman made it; therefore it is not God: but the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.
For*p they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: it hath no stalk: the bud shall yield no meal: if so be it yield, the strangers shall swallow it up.
Israel*p is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.
For*p they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath hired lovers.
Yea,*p though they have hired among the nations, now will I gather them, and they shall sorrow a little for the burden of the king of princes.

Who*p had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains:
Because*p that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.
And*p always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.
But*p when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshipped him,
And*p cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the most high God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not.
For*p he said unto him, Come*r out*r of*r the*r man,*r thou*r unclean*r spirit.*r
And*p he asked him, What*r is*r thy*r name?*r And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.
And*p he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
Now*p there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding.
And*p all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.

And*p forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.
And*p they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done.
And*p they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
And*p they that saw it told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and also concerning the swine.
And*p they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.
And*p when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him.

Howbeit*p Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go*r home*r to*r thy*r friends,*r and*r tell*r them*r how*r great*r things*r the*r Lord*r hath*r done*r for*r thee,*r and*r hath*r had*r compassion*r on*r thee.*r
And*p he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel.
And*p when Jesus was passed over again by ship unto the other side, much people gathered unto him: and he was nigh unto the sea.
And,*p behold, there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet,
And*p besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray thee, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live.
And*p Jesus went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him.
And*p a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,
And*p had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,
When*p she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment.
For*p she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.
And*p straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague.
And*p Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who*r touched*r my*r clothes?*r
And*p his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who*r touched*r me?*r
And*p he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.
But*p the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
And*p he said unto her, Daughter,*r thy*r faith*r hath*r made*r thee*r whole;*r go*r in*r peace,*r and*r be*r whole*r of*r thy*r plague.*r
While*p he yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue's house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further?
As*p soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be*r not*r afraid,*r only*r believe.*r
And*p he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
And*p he cometh to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.
And*p when he was come in, he saith unto them, Why*r make*r ye*r this*r ado,*r and*r weep?*r the*r damsel*r is*r not*r dead,*r but*r sleepeth.*r
And*p they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying.
And*p he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha*r cumi;*r which is, being interpreted, Damsel,*r I*r say*r unto*r thee,*r arise.*r
And*p straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.
And*p he charged them straitly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.
Mark 6
And*p he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.

And*p when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?
Is*p not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Judas, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.
But*p Jesus said unto them, A*r prophet*r is*r not*r without*r honour,*r but*r in*r his*r own*r country,*r and*r among*r his*r own*r kin,*r and*r in*r his*r own*r house.*r
And*p he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.
And*p he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.
And*p he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits;
And*p commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse:
But*p be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.
And*p he said unto them, In*r what*r place*r soever*r ye*r enter*r into*r an*r house,*r there*r abide*r till*r ye*r depart*r from*r that*r place.*r

And*rp whosoever*r shall*r not*r receive*r you,*r nor*r hear*r you,*r when*r ye*r depart*r thence,*r shake*r off*r the*r dust*r under*r your*r feet*r for*r a*r testimony*r against*r them.*r Verily*r I*r say*r unto*r you,*r It*r shall*r be*r more*r tolerable*r for*r Sodom*r and*r Gomorrha*r in*r the*r day*r of*r judgment,*r than*r for*r that*r city.*r
And*p they went out, and preached that men should repent.
And*p they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.
And*p king Herod heard of him; (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.
Others*p said, That it is Elias. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.
But*p when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.
For*p Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife: for he had married her.
For*p John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife.
Therefore*p Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:
For*p Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
And*p when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;
And*p when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
And*p he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.
And*p she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
And*p she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.
And*p the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath's sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.
And*p immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
And*p brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
And*p when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
And*p the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
And*p he said unto them, Come*r ye*r yourselves*r apart*r into*r a*r desert*r place,*r and*r rest*r a*r while:*r for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
And*p they departed into a desert place by ship privately.
And*p the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran afoot thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together unto him.
And*p Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.
And*p when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed:
Send*p them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat.
He*p answered and said unto them, Give*r ye*r them*r to*r eat.*r And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat?
He*p saith unto them, How*r many*r loaves*r have*r ye?*r go*r and*r see.*r And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.
And*p he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.
And*p they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.

And*p when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.
And*p they did all eat, and were filled.
And*p they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
And*p they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.
And*p straightway he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.
And*p when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.
And*p when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.
And*p he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
But*p when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:
For*p they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and saith unto them, Be*r of*r good*r cheer:*r it*r is*r I;*r be*r not*r afraid.*r
And*p he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.
For*p they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened.
And*p when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.
And*p when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,
And*p ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.

And*p whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.
Mark 7
Then*p came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.
And*p when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.
For*p the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.

And*p when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.
Then*p the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?

He*p answered and said unto them, Well*r hath*r Esaias*r prophesied*r of*r you*r hypocrites,*r as*r it*r is*r written,*r This*r people*r honoureth*r me*r with*r their*r lips,*r but*r their*r heart*r is*r far*r from*r me.*r
Howbeit*rp in*r vain*r do*r they*r worship*r me,*r teaching*r for*r doctrines*r the*r commandments*r of*r men.*r
For*rp laying*r aside*r the*r commandment*r of*r God,*r ye*r hold*r the*r tradition*r of*r men,*r as*r the*r washing*r of*r pots*r and*r cups:*r and*r many*r other*r such*r like*r things*r ye*r do.*r
And*p he said unto them, Full*r well*r ye*r reject*r the*r commandment*r of*r God,*r that*r ye*r may*r keep*r your*r own*r tradition.*r
For*rp Moses*r said,*r Honour*r thy*r father*r and*r thy*r mother;*r and,*r Whoso*r curseth*r father*r or*r mother,*r let*r him*r die*r the*r death:*r

But*rp ye*r say,*r If*r a*r man*r shall*r say*r to*r his*r father*r or*r mother,*r It*r is*r Corban,*r that*r is*r to*r say,*r a*r gift,*r by*r whatsoever*r thou*r mightest*r be*r profited*r by*r me;*r he*r shall*r be*r free.*r
And*rp ye*r suffer*r him*r no*r more*r to*r do*r ought*r for*r his*r father*r or*r his*r mother;*r
Making*rp the*r word*r of*r God*r of*r none*r effect*r through*r your*r tradition,*r which*r ye*r have*r delivered:*r and*r many*r such*r like*r things*r do*r ye.*r
And*p when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken*r unto*r me*r every*r one*r of*r you,*r and*r understand:*r

There*rp is*r nothing*r from*r without*r a*r man,*r that*r entering*r into*r him*r can*r defile*r him:*r but*r the*r things*r which*r come*r out*r of*r him,*r those*r are*r they*r that*r defile*r the*r man.*r
If*rp any*r man*r have*r ears*r to*r hear,*r let*r him*r hear.*r
And*p when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.

And*p he saith unto them, Are*r ye*r so*r without*r understanding*r also?*r Do*r ye*r not*r perceive,*r that*r whatsoever*r thing*r from*r without*r entereth*r into*r the*r man,*r it*r cannot*r defile*r him;*r
Because*rp it*r entereth*r not*r into*r his*r heart,*r but*r into*r the*r belly,*r and*r goeth*r out*r into*r the*r draught,*r purging*r all*r meats?*r
And*p he said, That*r which*r cometh*r out*r of*r the*r man,*r that*r defileth*r the*r man.*r
For*rp from*r within,*r out*r of*r the*r heart*r of*r men,*r proceed*r evil*r thoughts,*r adulteries,*r fornications,*r murders,*r
Thefts,*rp covetousness,*r wickedness,*r deceit,*r lasciviousness,*r an*r evil*r eye,*r blasphemy,*r pride,*r foolishness:*r
All*rp these*r evil*r things*r come*r from*r within,*r and*r defile*r the*r man.*r
And*p from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.
For*p a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:
The*p woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.
But*p Jesus said unto her, Let*r the*r children*r first*r be*r filled:*r for*r it*r is*r not*r meet*r to*r take*r the*r children's*r bread,*r and*r to*r cast*r it*r unto*r the*r dogs.*r
And*p she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs.
And*p he said unto her, For*r this*r saying*r go*r thy*r way;*r the*r devil*r is*r gone*r out*r of*r thy*r daughter.*r
And*p when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.
And*p again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.
And*p they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.
And*p he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;
And*p looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha,*r that is, Be*r opened.*r
And*p straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
And*p he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it;
And*p were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.
Mark 8
In*p those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples unto him, and saith unto them,
I*rp have*r compassion*r on*r the*r multitude,*r because*r they*r have*r now*r been*r with*r me*r three*r days,*r and*r have*r nothing*r to*r eat:*r
And*rp if*r I*r send*r them*r away*r fasting*r to*r their*r own*r houses,*r they*r will*r faint*r by*r the*r way:*r for*r divers*r of*r them*r came*r from*r far.*r
And*p his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness?
And*p he asked them, How*r many*r loaves*r have*r ye?*r And they said, Seven.

And*p he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before them; and they did set them before the people.
And*p they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before them.
So*p they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets.
And*p they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.
And*p straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
And*p the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.

And*p he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why*r doth*r this*r generation*r seek*r after*r a*r sign?*r verily*r I*r say*r unto*r you,*r There*r shall*r no*r sign*r be*r given*r unto*r this*r generation.*r

And*p when Jesus knew it, he saith unto them, Why*r reason*r ye,*r because*r ye*r have*r no*r bread?*r perceive*r ye*r not*r yet,*r neither*r understand?*r have*r ye*r your*r heart*r yet*r hardened?*r
Having*rp eyes,*r see*r ye*r not?*r and*r having*r ears,*r hear*r ye*r not?*r and*r do*r ye*r not*r remember?*r
When*rp I*r brake*r the*r five*r loaves*r among*r five*r thousand,*r how*r many*r baskets*r full*r of*r fragments*r took*r ye*r up?*r They say unto him, Twelve.
And*rp when*r the*r seven*r among*r four*r thousand,*r how*r many*r baskets*r full*r of*r fragments*r took*r ye*r up?*r And they said, Seven.
And*p he said unto them, How*r is*r it*r that*r ye*r do*r not*r understand?*r

After*p that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.
And*p he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither*r go*r into*r the*r town,*r nor*r tell*r it*r to*r any*r in*r the*r town.*r
And*p Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom*r do*r men*r say*r that*r I*r am?*r
And*p they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.

And*p he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
And*p he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
And*p he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

But*p when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get*r thee*r behind*r me,*r Satan:*r for*r thou*r savourest*r not*r the*r things*r that*r be*r of*r God,*r but*r the*r things*r that*r be*r of*r men.*r

And*p when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever*r will*r come*r after*r me,*r let*r him*r deny*r himself,*r and*r take*r up*r his*r cross,*r and*r follow*r me.*r
For*rp whosoever*r will*r save*r his*r life*r shall*r lose*r it;*r but*r whosoever*r shall*r lose*r his*r life*r for*r my*r sake*r and*r the*r gospel's,*r the*r same*r shall*r save*r it.*r
For*rp what*r shall*r it*r profit*r a*r man,*r if*r he*r shall*r gain*r the*r whole*r world,*r and*r lose*r his*r own*r soul?*r
Or*rp what*r shall*r a*r man*r give*r in*r exchange*r for*r his*r soul?*r

Whosoever*rp therefore*r shall*r be*r ashamed*r of*r me*r and*r of*r my*r words*r in*r this*r adulterous*r and*r sinful*r generation;*r of*r him*r also*r shall*r the*r Son*r of*r man*r be*r ashamed,*r when*r he*r cometh*r in*r the*r glory*r of*r his*r Father*r with*r the*r holy*r angels.*r
Mark 9

And*p he said unto them, Verily*r I*r say*r unto*r you,*r That*r there*r be*r some*r of*r them*r that*r stand*r here,*r which*r shall*r not*r taste*r of*r death,*r till*r they*r have*r seen*r the*r kingdom*r of*r God*r come*r with*r power.*r
And*p after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.
And*p his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.
And*p there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.

For*p he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.
And*p there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
And*p suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
And*p as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.
And*p they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.
And*p they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elias must first come?

And*p he answered and told them, Elias*r verily*r cometh*r first,*r and*r restoreth*r all*r things;*r and*r how*r it*r is*r written*r of*r the*r Son*r of*r man,*r that*r he*r must*r suffer*r many*r things,*r and*r be*r set*r at*r nought.*r
But*rp I*r say*r unto*r you,*r That*r Elias*r is*r indeed*r come,*r and*r they*r have*r done*r unto*r him*r whatsoever*r they*r listed,*r as*r it*r is*r written*r of*r him.*r
And*p when he came to his disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.
And*p straightway all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to him saluted him.
And*p he asked the scribes, What*r question*r ye*r with*r them?*r
And*p one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit;
And*p wheresoever he taketh him, he teareth him: and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast him out; and they could not.
He*p answereth him, and saith, O*r faithless*r generation,*r how*r long*r shall*r I*r be*r with*r you?*r how*r long*r shall*r I*r suffer*r you?*r bring*r him*r unto*r me.*r

Now*p Caiaphas was he, which gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
And*p Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple: that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest.
But*p Peter stood at the door without. Then went out that other disciple, which was known unto the high priest, and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.
Then*p saith the damsel that kept the door unto Peter, Art not thou also one of this man's disciples? He saith, I am not.
And*p the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; for it was cold: and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself.
The*p high priest then asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his doctrine.

Jesus*p answered him, I*r spake*r openly*r to*r the*r world;*r I*r ever*r taught*r in*r the*r synagogue,*r and*r in*r the*r temple,*r whither*r the*r Jews*r always*r resort;*r and*r in*r secret*r have*r I*r said*r nothing.*r
Why*rp askest*r thou*r me?*r ask*r them*r which*r heard*r me,*r what*r I*r have*r said*r unto*r them:*r behold,*r they*r know*r what*r I*r said.*r
And*p when he had thus spoken, one of the officers which stood by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?
Jesus*p answered him, If*r I*r have*r spoken*r evil,*r bear*r witness*r of*r the*r evil:*r but*r if*r well,*r why*r smitest*r thou*r me?*r
Now*p Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.
And*p Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore unto him, Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied it, and said, I am not.
One*p of the servants of the high priest, being his kinsman whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?
Peter*p then denied again: and immediately the cock crew.

Then*p led they Jesus from Caiaphas unto the hall of judgment: and it was early; and they themselves went not into the judgment hall, lest they should be defiled; but that they might eat the passover.
Pilate*p then went out unto them, and said, What accusation bring ye against this man?
They*p answered and said unto him, If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up unto thee.
Then*p said Pilate unto them, Take ye him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death:
That*p the saying of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spake, signifying what death he should die.
Then*p Pilate entered into the judgment hall again, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art thou the King of the Jews?
Jesus*p answered him, Sayest*r thou*r this*r thing*r of*r thyself,*r or*r did*r others*r tell*r it*r thee*r of*r me?*r
Pilate*p answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests have delivered thee unto me: what hast thou done?

Jesus*p answered, My*r kingdom*r is*r not*r of*r this*r world:*r if*r my*r kingdom*r were*r of*r this*r world,*r then*r would*r my*r servants*r fight,*r that*r I*r should*r not*r be*r delivered*r to*r the*r Jews:*r but*r now*r is*r my*r kingdom*r not*r from*r hence.*r

Pilate*p therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou*r sayest*r that*r I*r am*r a*r king.*r To*r this*r end*r was*r I*r born,*r and*r for*r this*r cause*r came*r I*r into*r the*r world,*r that*r I*r should*r bear*r witness*r unto*r the*r truth.*r Every*r one*r that*r is*r of*r the*r truth*r heareth*r my*r voice.*r
Pilate*p saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all.
But*p ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
Then*p cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.
John 19
Then*p Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him.
And*p the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe,
And*p said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they smote him with their hands.
Pilate*p therefore went forth again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that ye may know that I find no fault in him.
Then*p came Jesus forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them, Behold the man!
When*p the chief priests therefore and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Take ye him, and crucify him: for I find no fault in him.
The*p Jews answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.
When*p Pilate therefore heard that saying, he was the more afraid;
And*p went again into the judgment hall, and saith unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no answer.
Then*p saith Pilate unto him, Speakest thou not unto me? knowest thou not that I have power to crucify thee, and have power to release thee?

Jesus*p answered, Thou*r couldest*r have*r no*r power*r at*r all*r against*r me,*r except*r it*r were*r given*r thee*r from*r above:*r therefore*r he*r that*r delivered*r me*r unto*r thee*r hath*r the*r greater*r sin.*r
And*p from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Caesar's friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.
When*p Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.
And*p it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!
But*p they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar.
Then*p delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.
And*p he bearing his cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull, which is called in the Hebrew Golgotha:
Where*p they crucified him, and two other with him, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst.
And*p Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS.
This*p title then read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city: and it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin.
Then*p said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews.
Pilate*p answered, What I have written I have written.
Then*p the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also his coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

They*p said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, They parted my raiment among them, and for my vesture they did cast lots. These things therefore the soldiers did.
Now*p there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
When*p Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman,*r behold*r thy*r son!*r
Then*p saith he to the disciple, Behold*r thy*r mother!*r And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.
After*p this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, I*r thirst.*r
Now*p there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and they filled a sponge with vinegar, and put it upon hyssop, and put it to his mouth.
When*p Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It*r is*r finished:*r and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.

The*p Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.
Then*p came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him.
But*p when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs:
But*p one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.
And*p he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe.
For*p these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
And*p again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.

And*p after this Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus.
And*p there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight.
Then*p took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.
Now*p in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new sepulchre, wherein was never man yet laid.
There*p laid they Jesus therefore because of the Jews' preparation day; for the sepulchre was nigh at hand.
John 20
The*p first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre.

Then*p she runneth, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him.
Peter*p therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulchre.
So*p they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.
And*p he stooping down, and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in.
Then*p cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and seeth the linen clothes lie,
And*p the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself.
Then*p went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.
For*p as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.
