But*p when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away.
When*p I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.
For*p now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
And*p now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
1 Corinthians 14
Follow*p after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.
For*p he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth him; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.
But*p he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.
He*p that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.

I*p would that ye all spake with tongues, but rather that ye prophesied: for greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.
Now,*p brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, except I shall speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophesying, or by doctrine?
And*p even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?
For*p if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?
So*p likewise ye, except ye utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye shall speak into the air.
There*p are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without signification.
Therefore*p if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh shall be a barbarian unto me.
Even*p so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual gifts, seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church.
Wherefore*p let him that speaketh in an unknown tongue pray that he may interpret.
For*p if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.
What*p is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.
Else*p when thou shalt bless with the spirit, how shall he that occupieth the room of the unlearned say Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he understandeth not what thou sayest?
For*p thou verily givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.
I*p thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all:
Yet*p in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.
Brethren,*p be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men.
In*p the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord.
Wherefore*p tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe.
If*p therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those that are unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that ye are mad?
But*p if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all:
And*p thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth.
How*p is it then, brethren? when ye come together, every one of you hath a psalm, hath a doctrine, hath a tongue, hath a revelation, hath an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying.
If*p any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret.
But*p if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God.
Let*p the prophets speak two or three, and let the other judge.
If*p any thing be revealed to another that sitteth by, let the first hold his peace.
For*p ye may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be comforted.
And*p the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.
For*p God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.
Let*p your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.
And*p if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church.
What?*p came the word of God out from you? or came it unto you only?
If*p any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.
But*p if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant.
Wherefore,*p brethren, covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues.
Let*p all things be done decently and in order.
1 Corinthians 15
Moreover,*p brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand;
By*p which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain.
For*p I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;
And*p that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:
And*p that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve:
After*p that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep.
After*p that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles.
And*p last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.
For*p I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
But*p by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
Therefore*p whether it were I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.
Now*p if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?
But*p if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen:
And*p if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.
Yea,*p and we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not.
For*p if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised:
And*p if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins.
Then*p they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished.
If*p in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.
But*p now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.
For*p since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead.
For*p as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.
But*p every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.
Then*p cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.
For*p he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet.
The*p last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.
For*p he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted which did put all things under him.
And*p when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.
Else*p what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?
And*p why stand we in jeopardy every hour?
I*p protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
If*p after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die.
Be*p not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.
Awake*p to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame.
But*p some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?
Thou*p fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die:
And*p that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other grain:
But*p God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body.
All*p flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds.
There*p are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.
There*p is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for one star differeth from another star in glory.
So*p also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption:
It*p is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power:
It*p is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.
And*p so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit.
Howbeit*p that was not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; and afterward that which is spiritual.
The*p first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.
As*p is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy: and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.
And*p as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.
Now*p this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither doth corruption inherit incorruption.
Behold,*p I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed,
In*p a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
For*p this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
So*p when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.
O*p death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?
The*p sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law.
But*p thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore,*p my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
1 Corinthians 16
Now*p concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do ye.
Upon*p the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.
And*p when I come, whomsoever ye shall approve by your letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem.
And*p if it be meet that I go also, they shall go with me.
Now*p I will come unto you, when I shall pass through Macedonia: for I do pass through Macedonia.
And*p it may be that I will abide, yea, and winter with you, that ye may bring me on my journey whithersoever I go.
For*p I will not see you now by the way; but I trust to tarry a while with you, if the Lord permit.
But*p I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost.
For*p a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries.
Now*p if Timothy come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do.
Let*p no man therefore despise him: but conduct him forth in peace, that he may come unto me: for I look for him with the brethren.
As*p touching our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time.
Watch*p ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
Let*p all your things be done with charity.
I*p beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)
That*p ye submit yourselves unto such, and to every one that helpeth with us, and laboureth.
I*p am glad of the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: for that which was lacking on your part they have supplied.
For*p they have refreshed my spirit and yours: therefore acknowledge ye them that are such.
The*p churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house.
All*p the brethren greet you. Greet ye one another with an holy kiss.
The*p salutation of me Paul with mine own hand.
If*p any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha.
The*p grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
My*p love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
2 Corinthians 1
Paul,*p an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia:
Grace*p be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed*p be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;
Who*p comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
For*p as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ.

And*p whether we be afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation.
And*p our hope of you is stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation.
For*p we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life:
But*p we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead:
Who*p delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us;
Ye*p also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf.

For*p our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward.
For*p we write none other things unto you, than what ye read or acknowledge; and I trust ye shall acknowledge even to the end;
As*p also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also are ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.
And*p in this confidence I was minded to come unto you before, that ye might have a second benefit;
And*p to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea.
When*p I therefore was thus minded, did I use lightness? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea yea, and nay nay?
But*p as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.
For*p the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.
For*p all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.
Now*p he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God;
Who*p hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.
Moreover*p I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth.
Not*p for that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for by faith ye stand.
2 Corinthians 2
But*p I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness.
For*p if I make you sorry, who is he then that maketh me glad, but the same which is made sorry by me?
And*p I wrote this same unto you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.
For*p out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be grieved, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you.
But*p if any have caused grief, he hath not grieved me, but in part: that I may not overcharge you all.
Sufficient*p to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.
So*p that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.
Wherefore*p I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.
For*p to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.
To*p whom ye forgive any thing, I forgive also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave it, for your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ;
Lest*p Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.
Furthermore,*p when I came to Troas to preach Christ's gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,
I*p had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia.
Now*p thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.
For*p we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish:
To*p the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?
For*p we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ.
2 Corinthians 3
Do*p we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you, or letters of commendation from you?
Ye*p are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men:

Forasmuch*p as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.
And*p such trust have we through Christ to God-ward:
Not*p that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God;
Who*p also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.

But*p if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:
How*p shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious?
For*p if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.
For*p even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth.
For*p if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious.
Seeing*p then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech:
And*p not as Moses, which put a veil over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:
But*p their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same veil untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which veil is done away in Christ.
But*p even unto this day, when Moses is read, the veil is upon their heart.
Nevertheless*p when it shall turn to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away.
Now*p the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
But*p we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.
2 Corinthians 4
Therefore*p seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not;

But*p have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.
But*p if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost:
In*p whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.
For*p we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake.
For*p God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
But*p we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.
We*p are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;
Persecuted,*p but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;
Always*p bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body.
For*p we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus' sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.
So*p then death worketh in us, but life in you.
We*p having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak;
Knowing*p that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you.
For*p all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.
For*p which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
For*p our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;
While*p we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.
2 Corinthians 5
For*p we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
For*p in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven:
If*p so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.
For*p we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.
Now*p he that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing is God, who also hath given unto us the earnest of the Spirit.
Therefore*p we are always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord:
(For*p we walk by faith, not by sight:)
We*p are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.
Wherefore*p we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.
For*p we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.
Knowing*p therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.
For*p we commend not ourselves again unto you, but give you occasion to glory on our behalf, that ye may have somewhat to answer them which glory in appearance, and not in heart.
For*p whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause.
For*p the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead:
And*p that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.
Wherefore*p henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we him no more.
Therefore*p if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
And*p all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation;
To*p wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.
Now*p then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God.
For*p he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.
2 Corinthians 6
We*p then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.
(For*p he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)
Giving*p no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed:
But*p in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,
In*p stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings;
By*p pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering, by kindness, by the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned,
By*p the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,
By*p honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and yet true;
As*p unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed;
As*p sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.
O*p ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged.
Ye*p are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels.
Now*p for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto my children,) be ye also enlarged.
Be*p ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?
And*p what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?

And*p what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Wherefore*p come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you,
And*p will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.
2 Corinthians 7
Having*p therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
Receive*p us; we have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man.
I*p speak not this to condemn you: for I have said before, that ye are in our hearts to die and live with you.
Great*p is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.
For,*p when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.
Nevertheless*p God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;
And*p not by his coming only, but by the consolation wherewith he was comforted in you, when he told us your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me; so that I rejoiced the more.
For*p though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though it were but for a season.
Now*p I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing.
For*p godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

For*p behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.
Wherefore,*p though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.
Therefore*p we were comforted in your comfort: yea, and exceedingly the more joyed we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.
For*p if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; but as we spake all things to you in truth, even so our boasting, which I made before Titus, is found a truth.
And*p his inward affection is more abundant toward you, whilst he remembereth the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling ye received him.
I*p rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all things.
2 Corinthians 8
Moreover,*p brethren, we do you to wit of the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia;
How*p that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.
For*p to their power, I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they were willing of themselves;
Praying*p us with much entreaty that we would receive the gift, and take upon us the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.
And*p this they did, not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God.
Insomuch*p that we desired Titus, that as he had begun, so he would also finish in you the same grace also.
Therefore,*p as ye abound in every thing, in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all diligence, and in your love to us, see that ye abound in this grace also.
I*p speak not by commandment, but by occasion of the forwardness of others, and to prove the sincerity of your love.
For*p ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.
And*p herein I give my advice: for this is expedient for you, who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago.
Now*p therefore perform the doing of it; that as there was a readiness to will, so there may be a performance also out of that which ye have.
For*p if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not.
For*p I mean not that other men be eased, and ye burdened:
But*p by an equality, that now at this time your abundance may be a supply for their want, that their abundance also may be a supply for your want: that there may be equality:
As*p it is written, He that had gathered much had nothing over; and he that had gathered little had no lack.
But*p thanks be to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.
For*p indeed he accepted the exhortation; but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you.
And*p we have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches;
And*p not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind:
Avoiding*p this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us:
Providing*p for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
And*p we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which I have in you.
Whether*p any do enquire of Titus, he is my partner and fellowhelper concerning you: or our brethren be enquired of, they are the messengers of the churches, and the glory of Christ.
Wherefore*p shew ye to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf.
2 Corinthians 9
For*p as touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you:
For*p I know the forwardness of your mind, for which I boast of you to them of Macedonia, that Achaia was ready a year ago; and your zeal hath provoked very many.
Yet*p have I sent the brethren, lest our boasting of you should be in vain in this behalf; that, as I said, ye may be ready:
Lest*p haply if they of Macedonia come with me, and find you unprepared, we (that we say not, ye) should be ashamed in this same confident boasting.

Therefore*p I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof ye had notice before, that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.
But*p this I say, He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.
Every*p man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.
And*p God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work:
(As*p it is written, He hath dispersed abroad; he hath given to the poor: his righteousness remaineth for ever.
Now*p he that ministereth seed to the sower both minister bread for your food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;)
Being*p enriched in every thing to all bountifulness, which causeth through us thanksgiving to God.
For*p the administration of this service not only supplieth the want of the saints, but is abundant also by many thanksgivings unto God;
Whiles*p by the experiment of this ministration they glorify God for your professed subjection unto the gospel of Christ, and for your liberal distribution unto them, and unto all men;
And*p by their prayer for you, which long after you for the exceeding grace of God in you.
Thanks*p be unto God for his unspeakable gift.
2 Corinthians 10
Now*p I Paul myself beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, who in presence am base among you, but being absent am bold toward you:
But*p I beseech you, that I may not be bold when I am present with that confidence, wherewith I think to be bold against some, which think of us as if we walked according to the flesh.
For*p though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh:
(For*p the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)
Casting*p down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ;
And*p having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.
Do*p ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christ's, let him of himself think this again, that, as he is Christ's, even so are we Christ's.
For*p though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord hath given us for edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed:
That*p I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters.
For*p his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.
Let*p such an one think this, that, such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such will we be also in deed when we are present.

For*p we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves: but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise.
But*p we will not boast of things without our measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us, a measure to reach even unto you.
For*p we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure, as though we reached not unto you: for we are come as far as to you also in preaching the gospel of Christ:
Not*p boasting of things without our measure, that is, of other men's labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly,
To*p preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, and not to boast in another man's line of things made ready to our hand.
But*p he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.
For*p not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.
2 Corinthians 11
Would*p to God ye could bear with me a little in my folly: and indeed bear with me.
For*p I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
But*p I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.

For*p if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or if ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with him.
For*p I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.
But*p though I be rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; but we have been thoroughly made manifest among you in all things.
Have*p I committed an offence in abasing myself that ye might be exalted, because I have preached to you the gospel of God freely?
I*p robbed other churches, taking wages of them, to do you service.

And*p when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied: and in all things I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and so will I keep myself.
As*p the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia.
Wherefore?*p because I love you not? God knoweth.
But*p what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them which desire occasion; that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we.
For*p such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.
And*p no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.
Therefore*p it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.
I*p say again, Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little.
That*p which I speak, I speak it not after the Lord, but as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting.
Seeing*p that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.
For*p ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise.
For*p ye suffer, if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take of you, if a man exalt himself, if a man smite you on the face.
I*p speak as concerning reproach, as though we had been weak. Howbeit whereinsoever any is bold, (I speak foolishly,) I am bold also.
Are*p they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.
Are*p they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.
Of*p the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.
Thrice*p was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;

In*p journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;
In*p weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
Beside*p those things that are without, that which cometh upon me daily, the care of all the churches.
Who*p is weak, and I am not weak? who is offended, and I burn not?
If*p I must needs glory, I will glory of the things which concern mine infirmities.
The*p God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is blessed for evermore, knoweth that I lie not.
In*p Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me:
And*p through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.
2 Corinthians 12
It*p is not expedient for me doubtless to glory. I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
I*p knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.
And*p I knew such a man, (whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;)
How*p that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
Of*p such an one will I glory: yet of myself I will not glory, but in mine infirmities.
For*p though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth: but now I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth me to be, or that he heareth of me.

And*p lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.
For*p this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.

And*p he said unto me, My*r grace*r is*r sufficient*r for*r thee:*r for*r my*r strength*r is*r made*r perfect*r in*r weakness.*r Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
Therefore*p I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.
I*p am become a fool in glorying; ye have compelled me: for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing am I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I be nothing.
Truly*p the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds.
For*p what is it wherein ye were inferior to other churches, except it be that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong.

Behold,*p the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burdensome to you: for I seek not yours, but you: for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
And*p I will very gladly spend and be spent for you; though the more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved.
But*p be it so, I did not burden you: nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile.
Did*p I make a gain of you by any of them whom I sent unto you?
I*p desired Titus, and with him I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? walked we not in the same steps?
Again,*p think ye that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ: but we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.

For*p I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found unto you such as ye would not: lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults:

And*p lest, when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and that I shall bewail many which have sinned already, and have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they have committed.
2 Corinthians 13
This*p is the third time I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.

I*p told you before, and foretell you, as if I were present, the second time; and being absent now I write to them which heretofore have sinned, and to all other, that, if I come again, I will not spare:
Since*p ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you.
For*p though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you.
Examine*p yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?
But*p I trust that ye shall know that we are not reprobates.
Now*p I pray to God that ye do no evil; not that we should appear approved, but that ye should do that which is honest, though we be as reprobates.
For*p we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
For*p we are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong: and this also we wish, even your perfection.
Therefore*p I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness, according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.
Finally,*p brethren, farewell. Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace shall be with you.
Greet*p one another with an holy kiss.
All*p the saints salute you.
The*p grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen.
Galatians 1
Paul,*p an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;)
And*p all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia:
Grace*p be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,
Who*p gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father:
To*p whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I*p marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:
Which*p is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.
But*p though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.
As*p we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.
For*p do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.
But*p I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man.
For*p I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.
For*p ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:
And*p profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.
But*p when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace,
To*p reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood:
Neither*p went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.
Then*p after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.
But*p other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.
Now*p the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.
Afterwards*p I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia;
And*p was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ:
But*p they had heard only, That he which persecuted us in times past now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed.
And*p they glorified God in me.
Galatians 2
Then*p fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.

And*p I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.
But*p neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:
And*p that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:
To*p whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.
But*p of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man's person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:
But*p contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;
(For*p he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)

And*p when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
Only*p they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.
But*p when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.
For*p before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.
And*p the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.

But*p when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?
We*p who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

Knowing*p that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.
But*p if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.
For*p if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.
For*p I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God.

I*p am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
I*p do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.
Galatians 3
O*p foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?
This*p only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
Are*p ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh?
Have*p ye suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain.
He*p therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
Even*p as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.
Know*p ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.
And*p the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.
So*p then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.
For*p as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.
But*p that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.
And*p the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them.
Christ*p hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:
That*p the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
Brethren,*p I speak after the manner of men; Though it be but a man's covenant, yet if it be confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto.
Now*p to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.

And*p this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.
For*p if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.
Wherefore*p then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.
Now*p a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.
Is*p the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law.
But*p the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.
But*p before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.
Wherefore*p the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
But*p after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.
For*p ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.
For*p as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There*p is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.
And*p if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.
Galatians 4
Now*p I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;
But*p is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.
Even*p so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world:
But*p when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,
To*p redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.
And*p because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
Wherefore*p thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.
Howbeit*p then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods.
But*p now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?
Ye*p observe days, and months, and times, and years.
I*p am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.
Brethren,*p I beseech you, be as I am; for I am as ye are: ye have not injured me at all.
Ye*p know how through infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you at the first.
And*p my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
Where*p is then the blessedness ye spake of? for I bear you record, that, if it had been possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me.
Am*p I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?
They*p zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them.
But*p it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you.
My*p little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,
I*p desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.
Tell*p me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?
For*p it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.
But*p he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise.
Which*p things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, which is Agar.
For*p this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children.
But*p Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.
For*p it is written, Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband.
Now*p we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.
But*p as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, even so it is now.
Nevertheless*p what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman.
So*p then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.
Galatians 5
Stand*p fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
Behold,*p I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.
For*p I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
Christ*p is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.
For*p we through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness by faith.
For*p in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love.
Ye*p did run well; who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth?
This*p persuasion cometh not of him that calleth you.
A*p little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.
I*p have confidence in you through the Lord, that ye will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be.
And*p I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution? then is the offence of the cross ceased.
I*p would they were even cut off which trouble you.
For,*p brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.
For*p all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
But*p if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another.
This*p I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.
For*p the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.
But*p if ye be led of the Spirit, ye are not under the law.
Now*p the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,
Idolatry,*p witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies,
Envyings,*p murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.
But*p the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
Meekness,*p temperance: against such there is no law.
And*p they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.
If*p we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.
Let*p us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.
Galatians 6

For*p the hope which is laid up for you in heaven, whereof ye heard before in the word of the truth of the gospel;
Which*p is come unto you, as it is in all the world; and bringeth forth fruit, as it doth also in you, since the day ye heard of it, and knew the grace of God in truth:
As*p ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ;
Who*p also declared unto us your love in the Spirit.
For*p this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;
That*p ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;
Strengthened*p with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness;

And,*p having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven.

Let*p no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days:

(Touch*p not; taste not; handle not;
Which*p all are to perish with the using;) after the commandments and doctrines of men?

When*p Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory.

For*p which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience:
In*p the which ye also walked some time, when ye lived in them.
But*p now ye also put off all these; anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, filthy communication out of your mouth.

Walk*p in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time.
Let*p your speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.

Whom*p I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that he might know your estate, and comfort your hearts;

Aristarchus*p my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Mark, sister's son to Barnabas, (touching whom ye received commandments: if he come unto you, receive him;)

1 Thessalonians 1

We*p give thanks to God always for you all, making mention of you in our prayers;
Remembering*p without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father;
Knowing,*p brethren beloved, your election of God.
For*p our gospel came not unto you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Ghost, and in much assurance; as ye know what manner of men we were among you for your sake.
And*p ye became followers of us, and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Ghost:
So*p that ye were ensamples to all that believe in Macedonia and Achaia.
For*p from you sounded out the word of the Lord not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith to God-ward is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing.
For*p they themselves shew of us what manner of entering in we had unto you, and how ye turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God;
And*p to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.
1 Thessalonians 2
For*p yourselves, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain:
But*p even after that we had suffered before, and were shamefully entreated, as ye know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God with much contention.
For*p our exhortation was not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile:
But*p as we were allowed of God to be put in trust with the gospel, even so we speak; not as pleasing men, but God, which trieth our hearts.
For*p neither at any time used we flattering words, as ye know, nor a cloak of covetousness; God is witness:
Nor*p of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor yet of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ.
But*p we were gentle among you, even as a nurse cherisheth her children:
So*p being affectionately desirous of you, we were willing to have imparted unto you, not the gospel of God only, but also our own souls, because ye were dear unto us.
For*p ye remember, brethren, our labour and travail: for labouring night and day, because we would not be chargeable unto any of you, we preached unto you the gospel of God.
Ye*p are witnesses, and God also, how holily and justly and unblameably we behaved ourselves among you that believe:
As*p ye know how we exhorted and comforted and charged every one of you, as a father doth his children,
That*p ye would walk worthy of God, who hath called you unto his kingdom and glory.

For*p this cause also thank we God without ceasing, because, when ye received the word of God which ye heard of us, ye received it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, the word of God, which effectually worketh also in you that believe.
For*p ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judaea are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Jews:
Who*p both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men:
Forbidding*p us to speak to the Gentiles that they might be saved, to fill up their sins alway: for the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost.
But*p we, brethren, being taken from you for a short time in presence, not in heart, endeavoured the more abundantly to see your face with great desire.
Wherefore*p we would have come unto you, even I Paul, once and again; but Satan hindered us.
For*p what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even ye in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?
For*p ye are our glory and joy.
1 Thessalonians 3
Wherefore*p when we could no longer forbear, we thought it good to be left at Athens alone;
And*p sent Timothy, our brother, and minister of God, and our fellowlabourer in the gospel of Christ, to establish you, and to comfort you concerning your faith:
That*p no man should be moved by these afflictions: for yourselves know that we are appointed thereunto.
For*p verily, when we were with you, we told you before that we should suffer tribulation; even as it came to pass, and ye know.
For*p this cause, when I could no longer forbear, I sent to know your faith, lest by some means the tempter have tempted you, and our labour be in vain.
But*p now when Timothy came from you unto us, and brought us good tidings of your faith and charity, and that ye have good remembrance of us always, desiring greatly to see us, as we also to see you:
Therefore,*p brethren, we were comforted over you in all our affliction and distress by your faith:
For*p now we live, if ye stand fast in the Lord.
For*p what thanks can we render to God again for you, for all the joy wherewith we joy for your sakes before our God;
Night*p and day praying exceedingly that we might see your face, and might perfect that which is lacking in your faith?
Now*p God himself and our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way unto you.
And*p the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all men, even as we do toward you:
To*p the end he may stablish your hearts unblameable in holiness before God, even our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.
1 Thessalonians 4
Furthermore*p then we beseech you, brethren, and exhort you by the Lord Jesus, that as ye have received of us how ye ought to walk and to please God, so ye would abound more and more.
For*p ye know what commandments we gave you by the Lord Jesus.
For*p this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication:
That*p every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour;
Not*p in the lust of concupiscence, even as the Gentiles which know not God:
That*p no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter: because that the Lord is the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified.
For*p God hath not called us unto uncleanness, but unto holiness.
He*p therefore that despiseth, despiseth not man, but God, who hath also given unto us his holy Spirit.
But*p as touching brotherly love ye need not that I write unto you: for ye yourselves are taught of God to love one another.
And*p indeed ye do it toward all the brethren which are in all Macedonia: but we beseech you, brethren, that ye increase more and more;
And*p that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you;
That*p ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing.
But*p I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.
For*p if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.
For*p this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep.
For*p the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
Then*p we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
Wherefore*p comfort one another with these words.
1 Thessalonians 5
But*p of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.
For*p yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.
For*p when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.
But*p ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief.
Ye*p are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness.
Therefore*p let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.
For*p they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night.
But*p let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation.
For*p God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ,
Who*p died for us, that, whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him.
Wherefore*p comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.
And*p we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you;
And*p to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. And be at peace among yourselves.
Now*p we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.
See*p that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men.
Rejoice*p evermore.
Pray*p without ceasing.
In*p every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
Quench*p not the Spirit.
Despise*p not prophesyings.
Prove*p all things; hold fast that which is good.

And*p the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

The*p grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
2 Thessalonians 1
Paul,*p and Silvanus, and Timothy, unto the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace*p unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We*p are bound to thank God always for you, brethren, as it is meet, because that your faith groweth exceedingly, and the charity of every one of you all toward each other aboundeth;

Wherefore*p also we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling, and fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness, and the work of faith with power:

But*p we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth:

Therefore,*p brethren, stand fast, and hold the traditions which ye have been taught, whether by word, or our epistle.

2 Thessalonians 3
Finally,*p brethren, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may have free course, and be glorified, even as it is with you:

But*p the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil.
And*p we have confidence in the Lord touching you, that ye both do and will do the things which we command you.
And*p the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God, and into the patient waiting for Christ.
Now*p we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly, and not after the tradition which he received of us.
For*p yourselves know how ye ought to follow us: for we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you;
Neither*p did we eat any man's bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you:
Not*p because we have not power, but to make ourselves an ensample unto you to follow us.
For*p even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.
For*p we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies.
Now*p them that are such we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread.

The*p salutation of Paul with mine own hand, which is the token in every epistle: so I write.
The*p grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
1 Timothy 1
Paul,*p an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Saviour, and Lord Jesus Christ, which is our hope;
Unto*p Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
As*p I besought thee to abide still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine,

Now*p the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned:
From*p which some having swerved have turned aside unto vain jangling;
Desiring*p to be teachers of the law; understanding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm.
But*p we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully;

Knowing*p this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,
For*p whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine;
According*p to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
And*p I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry;
Who*p was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
And*p the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
This*p is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
Howbeit*p for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might shew forth all longsuffering, for a pattern to them which should hereafter believe on him to life everlasting.

This*p charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare;

I*p exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;

Who*p will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.

Who*p gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.

I*p will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.
In*p like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;
