Not*p given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous;
One*p that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity;
(For*p if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)
Not*p a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
Moreover*p he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
Likewise*p must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;
Holding*p the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
And*p let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.
Even*p so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
Let*p the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.
For*p they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
These*p things write I unto thee, hoping to come unto thee shortly:
But*p if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

And*p without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.
1 Timothy 4
Now*p the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils;
Speaking*p lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron;
Forbidding*p to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.
For*p every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving:
For*p it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
If*p thou put the brethren in remembrance of these things, thou shalt be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished up in the words of faith and of good doctrine, whereunto thou hast attained.
But*p refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness.
For*p bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.
This*p is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.
For*p therefore we both labour and suffer reproach, because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.
These*p things command and teach.
Let*p no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Till*p I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
Neglect*p not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.
Meditate*p upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all.
Take*p heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.
1 Timothy 5
Rebuke*p not an elder, but entreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren;
The*p elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity.
Honour*p widows that are widows indeed.
But*p if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God.
Now*p she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.
But*p she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.
And*p these things give in charge, that they may be blameless.
But*p if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.
Let*p not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man,

Well*p reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.
But*p the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry;
Having*p damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.
And*p withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.
I*p will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.
For*p some are already turned aside after Satan.
If*p any man or woman that believeth have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.
Let*p the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine.
For*p the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The*r labourer*r is*r worthy*r of*r his*r reward.*r
Against*p an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.
Them*p that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear.
I*p charge thee before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.
Lay*p hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure.
Drink*p no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities.
Some*p men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after.
Likewise*p also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.
1 Timothy 6
Let*p as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.

And*p they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort.
If*p any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness;
He*p is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings,
Perverse*p disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself.
But*p godliness with contentment is great gain.
For*p we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.
And*p having food and raiment let us be therewith content.
But*p they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.
For*p the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
But*p thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.
Fight*p the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
I*p give thee charge in the sight of God, who quickeneth all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession;
That*p thou keep this commandment without spot, unrebukeable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:
Which*p in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;
Who*p only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.
Charge*p them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;
That*p they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate;
Laying*p up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life.
O*p Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called:
Which*p some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen.
2 Timothy 1
Paul,*p an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in Christ Jesus,
To*p Timothy, my dearly beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I*p thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with pure conscience, that without ceasing I have remembrance of thee in my prayers night and day;
Greatly*p desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy;
When*p I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also.
Wherefore*p I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands.
For*p God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Be*p not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God;
Who*p hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began,
But*p is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who hath abolished death, and hath brought life and immortality to light through the gospel:
Whereunto*p I am appointed a preacher, and an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.

For*p the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.
Hold*p fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
That*p good thing which was committed unto thee keep by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us.
This*p thou knowest, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes.
The*p Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus; for he oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain:
But,*p when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me.
The*p Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day: and in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus, thou knowest very well.
2 Timothy 2
Thou*p therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
And*p the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.
Thou*p therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
No*p man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.
And*p if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.
The*p husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits.
Consider*p what I say; and the Lord give thee understanding in all things.
Remember*p that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel:
Wherein*p I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound.
Therefore*p I endure all things for the elect's sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
It*p is a faithful saying: For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him:
If*p we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us:
If*p we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself.
Of*p these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord that they strive not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers.
Study*p to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
But*p shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.
And*p their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus;
Who*p concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some.
Nevertheless*p the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.
But*p in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.
If*p a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.
Flee*p also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
But*p foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes.
And*p the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient,
In*p meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth;
And*p that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will.
2 Timothy 3
This*p know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.
For*p men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,
Without*p natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good,
Traitors,*p heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God;
Having*p a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away.
For*p of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts,
Ever*p learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
Now*p as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith.
But*p they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs also was.
But*p thou hast fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience,
Persecutions,*p afflictions, which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me.
Yea,*p and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.
But*p evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived.
But*p continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them;
And*p that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.
All*p scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
That*p the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works.
2 Timothy 4
I*p charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;
Preach*p the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.
For*p the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;
And*p they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.
But*p watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry.
For*p I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.
I*p have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
Henceforth*p there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.
Do*p thy diligence to come shortly unto me:
For*p Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.
Only*p Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.
And*p Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus.
The*p cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.
Alexander*p the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works:
Of*p whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words.
At*p my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.
Notwithstanding*p the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
And*p the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Salute*p Priscilla and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus*p abode at Corinth: but Trophimus have I left at Miletus sick.
Do*p thy diligence to come before winter. Eubulus greeteth thee, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren.
The*p Lord Jesus Christ be with thy spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.
Titus 1
Paul,*p a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;
In*p hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;
But*p hath in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Saviour;
To*p Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.
For*p this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:
If*p any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.
For*p a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre;
But*p a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate;
Holding*p fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.
For*p there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision:
Whose*p mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.
One*p of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretans are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.
This*p witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;
Not*p giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.
Unto*p the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.
They*p profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.
Titus 2
But*p speak thou the things which become sound doctrine:
That*p the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience.
The*p aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;
That*p they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children,
To*p be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.
Young*p men likewise exhort to be sober minded.
In*p all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,
Sound*p speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you.
Exhort*p servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again;
Not*p purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.
For*p the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men,
Teaching*p us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;
Looking*p for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;
Who*p gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.
These*p things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.
Titus 3
Put*p them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work,
To*p speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.
For*p we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
But*p after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared,
Not*p by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;
Which*p he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour;
That*p being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

This*p is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.
But*p avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.
A*p man that is an heretic after the first and second admonition reject;
Knowing*p that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.
When*p I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter.
Bring*p Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them.
And*p let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.
All*p that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
Philemon 1
Paul,*p a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,
And*p to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:
Grace*p to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I*p thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers,
Hearing*p of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints;
That*p the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.
For*p we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
Wherefore,*p though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,
Yet*p for love's sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I*p beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds:
Which*p in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me:
Whom*p I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels:
Whom*p I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel:
But*p without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly.
For*p perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever;
Not*p now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?
If*p thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.
If*p he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account;
I*p Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.
Yea,*p brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord.
Having*p confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say.
But*p withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.
There*p salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;
Mark,*p Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellowlabourers.
The*p grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
Hebrews 1
God,*p who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets,
Hath*p in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;

Who*p being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
Being*p made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.
For*p unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?
And*p again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.
And*p of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.
But*p unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.
Thou*p hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
And,*p Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands:
They*p shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment;
And*p as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.
But*p to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?
Are*p they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?
Hebrews 2
Therefore*p we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.
For*p if the word spoken by angels was stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward;
How*p shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
God*p also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will?
For*p unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak.
But*p one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
Thou*p madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands:
Thou*p hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.
But*p we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.
For*p it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
For*p both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
Saying,*p I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.
And*p again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold I and the children which God hath given me.

Forasmuch*p then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;
And*p deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
For*p verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.

Wherefore*p in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
For*p in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.
Hebrews 3
Wherefore,*p holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus;
Who*p was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.
For*p this man was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who hath builded the house hath more honour than the house.
For*p every house is builded by some man; but he that built all things is God.
And*p Moses verily was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after;
But*p Christ as a son over his own house; whose house are we, if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end.
Wherefore*p (as the Holy Ghost saith, To day if ye will hear his voice,
Harden*p not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness:
When*p your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years.
Wherefore*p I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways.
So*p I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.)
Take*p heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.
But*p exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.
For*p we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end;
While*p it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.
For*p some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
But*p with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?
And*p to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?
So*p we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
Hebrews 4
Let*p us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.
For*p unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.
For*p we which have believed do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
For*p he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.
And*p in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest.
Seeing*p therefore it remaineth that some must enter therein, and they to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief:
Again,*p he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
For*p if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.
There*p remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
For*p he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.
Let*p us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.

For*p the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
Neither*p is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
Seeing*p then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.
For*p we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
Let*p us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
Hebrews 5
For*p every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
Who*p can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way; for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity.
And*p by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
And*p no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.
So*p also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.
As*p he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
Who*p in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;
Though*p he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;
And*p being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;
Called*p of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec.
Of*p whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.

For*p when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.
For*p every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.
But*p strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.
Hebrews 6
Therefore*p leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
Of*p the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
And*p this will we do, if God permit.
For*p it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost,
And*p have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,
If*p they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.
For*p the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:
But*p that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.
But,*p beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.
For*p God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
And*p we desire that every one of you do shew the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end:
That*p ye be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
For*p when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,
Saying,*p Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.
And*p so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
For*p men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.
Wherein*p God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:
That*p by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
Which*p hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
Whither*p the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
Hebrews 7
For*p this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
To*p whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;
Without*p father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.
Now*p consider how great this man was, unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.

And*p verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham:
But*p he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.
And*p without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.
And*p here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them, of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.
And*p as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
For*p he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.

If*p therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
For*p the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.
For*p he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar.
For*p it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Judah; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
And*p it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,
Who*p is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.
For*p he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
For*p there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.
For*p the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.
And*p inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest:
(For*p those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)
By*p so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.
And*p they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:
But*p this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.
Wherefore*p he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
For*p such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
Who*p needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
For*p the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.
Hebrews 8
Now*p of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;
A*p minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
For*p every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.
For*p if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law:

Who*p serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.
But*p now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.
For*p if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.
For*p finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:

Not*p according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.

For*p this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:
And*p they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.
For*p I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.
In*p that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.
Hebrews 9
Then*p verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
For*p there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.
And*p after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;
Which*p had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
And*p over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.
Now*p when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God.
But*p into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:
The*p Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:
Which*p was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
Which*p stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.
But*p Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;
Neither*p by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.
For*p if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh:
How*p much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

And*p for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
For*p where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.
For*p a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.
Whereupon*p neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.

For*p when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people,
Saying,*p This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.
Moreover*p he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry.
And*p almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.
It*p was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
For*p Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:
Nor*p yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others;
For*p then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
And*p as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:
So*p Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.
Hebrews 10

For*p the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.
For*p then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.
But*p in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.
For*p it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.
Wherefore*p when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me:
In*p burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.
Then*p said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.
Above*p when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law;
Then*p said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.
By*p the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And*p every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:
But*p this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;
From*p henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.
For*p by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
Whereof*p the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,
This*p is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;
And*p their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.
Now*p where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
Having*p therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,
By*p a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
And*p having an high priest over the house of God;
Let*p us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let*p us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;)
And*p let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works:
Not*p forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
For*p if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,
But*p a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.
He*p that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:

Of*p how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?
For*p we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.
It*p is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
But*p call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions;
Partly,*p whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used.
For*p ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.
Cast*p not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward.
For*p ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.
For*p yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry.
Now*p the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.
But*p we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.
Hebrews 11
Now*p faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
For*p by it the elders obtained a good report.
Through*p faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
By*p faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
By*p faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.
But*p without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

By*p faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
By*p faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
By*p faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
For*p he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
Through*p faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.
Therefore*p sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.

These*p all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
For*p they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.
And*p truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.
But*p now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.
By*p faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son,
Of*p whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:
Accounting*p that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.
By*p faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
By*p faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.
By*p faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.
By*p faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
By*p faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;
Choosing*p rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
Esteeming*p the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.
By*p faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
Through*p faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.
By*p faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.
By*p faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.
By*p faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.
And*p what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:
Who*p through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
Quenched*p the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.
Women*p received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:
And*p others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:
They*p were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented;
(Of*p whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.
And*p these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:
God*p having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.
Hebrews 12

Wherefore*p seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
Looking*p unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
For*p consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.
Ye*p have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.
And*p ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:
For*p whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
If*p ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?
But*p if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
Furthermore*p we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
For*p they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.
Now*p no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
Wherefore*p lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;
And*p make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.
Follow*p peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:
Looking*p diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;
Lest*p there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.
For*p ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.
For*p ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,
And*p the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which voice they that heard entreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more:
(For*p they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart:
And*p so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:)
But*p ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels,
To*p the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,
And*p to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.
See*p that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven:
Whose*p voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.
And*p this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
Wherefore*p we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear:
For*p our God is a consuming fire.
Hebrews 13
Let*p brotherly love continue.
Be*p not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
Remember*p them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.
Marriage*p is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.
Let*p your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
So*p that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.
Remember*p them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.
Jesus*p Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.

Be*p not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. For it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein.
We*p have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle.
For*p the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.
Wherefore*p Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.
Let*p us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.
For*p here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come.
By*p him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.
But*p to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

Obey*p them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.
Pray*p for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly.
But*p I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.
Now*p the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
Make*p you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
And*p I beseech you, brethren, suffer the word of exhortation: for I have written a letter unto you in few words.
Know*p ye that our brother Timothy is set at liberty; with whom, if he come shortly, I will see you.
Salute*p all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints. They of Italy salute you.
Grace*p be with you all. Amen.
James 1
James,*p a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.
My*p brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;
Knowing*p this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.
But*p let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
If*p any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
But*p let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
For*p let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.
A*p double minded man is unstable in all his ways.
Let*p the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:
But*p the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.

For*p the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.
Blessed*p is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.
Let*p no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:
But*p every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.
Then*p when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.
Do*p not err, my beloved brethren.
Every*p good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
Of*p his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
Wherefore,*p my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
For*p the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.
Wherefore*p lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.
But*p be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
For*p if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass:
For*p he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.
But*p whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.
If*p any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain.
Pure*p religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
James 2
My*p brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.
For*p if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;
And*p ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:
Are*p ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?
Hearken,*p my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?
But*p ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?
Do*p not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?
If*p ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:
But*p if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.
For*p whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
For*p he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.
So*p speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.
For*p he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.
What*p doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?
If*p a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,
And*p one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?
Even*p so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
Yea,*p a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.
Thou*p believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.
But*p wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?
Was*p not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
Seest*p thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?
And*p the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.
Ye*p see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.
Likewise*p also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
For*p as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
James 3
My*p brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.
For*p in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.
Behold,*p we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
Behold*p also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.
Even*p so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!
And*p the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.
For*p every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind:
But*p the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
Therewith*p bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God.
Out*p of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.
Doth*p a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter?
Can*p the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so can no fountain both yield salt water and fresh.
Who*p is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.
But*p if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.
This*p wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.
For*p where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.
But*p the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
And*p the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.
James 4
From*p whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?
Ye*p lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.
Ye*p ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.
Ye*p adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.
Do*p ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy?
But*p he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.
Submit*p yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

Go*p to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:
Whereas*p ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
For*p that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.
But*p now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.
Therefore*p to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.
James 5

Your*p riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten.

But*p above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.
Is*p any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.
Is*p any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:
And*p the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.

And*p he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.
Brethren,*p if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him;
Let*p him know, that he which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.

Who*p are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

Receiving*p the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.
Of*p which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you:

But*p as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;
Because*p it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy.
And*p if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man's work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear:

Seeing*p ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently:

For*p all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withereth, and the flower thereof falleth away:
But*p the word of the Lord endureth for ever. And this is the word which by the gospel is preached unto you.
1 Peter 2
Wherefore*p laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings,

If*p so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.
To*p whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious,
Ye*p also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

Who,*p when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously:

Likewise,*p ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.

And*p who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?
But*p and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;
But*p sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
Having*p a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.
